title.zh: 卷四十八 志第三十八 百官三
title.raw: 卷四十八 志第三十八 百官三 Volume 48 Treatises 43: Official Posts 3

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 御史臺大夫一人，正三品；

translations.literal: One Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, regular third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate had one Censor-in-Chief, of regular third rank;

sentences.zh: 中丞二人，正四品下。

translations.literal: two Vice Censors, regular fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Censors, of regular fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 大夫掌以刑法典章糾正百官之罪惡，中丞爲之貳。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief held charge of correcting the crimes and wrongdoing of the hundred officials by penal codes and statutes; the Vice Censors were his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief used the penal code and administrative statutes to correct the offenses of all officials; the Vice Censors served as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 其屬有三院：一曰臺院，侍御史隸焉；

translations.literal: Its subordinates had three bureaus: the first was called the Bureau of the Censorate, to which Attending Censors were attached;
translations.idiomatic: Under them were three bureaus: the Bureau of the Censorate, staffed by Attending Censors;

sentences.zh: 二曰殿院，殿中侍御史隸焉；

translations.literal: the second was called the Bureau of the Palace, to which Palace Attending Censors were attached;
translations.idiomatic: the Bureau of the Palace, staffed by Palace Attending Censors;

sentences.zh: 三曰察院，監察御史隸焉。

translations.literal: the third was called the Bureau of Investigation, to which Investigating Censors were attached.
translations.idiomatic: and the Bureau of Investigation, staffed by Investigating Censors.

sentences.zh: 凡冤而無告者，三司詰之。

translations.literal: In all cases of injustice with no one to appeal to, the Three Offices examined them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever someone suffered injustice with no recourse, the Three Offices investigated the case.

sentences.zh: 三司，謂御史大夫、中書、門下也。

translations.literal: The Three Offices meant the Censor-in-Chief, the Secretariat, and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices were the Censor-in-Chief, the Secretariat, and the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 大事奏裁，小事專達。

translations.literal: Great matters were memorialized for imperial decision; minor matters were reported on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases were submitted for the emperor's decision; minor ones were handled directly.

sentences.zh: 凡有彈劾，御史以白大夫，大事以方幅，小事署名而已。

translations.literal: Whenever there was impeachment, the censor reported to the Censor-in-Chief; for great matters a full sheet was used, for minor matters a signature alone.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor impeached someone, he informed the Censor-in-Chief; major charges required a full memorial, minor ones only a signature.

sentences.zh: 有制覆囚，則與刑部尙書平閲。

translations.literal: When there was an imperial order to review prisoners, they jointly reviewed together with the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered a review of prisoners, they examined the cases jointly with the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 行幸，乘路車爲導。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses, they rode the protocol carriage as escort.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours they rode the protocol carriage at the head of the procession.

sentences.zh: 朝會，則率其屬正百官之班序，遲明列於兩觀，監察御史二人押班，侍御史顓舉不如法者。

translations.literal: At court assemblies, they led their subordinates to rectify the order of the hundred officials' ranks; at dawn they lined up at the twin watchtowers; two Investigating Censors supervised the formation; Attending Censors exclusively cited those not conforming to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies they led their staff in setting the order of officials' ranks; before dawn they took position at the twin watchtowers, two Investigating Censors supervised the formation, and Attending Censors cited anyone who violated protocol.

sentences.zh: 文武官職事九品以上及二王後，朝朔望。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials with substantive posts of the ninth rank and above, and the heirs of the two [Han] dynasties, attended court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials in substantive posts of ninth rank or higher, and the heirs of the Former and Latter Han, attended court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 文官五品以上及兩省供奉官、監察御史、員外郎、太常博士，日參，號常參官。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the fifth rank and above, tribute officials of the Two Departments, Investigating Censors, vice directors, and Masters of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices attended daily—they were called Regular Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of fifth rank and above, tribute officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Investigating Censors, vice directors, and Masters of Rites attended daily; they were called Regular Attendants.

sentences.zh: 武官三品以上，三日一朝，號九參官；

translations.literal: Military officials of the third rank and above attended court once every three days—they were called Nine-Day Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Military officials of third rank and above attended once every three days; they were called Nine-Day Attendants;

sentences.zh: 五品以上及折衝當番者，五日一朝，號六參官。

translations.literal: Those of the fifth rank and above and Zhechong guards on duty rotation attended once every five days—they were called Six-Day Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: those of fifth rank and above and Zhechong guards on active rotation attended once every five days; they were called Six-Day Attendants.

sentences.zh: 弘文、崇文舘、國子監學生，四時參。

translations.literal: Students of the Hongwen and Chongwen institutes and the Directorate of Education attended at the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Hongwen and Chongwen Academies and the Directorate of Education attended at the four seasonal audiences.

sentences.zh: 凡諸王入朝及以恩追至者，日參。

translations.literal: All princes coming to court and those summoned by grace attended daily.
translations.idiomatic: All princes present at court and those summoned by special grace attended daily.

sentences.zh: 九品以上，自十月至二月，袴褶以朝；

translations.literal: Those of the ninth rank and above, from the tenth month through the second, wore trousers and jackets at court;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of ninth rank and above wore trousers and jackets at court from the tenth month through the second;

sentences.zh: 五品以上有珂，蕃官及四品非淸官則否。

translations.literal: those of the fifth rank and above might wear ke ornaments; foreign officials and fourth-rank non-pure officials might not.
translations.idiomatic: fifth-rank officials and above might display rank markers on their horses; foreign officials and fourth-rank officials who were not pure officials might not.

sentences.zh: 凡朝位以官，職事同者先爵，爵同以齒，致仕官居上；

translations.literal: Court positions were ordered by office; when substantive posts were equal, nobility rank came first; when nobility was equal, age; retired officials stood above;
translations.idiomatic: Court standing followed office; when substantive posts were equal, nobility took precedence, and when nobility was equal, age; retired officials stood ahead;

sentences.zh: 職事與散官、勳官合班，則文散官居職事之下，武散官次之，勳官又次之；

translations.literal: when substantive post joined ranks with honorary titles and merit titles, civil honorary titles stood below the substantive post, military honorary next, merit titles last;
translations.idiomatic: when substantive posts, honorary titles, and merit titles stood together, civil honorary titles ranked below the substantive post, military honorary titles below those, and merit titles below them;

sentences.zh: 官同者，異姓爲後。

translations.literal: when offices were equal, different surnames stood behind.
translations.idiomatic: when offices were equal, officials of different surnames stood behind.

sentences.zh: 親王、嗣王任文武官者，從其班，官卑者從王品；

translations.literal: Imperial and heir princes who held civil or military posts followed those ranks; if the post was lower, they followed princely rank;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial and heir princes who held civil or military offices followed those ranks; if the office was lower, they followed their princely rank;

sentences.zh: 郡王任三品以下職事者，居同階品之上，非任文武官者，嗣王居太子太保之下，郡王次之，國公居三品之下，郡公居從三品之下，縣公居四品之下，侯居從四品之下，伯居五品之下，子居從五品之上，男居從五品之下。

translations.literal: When a prince of a commandery held a substantive post of the third rank or below, he stood above others of the same rank; when not holding civil or military posts, the heir prince stood below the Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, princes of commanderies next, the Duke of the State below third rank, the Duke of the Commandery below subordinate third rank, the Duke of the County below fourth rank, the Marquis below subordinate fourth rank, the Earl below fifth rank, the Viscount above subordinate fifth rank, the Baron below subordinate fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery prince in a substantive post of third rank or lower stood above peers of that rank; if he held no civil or military office, the heir prince stood below the Heir Apparent's Grand Guardian, commandery princes below that, state dukes below third rank, commandery dukes below subordinate third rank, county dukes below fourth rank, marquises below subordinate fourth rank, earls below fifth rank, viscounts above subordinate fifth rank, and barons below subordinate fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 以前官召見者，居本品見任之上，以理解者，居同品之下。

translations.literal: Those summoned having held a former post stood above their current rank in that former grade; those on leave of absence stood below those of the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those summoned while holding a former rank stood above their current rank in that former grade; those on leave stood below peers of the same rank.

sentences.zh: 本司參集者，以職事爲上下。

translations.literal: When assembling within one's own ministry, order followed substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: When officials assembled within their own ministry, standing followed substantive post.

sentences.zh: 文武三品非職事官者，朝參名簿，皆稱曰諸公。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of third rank without substantive posts were all called "the Dukes" on attendance registers.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of third rank without substantive posts were all listed on attendance registers as "the Dukes."

sentences.zh: 凡出，不踰四面關則不辭見。

translations.literal: For departures, if one did not cross the Four Passes, one need not take leave in audience.
translations.idiomatic: For departures, if one did not travel beyond the Four Passes, one need not take formal leave in audience.

sentences.zh: 都督、刺史、都護旣辭，候旨於側門。

translations.literal: After regional commanders, prefects, and protectors had taken leave, they awaited orders at the side gate.
translations.idiomatic: After regional commanders, prefects, and protectors had taken their leave, they waited for orders at the side gate.

sentences.zh: 左右僕射、侍中、中書令初拜，以表讓。

translations.literal: When the Left and Right Vice Directors, Palace Attendants, and Chief Ministers of the Secretariat first received appointment, they submitted a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: When the Left and Right Vice Directors, Palace Attendants, and Chief Ministers of the Secretariat were first appointed, they submitted a memorial declining the office.

sentences.zh: 中書門下五品以上及諸司長官，謝於正衙，復進狀謝於側門。

translations.literal: Fifth-rank and above of the Secretariat and Chancellery and heads of the various ministries gave thanks at the main hall, then submitted a petition of thanks at the side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank officials and above of the Secretariat and Chancellery and the heads of the various ministries gave thanks in the main hall, then submitted a petition of thanks at the side gate.

sentences.zh: 兩班三品以朔望朝，就食廊下，殿中侍御史二人爲使涖之。

translations.literal: The two shifts of third rank attended on the new and full moon, dined in the corridor below; two Palace Attending Censors served as envoys supervising them.
translations.idiomatic: The two shifts of third-rank officials attended on the first and fifteenth of the month and took their meal in the corridor below; two Palace Attending Censors served as supervisors.

sentences.zh: 髙宗改治書侍御史中丞，以避帝名；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong changed the title Vice Censor for Drafting Memorials to avoid the emperor's taboo name;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong changed the title Vice Censor for Drafting Memorials to avoid the imperial taboo;

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改御史臺曰憲臺，大夫曰大司憲，中丞曰司憲大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Censorate was renamed the Bureau of Discipline; the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Director of Discipline; the Vice Censor was renamed Director of Discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo the Censorate was renamed the Bureau of Discipline, the Censor-in-Chief became Grand Director of Discipline, and the Vice Censor became Director of Discipline.

sentences.zh: 武后文明元年，改御史臺曰肅政臺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Civilizing Rule under Empress Wu, the Censorate was renamed the Bureau of Sober Government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Civilizing Rule, Empress Wu renamed the Censorate the Bureau of Sober Government.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，分左右臺：左臺知百司，監軍旅；

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, it was divided into Left and Right Bureaus: the Left Bureau oversaw the hundred offices and supervised the army;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai the Censorate was split into Left and Right Bureaus: the Left oversaw all offices and supervised the military;

sentences.zh: 右臺察州縣、省風俗。

translations.literal: the Right Bureau inspected prefectures and counties and reviewed local customs.
translations.idiomatic: the Right inspected prefectures and counties and reviewed local customs.

sentences.zh: 尋命左臺兼察州縣。

translations.literal: Soon the Left Bureau was also ordered to inspect prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Left Bureau was also charged with inspecting prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 兩臺歳再發使八人，春曰風俗，秋曰廉察，以四十八條察州縣。

translations.literal: The two bureaus each year dispatched eight envoys twice: in spring called Customs, in autumn called Integrity Inspection, using forty-eight articles to inspect prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the two bureaus dispatched eight envoys twice—in spring for customs inspection, in autumn for integrity inspection—using forty-eight articles to examine prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 兩臺御史，有假、有檢校、有員外、有試，至神龍初皆廢。

translations.literal: Censors of the two bureaus included acting, inspecting, vice, and probationary appointments; by the beginning of Shenlong all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Censors of the two bureaus included acting, inspecting, vice, and probationary posts; by the beginning of Shenlong all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 景雲三年，以兩臺望齊，糾舉苛察，百僚厭其煩，乃廢右臺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyun, because the two bureaus were equal in prestige and their impeachments were harsh and exacting, the hundred officials grew weary of the trouble, and the Right Bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingyun, because the two bureaus were equal in prestige and their investigations were harsh and exacting, officials grew weary of the burden, and the Right Bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 延和元年，復置，歳中以尙書省隸左臺，月餘而右臺復廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanhe it was restored; mid-year the Department of State Affairs was placed under the Left Bureau; after a little more than a month the Right Bureau was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe it was restored; mid-year the Department of State Affairs was placed under the Left Bureau, and a little over a month later the Right Bureau was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 至德後，諸道使府參佐，皆以御史爲之，謂之外臺；

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, aides in the commissioner offices of the various circuits were all made censors—called the Outer Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era, aides in the various circuit commissioner offices were all appointed censors—called the Outer Bureau;

sentences.zh: 復有檢校、裏行、内供奉，或兼或攝，諸使下官亦如之。

translations.literal: there were again inspecting, bureau-attached, and inner-attendant posts, some concurrent and some acting; subordinate officials of the various commissioners were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: there were again inspecting, bureau-attached, and inner-attendant posts, some held concurrently and some in an acting capacity; subordinate officials of the various commissioners followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，升大夫、中丞品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang era, the ranks of the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor were raised.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huichang the ranks of the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor were raised.

sentences.zh: 東都留臺，有中丞一人、侍御史一人、殿中侍御史二人、監察御史三人；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's resident Censorate had one Vice Censor, one Attending Censor, two Palace Attending Censors, and three Investigating Censors;
translations.idiomatic: The resident Censorate at the Eastern Capital had one Vice Censor, one Attending Censor, two Palace Attending Censors, and three Investigating Censors;

sentences.zh: 元和後，不置中丞，以侍御史、殿中侍御史、監察御史主留臺務，而三院御史亦不常備。

translations.literal: After the Yuanhe era, no Vice Censor was appointed; Attending Censors, Palace Attending Censors, and Investigating Censors managed resident Censorate affairs, and censors of the three bureaus were not always fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhe no Vice Censor was appointed; Attending, Palace Attending, and Investigating Censors managed the resident bureau, and the three bureaus were not always fully staffed.

sentences.zh: 侍御史六人，從六品下。

translations.literal: Six Attending Censors, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Attending Censors, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌糾舉百寮及入閤承詔，知推、彈、雜事。

translations.literal: They held charge of impeaching the hundred officials and entering the Inner Hall to receive edicts, and managed investigation, impeachment, and miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: They impeached officials, entered the Inner Hall to receive edicts, and handled investigations, impeachments, and miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 凡三司理事，與給事中、中書舍人更直朝堂。

translations.literal: Whenever the Three Offices handled cases, they rotated duty in the court hall with the Supervising Secretary and Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Offices heard cases, they rotated duty in the court hall with the Supervising Secretary and Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 若三司所按而非其長官，則與刑部郎中、員外郎、大理司直、評事往訊。

translations.literal: If what the Three Offices prosecuted was not their own superior, they went with the Director and Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, the Direct Assessor and Reviewing Officer of the Court of Judicial Review to conduct inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: If the accused was not the censor's own superior, they went with officials of the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 彈劾，則大夫、中丞押奏。

translations.literal: For impeachment, the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor endorsed the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: For impeachments, the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor endorsed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 大事，法冠、朱衣、纁裳、白紗中單；

translations.literal: For great matters, the law cap, vermilion robe, crimson skirt, and white gauze inner garment;
translations.idiomatic: For major cases they wore the law cap, vermilion robe, crimson skirt, and white gauze undergarment;

sentences.zh: 小事，常服。

translations.literal: for minor matters, regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: for minor cases, regular dress.

sentences.zh: 久次者一人知雜事，謂之雜端，殿中監察職掌、進名、遷改及令史考第，臺内事顓決，亦號臺端。

translations.literal: The one longest in tenure managed miscellaneous matters—called the Miscellaneous Chief; he exclusively decided Palace and Investigation duties, name submissions, transfers, and clerks' examinations, and was also called the Bureau Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The senior censor managed miscellaneous affairs as the Miscellaneous Chief; he decided Palace and Investigation assignments, name submissions, transfers, and clerks' examinations, and was also called the Bureau Chief.

sentences.zh: 次一人知公廨。

translations.literal: The next one managed the office compound.
translations.idiomatic: The next censor managed the office compound.

sentences.zh: 次一人知彈。

translations.literal: The next one managed impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: The next managed impeachments.

sentences.zh: 分京城諸司及諸州爲東、西：次一人知西推、贓贖、三司受事，號副端；

translations.literal: The capital's various offices and prefectures were divided into East and West: the next one managed Western investigation, bribery redemption, and Three Offices reception of cases—called the Deputy Chief;
translations.idiomatic: The capital's offices and prefectures were divided into East and West: the next censor managed western investigations, bribery cases, and Three Offices intake—called the Deputy Chief;

sentences.zh: 次一人知東推、理匭等，有不糾舉者罰之；

translations.literal: the next one managed Eastern investigation, complaint-box cases, and the like; those who failed to impeach were punished;
translations.idiomatic: the next managed eastern investigations and complaint-box cases, and punished censors who failed to act;

sentences.zh: 以殿中侍御史第一人同知東推，莅太倉出納；

translations.literal: the first Palace Attending Censor jointly managed Eastern investigation and supervised receipts and disbursements at the Grand Granary;
translations.idiomatic: the senior Palace Attending Censor jointly managed eastern investigations and supervised the Grand Granary's receipts and disbursements;

sentences.zh: 第二人同知西推，莅左藏出納。

translations.literal: the second jointly managed Western investigation and supervised receipts and disbursements at the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: the second jointly managed western investigations and supervised the Left Treasury's receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 號四推御史。

translations.literal: They were called the Four Investigation Censors.
translations.idiomatic: They were called the Four Investigation Censors.

sentences.zh: 隻日，臺院受事；

translations.literal: On odd days the Bureau of the Censorate received cases;
translations.idiomatic: On odd days the Bureau of the Censorate received cases;

sentences.zh: 雙日，殿院受事。

translations.literal: on even days the Bureau of the Palace received cases.
translations.idiomatic: on even days the Bureau of the Palace received cases.

sentences.zh: 次侍御史一人，分司東都臺。

translations.literal: The next Attending Censor served at the Eastern Capital's resident bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Another Attending Censor served at the Eastern Capital's resident bureau.

sentences.zh: 凡御史以下遇長官於路，去戴下馬，長官斂轡止之。

translations.literal: Whenever censors below met their superiors on the road, they removed their hats and dismounted; the superior reined in and stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a censor met his superior on the road, he removed his hat and dismounted; the superior would rein in and tell him to remount.

sentences.zh: 出入行止，殿中以下視以爲法，先後有罰。

translations.literal: For coming, going, and conduct, those below the Palace Attending Censors took them as models; precedence violations were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Junior censors took the Palace Attending Censors as their model in conduct; violations of precedence were punished.

sentences.zh: 入朝，則與殿中侍御史隨仗分入，東則居侍中、黃門侍郎，給事中之次，西則居中書令、侍郎、舍人之次，各居中丞、大夫下。

translations.literal: On entering court, they entered with the Palace Attending Censors following the guard, divided east and west: on the east they stood after the Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and Supervising Secretary; on the west after the Chief Minister, Vice Minister, and Drafting Officer of the Secretariat—each below the Vice Censor and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At court they entered with the Palace Attending Censors in the guard formation, divided east and west: on the east they stood after the Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, and Supervising Secretary; on the west after the Chief Minister, Vice Minister, and Drafting Officer—all below the Vice Censor and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 毎一人東嚮承詔五日，有旨召御史，不呼名則承詔者出。

translations.literal: Each day one person faced east to receive edicts for five days; when an edict summoned a censor, if no name was called the one receiving edicts went out.
translations.idiomatic: Each censor in turn faced east to receive edicts for five days; when the emperor summoned a censor without naming him, the censor on edict duty responded.

sentences.zh: 樂彦瑋爲大夫，以嘗召兩御史，乃加副承詔一人，闕則殿中承乏。

translations.literal: When Yue Yanwei was Censor-in-Chief, because two censors had once been summoned, a deputy edict-receiver was added; if absent, a Palace Attending Censor filled in.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Yanwei was Censor-in-Chief, because two censors had once been summoned at once, a deputy edict-receiver was added; if he was absent, a Palace Attending Censor filled in.

sentences.zh: 監察御史分日直朝堂，入自側門，非奏事不至殿庭，正門無籍；

translations.literal: Investigating Censors rotated daily duty at the court hall, entering by the side gate; unless presenting a memorial they did not reach the hall courtyard; at the main gate there was no register;
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors rotated daily duty in the court hall, entering by the side gate; unless presenting a memorial they did not enter the hall courtyard, and they were not registered at the main gate;

sentences.zh: 天授中，詔側門置籍，得至殿庭；

translations.literal: during Tianshou, an edict ordered a register at the side gate, allowing access to the hall courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: during Tianshou an edict ordered a register at the side gate, allowing access to the hall courtyard;

sentences.zh: 開元七年，又詔隨仗入閤。

translations.literal: in the seventh year of Kaiyuan, another edict ordered them to enter the Inner Hall with the guard.
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh year of Kaiyuan another edict ordered them to enter the Inner Hall with the guard.

sentences.zh: 分左右巡，糾察違失，左巡知京城内，右巡知京城外，盡雍、洛二州之境，月一代，將晦，卽巡刑部、大理、東西徒坊、金吾、縣獄。

translations.literal: They were divided into Left and Right Patrol to investigate violations; the Left Patrol oversaw within the capital, the Right Patrol outside, throughout the territory of the Yong and Luo prefectures; they rotated monthly; near month's end they patrolled the Ministry of Justice, Court of Judicial Review, Eastern and Western penal wards, Golden Crow guards, and county prisons.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into Left and Right Patrols to investigate violations: the Left Patrol covered the capital interior, the Right the exterior, throughout Yong and Luo prefectures, rotating monthly; near month's end they inspected the Ministry of Justice, Court of Judicial Review, eastern and western penal wards, Golden Crow guards, and county prisons.

sentences.zh: 蒐狩，則監圍，察斷絶失禽者。

translations.literal: On hunts, they supervised the encirclement and investigated those who broke the line and lost game.
translations.idiomatic: On hunts they supervised the encirclement and investigated anyone who broke the line and lost game.

sentences.zh: 其後，以殿中掌左右巡；

translations.literal: Later, Palace Attending Censors took charge of the Left and Right Patrols;
translations.idiomatic: Later Palace Attending Censors took charge of the Left and Right Patrols;

sentences.zh: 尋以務劇，選用京畿縣尉。

translations.literal: soon because the duties were heavy, metropolitan county assistants were selected.
translations.idiomatic: soon because the duties were too heavy, metropolitan county assistants were appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 又置御史裏行使、侍御史裏行使、殿中裏行使、監察裏行使，以未爲正官，無員數。

translations.literal: Bureau-attached censors were again established—for Censor, Attending Censor, Palace Attending Censor, and Investigating Censor—because they were not regular posts, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau-attached posts were again established for censors, attending censors, palace attending censors, and investigating censors; because they were not regular posts, there was no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 唐法，殿中侍御史遷拜及職事，與侍御史鈞。

translations.literal: By Tang law, Palace Attending Censors in promotion and substantive duties were equal to Attending Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, Palace Attending Censors were equal to Attending Censors in promotion and substantive duties.

sentences.zh: 開元以降，權屬侍御史，而殿中兼知庫藏、宮門内事。

translations.literal: From Kaiyuan onward, authority belonged to Attending Censors, while Palace Attending Censors also managed treasuries and inner palace gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiyuan onward authority rested with Attending Censors, while Palace Attending Censors also managed treasuries and inner palace gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史臺不受訟，有訴可聞者略其姓名，託以風聞。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Censorate did not accept lawsuits; when there was a complaint that could be heard, the name was omitted and it was submitted as hearsay report.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Censorate did not accept lawsuits; when a complaint could be heard, the complainant's name was omitted and the case was submitted as a hearsay report.

sentences.zh: 其後，御史嫉惡者少，通狀壅絶。

translations.literal: Later, censors who hated evil were few, and general memorials were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Later few censors were zealous in prosecution, and general memorials were blocked.

sentences.zh: 十四年，乃定授事御史一人，知其日劾狀，題告事人姓名。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, one Case-Receiving Censor was fixed, who knew the day's impeachment reports and recorded the complainant's name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year one Case-Receiving Censor was appointed to track daily impeachment reports and record the complainant's name.

sentences.zh: 其後，宰相以御史權重，建議彈奏先白中丞、大夫，復通狀中書、門下，然後得奏。

translations.literal: Later, because the chancellors thought censors' authority was heavy, they proposed that impeachments first be reported to the Vice Censor and Censor-in-Chief, then a general memorial passed through the Secretariat and Chancellery, and only then could they be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because chancellors thought censors held too much power, they proposed that impeachments first be reported to the Vice Censor and Censor-in-Chief, then circulated through the Secretariat and Chancellery, before submission.

sentences.zh: 自是御史之任輕矣。

translations.literal: From this the censors' responsibilities became lighter.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the censors' authority was diminished.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，以侍御史分掌公廨、推、彈，自是雜端之任輕矣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Attending Censors were assigned separately to manage the office compound, investigation, and impeachment; from this the Miscellaneous Chief's responsibilities became lighter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong Attending Censors were assigned separately to manage the office compound, investigations, and impeachments; from then on the Miscellaneous Chief's role was diminished.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，命四推御史受事，周而復始，罷東西分日之限。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, the Four Investigation Censors were ordered to receive cases in rotation, and the limit of dividing East and West by day was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe the Four Investigation Censors were ordered to receive cases in rotation, abolishing the rule of dividing eastern and western cases by odd and even days.

sentences.zh: 隋末，廢殿内侍御史；

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, Palace Attending Censors within the Hall were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui the Palace Attending Censors were abolished;

sentences.zh: 義寧元年，承相府置察非掾二人；

translations.literal: in the first year of Yining, the Chancellor's Office established two Investigators of Wrongdoing;
translations.idiomatic: in the first year of Yining the Chancellor's Office established two Investigators of Wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 武德元年，改曰殿中侍御史；

translations.literal: in the first year of Wude, they were renamed Palace Attending Censors;
translations.idiomatic: in the first year of Wude they were renamed Palace Attending Censors;

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，置監察御史裏行；

translations.literal: in the first year of Longshuo, bureau-attached Investigating Censors were established;
translations.idiomatic: in the first year of Longshuo bureau-attached Investigating Censors were established;

sentences.zh: 武后文明元年，置殿中裏行，後亦顓以裏行名官；

translations.literal: in the first year of Civilizing Rule under Empress Wu, bureau-attached Palace posts were established; later offices were also exclusively named bureau-attached;
translations.idiomatic: in the first year of Civilizing Rule Empress Wu established bureau-attached Palace posts; later many offices were also given bureau-attached titles;

sentences.zh: 長安二年，置内供奉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, inner attendants were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chang'an inner attendants were established.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從七品下。

translations.literal: One Registrar, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Registrar, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌印，受事發辰，覈臺務，主公廨及戸奴婢、勳散官之職。

translations.literal: He held charge of seals, received cases and issued time-stamps, audited bureau affairs, and managed the office compound, household slaves and maidservants, and merit and honorary officials' duties.
translations.idiomatic: He managed seals, received cases and issued time-stamps, audited bureau affairs, and oversaw the office compound, household slaves and servants, and merit and honorary officials.

sentences.zh: 録事二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Two Recording Clerks, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Recording Clerks, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 有主事二人。

translations.literal: There were two Section Chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Section Chiefs.

sentences.zh: 臺院有令史七十八人，書令史二十五人，亭長六人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: The Bureau of the Censorate had seventy-eight clerks, twenty-five document clerks, six station chiefs, and twelve compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of the Censorate had seventy-eight clerks, twenty-five document clerks, six station chiefs, and twelve compound guards.

sentences.zh: 殿院有令史八人，書令史十八人。

translations.literal: The Bureau of the Palace had eight clerks and eighteen document clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of the Palace had eight clerks and eighteen document clerks.

sentences.zh: 察院有計史三十四人，令史十人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Investigation had thirty-four accounting clerks, ten clerks, and twelve compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Investigation had thirty-four accounting clerks, ten clerks, and twelve compound guards.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史九人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Nine Palace Attending Censors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine Palace Attending Censors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌殿庭供奉之儀，京畿諸州兵皆隸焉。

translations.literal: They held charge of ceremonial protocol in the palace hall; troops of the capital region and various prefectures were all subordinate to them.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised ceremonial protocol in the palace hall, and troops of the capital region and its prefectures were subordinate to them.

sentences.zh: 正班，列於閤門之外，糾離班、語不肅者。

translations.literal: In the regular formation they stood outside the Gate of the Inner Hall and cited those who left formation or spoke without decorum.
translations.idiomatic: In regular formation they stood outside the Gate of the Inner Hall and cited anyone who left ranks or spoke without decorum.

sentences.zh: 元日、冬至朝會，則乘馬、具服、戴黑豸升殿。

translations.literal: At New Year's and winter solstice court assemblies, they rode horses, wore full dress, and ascended the hall wearing black xie caps.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year's and winter solstice assemblies they rode horseback, wore full dress, and ascended the hall wearing black xie caps.

sentences.zh: 巡幸，則往來門旗之内，檢校文物虧失者。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses, they moved within the gate banners and inspected for losses or damage to ritual objects.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours they moved within the gate banners and inspected ritual objects for loss or damage.

sentences.zh: 一人同知東推，監太倉出納；

translations.literal: One jointly managed Eastern investigation and supervised receipts and disbursements at the Grand Granary;
translations.idiomatic: One jointly managed eastern investigations and supervised the Grand Granary's receipts and disbursements;

sentences.zh: 一人同知西推，監左藏出納；

translations.literal: one jointly managed Western investigation and supervised receipts and disbursements at the Left Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: one jointly managed western investigations and supervised the Left Treasury's receipts and disbursements;

sentences.zh: 二人爲廊下食使；

translations.literal: two served as corridor meal supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: two served as corridor meal supervisors;

sentences.zh: 二人分知左右巡；

translations.literal: two divided management of the Left and Right Patrols;
translations.idiomatic: two divided management of the Left and Right Patrols;

sentences.zh: 三人内供奉。

translations.literal: three were inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: and three were inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 監察御史十五人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Fifteen Investigating Censors, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were fifteen Investigating Censors, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌分察百僚，巡按州縣，獄訟、軍戎、祭祀、營作、太府出納皆莅焉；

translations.literal: They held charge of investigating the hundred officials separately, touring and inspecting prefectures and counties; lawsuits, military affairs, sacrifices, construction, and Grand Treasury receipts and disbursements were all overseen by them;
translations.idiomatic: They investigated officials, toured prefectures and counties, and oversaw lawsuits, military affairs, sacrifices, construction projects, and Grand Treasury receipts and disbursements;

sentences.zh: 知朝堂左右廂及百司綱目。

translations.literal: they knew the left and right wings of the court hall and the outlines of the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: they supervised the left and right wings of the court hall and tracked the business of the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 凡十道巡按，以判官二人爲佐，務繁則有支使。

translations.literal: For tours of inspection in the ten circuits, two judicial assistants served as aides; when duties were heavy there were dispatch officers.
translations.idiomatic: On tours of the ten circuits, two judicial assistants served as aides; when duties were heavy, dispatch officers were added.

sentences.zh: 其一，察官人善惡；

translations.literal: First, to inspect officials' good and evil conduct;
translations.idiomatic: First, to inspect the conduct of officials, good and bad;

sentences.zh: 其二，察戸口流散，籍帳隱沒，賦役不均；

translations.literal: second, to inspect scattered households, concealed registers, and unequal taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: second, to inspect scattered households, concealed registers, and unequal taxes and corvée labor;

sentences.zh: 其三，察農桑不勤，倉庫減耗；

translations.literal: third, to inspect neglect of agriculture and sericulture and depletion of granaries and storehouses;
translations.idiomatic: third, to inspect neglect of farming and sericulture and depletion of granaries and storehouses;

sentences.zh: 其四，察妖猾盜賊，不事生業，爲私蠧害；

translations.literal: fourth, to inspect crafty villains and bandits who did not pursue livelihoods and wrought private harm;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, to inspect crafty criminals and bandits who abandoned honest livelihoods and preyed on the people;

sentences.zh: 其五，察德行孝悌，茂才異等，藏器晦跡，應時用者；

translations.literal: fifth, to inspect those of filial and fraternal conduct, outstanding talent of exceptional grade, and hidden worth suited to the times;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, to identify men of filial and fraternal virtue, outstanding talent, and hidden ability fit for service;

sentences.zh: 其六，察黠吏豪宗兼幷縱暴，貧弱冤苦不能自申者。

translations.literal: sixth, to inspect crafty clerks and powerful clans who merged holdings and indulged in violence, and the poor and weak who suffered injustice and could not speak for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, to inspect crafty clerks and powerful clans who seized property and acted with violence, and the poor and weak who could not obtain redress for their grievances.

sentences.zh: 凡戰伐大克獲，則數俘馘、審功賞，然後奏之。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a great victory in war, they counted captives and severed ears, reviewed merit for rewards, and then memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: After a major military victory they counted captives and severed ears, reviewed merit for rewards, and then submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 屯田、鑄錢，嶺南、黔府選補，亦視功過糾察。

translations.literal: For garrison farming, coin casting, and selection and appointment in Lingnan and Qian prefectures, they likewise inspected achievements and faults.
translations.idiomatic: They also inspected garrison farming, coin casting, and appointments in Lingnan and Qian for merit and misconduct.

sentences.zh: 決囚徒，則與中書舍人、金吾將軍莅之。

translations.literal: When deciding cases of convicts, they attended together with the Secretariat Drafting Officer and the Golden Crow general.
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners were sentenced to death, they attended together with the Secretariat Drafting Officer and the Golden Crow general.

sentences.zh: 國忌齋，則與殿中侍御史分察寺觀。

translations.literal: On national mourning fasts, they divided inspection of temples and monasteries with Palace Attending Censors.
translations.idiomatic: On national mourning fasts they divided inspection of temples and monasteries with Palace Attending Censors.

sentences.zh: 莅宴射、習射及大祠、中祠，視不如儀者以聞。

translations.literal: They attended banquet archery, practice archery, and major and intermediate sacrifices, and reported those not conforming to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: They attended banquet archery, practice archery, and major and intermediate sacrifices, and reported violations of ritual.

sentences.zh: 初，開元中，兼巡傳驛，至二十五年，以監察御史檢校兩京舘驛。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Kaiyuan era, they also toured relay stations; by the twenty-fifth year Investigating Censors were appointed to inspect the two capitals' post stations.
translations.idiomatic: Initially in the Kaiyuan era they also toured relay stations; by the twenty-fifth year Investigating Censors were appointed to inspect post stations in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 大暦十四年，兩京以御史一人知舘驛，號舘驛使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali, one censor in each capital managed post stations—called the Post Station Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Dali one censor in each capital managed the post stations, titled Post Station Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 監察御史分察尙書省六司，繇下第一人爲始，出使亦然。

translations.literal: Investigating Censors divided inspection of the six bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, beginning with the lowest-ranked first; the same applied to those sent on mission.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors divided inspection of the six bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, beginning with the junior censor; the same rule applied to those on mission.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，以第一人察吏部、禮部，兼監祭使；

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, the first inspected the Ministries of Personnel and Rites and concurrently served as Sacrifice Supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan the senior censor inspected the Ministries of Personnel and Rites and concurrently served as Sacrifice Supervisor;

sentences.zh: 第二人察兵部、工部，兼舘驛使；

translations.literal: the second inspected the Ministries of War and Works and concurrently served as Post Station Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: the second inspected the Ministries of War and Works and concurrently served as Post Station Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 第三人察戸部、刑部。

translations.literal: the third inspected the Ministries of Revenue and Justice.
translations.idiomatic: the third inspected the Ministries of Revenue and Justice.

sentences.zh: 歳終議殿最。

translations.literal: At year's end they deliberated on superior and inferior performance.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they rated officials' performance.

sentences.zh: 元和中，以新人不出使無以觀能否，乃命顓察尙書省，號曰六察官。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, because new appointees did not go on mission and there was no way to observe their ability, they were ordered exclusively to inspect the Department of State Affairs—called the Six Inspection Officers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, because new appointees did not go on mission and their ability could not be tested, they were assigned exclusively to inspect the Department of State Affairs and were called the Six Inspection Officers.

sentences.zh: 開元十九年，以監察御史二人莅太倉、左藏庫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, two Investigating Censors oversaw the Grand Granary and Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan two Investigating Censors oversaw the Grand Granary and the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 三院御史，皆初領繁劇外府推事。

translations.literal: Censors of the three bureaus all initially took on the heavy duty of investigation cases in outer prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Censors of all three bureaus initially handled the demanding duty of investigating cases in outer prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其後，以殿中侍御史上一人爲監太倉使，第二人爲監左藏庫使。

translations.literal: Later, the senior Palace Attending Censor became Commissioner of the Grand Granary, the second Commissioner of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Later the senior Palace Attending Censor became Commissioner of the Grand Granary and the second became Commissioner of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 凡諸使下三院御史内供奉，其班居正臺監察御史之上。

translations.literal: For inner attendants among the three bureaus' censors under the various commissioners, their formation stood above regular Investigating Censors of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-attendant censors of the three bureaus under the various commissioners ranked above regular Investigating Censors of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 太常寺卿一人，正三品；

translations.literal: One Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, regular third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices had one Director, of regular third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，正四品上。

translations.literal: two Vice Directors, regular fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two Vice Directors, of regular fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌禮樂、郊廟、社稷之事，總郊社、太樂、鼓吹、太醫、太卜、廩犧、諸祠廟等署，少卿爲之貳。

translations.literal: They held charge of rites, music, suburban sacrifices, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; they oversaw the offices of Suburban Sacrifices, Grand Music, Military Music, Imperial Physicians, Grand Divination, Sacrificial Animals, and various temples and shrines; the Vice Directors were their deputies.
translations.idiomatic: They managed rites, music, suburban sacrifices, ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain, and oversaw the offices of Suburban Sacrifices, Grand Music, Military Music, Imperial Physicians, Grand Divination, Sacrificial Animals, and various temples; the Vice Directors served as deputies.

sentences.zh: 凡大禮，則贊引；

translations.literal: For all great rites, they guided and led;
translations.idiomatic: At major rites they guided the ceremony;

sentences.zh: 有司攝事，則爲亞獻；

translations.literal: when the relevant office acted in proxy, they served as secondary offerer;
translations.idiomatic: when a relevant office acted in the emperor's place, they served as secondary offerer;

sentences.zh: 三公行園陵，則爲副；

translations.literal: when the Three Dukes performed at imperial tombs, they served as deputies;
translations.idiomatic: when the Three Dukes performed rites at imperial tombs, they served as deputies;

sentences.zh: 大祭祀，省牲、器，則謁者爲之導；

translations.literal: at great sacrifices, when inspecting victims and vessels, ushers served as guides;
translations.idiomatic: at major sacrifices, when victims and vessels were inspected, ushers served as guides;

sentences.zh: 小祀及公卿嘉禮，命謁者贊相。

translations.literal: for minor sacrifices and congratulatory rites of dukes and ministers, ushers were ordered to assist.
translations.idiomatic: for minor sacrifices and congratulatory rites of dukes and ministers, ushers were ordered to assist.

sentences.zh: 凡巡幸、出師、克獲，皆擇日告太廟。

translations.literal: For all imperial progresses, dispatch of armies, and victories, an auspicious day was chosen to report to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial tours, military campaigns, and victories, an auspicious day was chosen to report to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 凡藏大享之器服，有四院：一曰天府院，藏瑞應及伐國所獲之寶，禘祫則陳于廟庭；

translations.literal: For storing vessels and robes of great offerings there were four courts: the first was called the Celestial Treasury Court, storing auspicious omens and treasures taken in campaigns against states—at di and xia sacrifices they were displayed in the temple courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Vessels and robes for great offerings were stored in four courts: the Celestial Treasury Court held auspicious objects and spoils of war, displayed in the temple courtyard at di and xia sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 二曰御衣院，藏天子祭服；

translations.literal: the second was called the Imperial Robes Court, storing the Son of Heaven's sacrificial garments;
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Robes Court held the emperor's sacrificial garments;

sentences.zh: 三曰樂縣院，藏六樂之器；

translations.literal: the third was called the Music and Bells Court, storing instruments of the six kinds of music;
translations.idiomatic: the Music and Bells Court held instruments of the six kinds of music;

sentences.zh: 四曰神廚院，藏御廩及諸器官奴婢。

translations.literal: the fourth was called the Divine Kitchen Court, storing the imperial granary and slaves and maidservants of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: the Divine Kitchen Court held the imperial granary and the slaves and servants of the various ritual offices.

sentences.zh: 初，有衣冠署，令，正八品上；

translations.literal: Initially there was the Office of Caps and Robes, with a director of regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Initially there was an Office of Caps and Robes, with a director of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，署廢。

translations.literal: in the first year of Zhenguan the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: abolished in the first year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 髙宗卽位，改治禮郎曰奉禮郎，以避帝名；

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, the Rite-Regulating Gentleman was renamed Ritual Gentleman to avoid the emperor's taboo name;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, the Rite-Regulating Gentleman was renamed Ritual Gentleman to avoid the imperial taboo;

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改太常寺曰奉常寺，九寺卿皆曰正卿，少卿曰大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was renamed the Court of Constant Offerings; directors of the nine courts were all called Chief Directors, Vice Directors were called Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was renamed the Court of Constant Offerings; directors of the nine courts were all called Chief Directors and vice directors Grand Masters.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年，復改太常寺曰司禮寺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu, it was again renamed the Court of Ritual Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai Empress Wu renamed it the Court of Ritual Administration.

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從五品下。

translations.literal: Two Assistants, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Assistants, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌判寺事。

translations.literal: They held charge of adjudicating court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated the court's affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡享太廟，則脩七祀于西門之内。

translations.literal: Whenever offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the seven sacrifices were performed within the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: When offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the seven sacrifices were performed within the west gate.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Two Registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 博士四人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Four Erudites, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Erudites, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌辨五禮；

translations.literal: They held charge of distinguishing the five rites;
translations.idiomatic: They distinguished the five rites;

sentences.zh: 按王公、三品以上功過善惡爲之諡；

translations.literal: they reviewed the merits, faults, good, and evil of princes, dukes, and those of third rank and above to assign posthumous titles;
translations.idiomatic: they reviewed the merits and faults of princes, dukes, and officials of third rank and above to assign posthumous titles;

sentences.zh: 大禮，則贊卿導引。

translations.literal: at great rites, they assisted and guided the Director.
translations.idiomatic: at major rites they assisted and guided the Director.

sentences.zh: 太祝六人，正九品上。

translations.literal: Six Grand Invokers, regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Grand Invokers, of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌出納神主；

translations.literal: They held charge of receiving and issuing spirit tablets;
translations.idiomatic: They received and issued spirit tablets;

sentences.zh: 祭祀則跪讀祝文；

translations.literal: at sacrifices they knelt and read the invocation;
translations.idiomatic: at sacrifices they knelt and read the invocation;

sentences.zh: 卿省牲則循牲告充，牽以授太官。

translations.literal: when the Director inspected the victims, they walked along the victims declaring them sufficient and led them to hand over to the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: when the Director inspected the sacrificial victims, they walked along the line declaring them acceptable and led them to the Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two Ritual Gentlemen, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Ritual Gentlemen, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌君臣版位，以奉朝會、祭祀之禮。

translations.literal: They held charge of the positions of ruler and ministers to serve the rites of court assemblies and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They arranged the positions of ruler and ministers for court assemblies and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宗廟則設皇帝位於庭，九廟子孫列焉，昭、穆異位，去爵從齒。

translations.literal: At the ancestral temple they set the emperor's position in the courtyard; descendants of the nine temples lined up—zhao and mu in different positions, setting aside rank to follow age.
translations.idiomatic: At the ancestral temple they placed the emperor's position in the courtyard; descendants of the nine temples lined up in zhao and mu positions, setting aside rank to follow age.

sentences.zh: 凡樽、彝、勺、冪、篚、坫、簠、簋、登，鈃、籩、豆，皆辨其位。

translations.literal: For all wine vessels, sacrificial vessels, ladles, covers, baskets, stands, grain vessels, food vessels, meat stands, platters, and cups, they distinguished their positions.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned positions for all ritual vessels—wine vessels, sacrificial bronzes, ladles, covers, baskets, stands, grain vessels, food vessels, meat stands, platters, and cups.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀、朝會，在位拜跪之節，皆贊導之。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices and court assemblies, the protocols of bowing and kneeling in position were all guided by them.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices and court assemblies they guided all protocols of bowing and kneeling.

sentences.zh: 公卿巡行諸陵，則主其威儀鼓吹，而相其禮。

translations.literal: When dukes and ministers toured the tombs, they directed their ceremonial guards and music and assisted in their rites.
translations.idiomatic: When dukes and ministers toured the imperial tombs, they directed their ceremonial guards and music and assisted in the rites.

sentences.zh: 協律郎二人，正八品上。

translations.literal: Two Pitch-Regulating Gentlemen, regular eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Pitch-Regulating Gentlemen, of regular eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌和律呂。

translations.literal: They held charge of harmonizing the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: They harmonized the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 録事二人，從九品上；

translations.literal: Two Recording Clerks, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: There were two Recording Clerks, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 八寺録事品同。

translations.literal: the Recording Clerks of the eight courts shared the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: the Recording Clerks of the eight courts shared the same rank.

sentences.zh: 有禮院修撰、檢討官各一人，府十二人，史二十三人，謁者十人，贊引二十人，贊者四人，祝史六人，贊者十六人。

translations.literal: There was one compiler and one reviser in the Rites Bureau, twelve clerks, twenty-three scribes, ten ushers, twenty guides, four assistants, six invocation scribes, and sixteen assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Bureau had one compiler and one reviser, twelve clerks, twenty-three scribes, ten ushers, twenty guides, four assistants, six invocation scribes, and sixteen ritual assistants.

sentences.zh: 太常寺、禮院禮生各三十五人，亭長八人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Rites Bureau each had thirty-five ritual students, eight station chiefs, and twelve compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Rites Bureau each had thirty-five ritual students, eight station chiefs, and twelve compound guards.

sentences.zh: 兩京郊社署兩京郊社署令各一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Suburban Sacrifices Offices of the two capitals each had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifices Offices of the two capitals each had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，從八品上。

translations.literal: each had one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: each with one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令掌五郊、社稷、明堂之位，與奉禮郎設樽、罍、篚、冪，而太官令實之。

translations.literal: The director held charge of the positions for the five suburban sacrifices, altars of soil and grain, and Hall of Enlightenment; with Ritual Gentlemen he set out wine vessels, jars, baskets, and covers, and the Director of the Grand Steward filled them.
translations.idiomatic: The director managed positions for the five suburban sacrifices, the altars of soil and grain, and the Hall of Enlightenment; with Ritual Gentlemen he arranged wine vessels, jars, baskets, and covers, and the Director of the Grand Steward filled them.

sentences.zh: 立燎壇，積柴。

translations.literal: He erected the fire altar and piled firewood.
translations.idiomatic: He erected the fire altar and piled firewood.

sentences.zh: 合朔有變，則巡察四門，以俟變過，明則罷。

translations.literal: When the new moon showed an eclipse, he patrolled the four gates to await the eclipse's passing; at dawn he ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When an eclipse occurred at the new moon, he patrolled the four gates until it passed; at dawn he ceased.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人，典事五人，掌固五人，門僕八人，齋郎百一十人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, four scribes, five stewards, five compound guards, eight gate servants, and one hundred ten fast officers.
translations.idiomatic: The office had two clerks, four scribes, five stewards, five compound guards, eight gate servants, and one hundred ten fast officers.

sentences.zh: 齋郎掌供郊廟之役。

translations.literal: Fast officers held charge of supplying labor for suburban sacrifices and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Fast officers supplied labor for suburban sacrifices and temples.

sentences.zh: 太廟九室，室有長三人，以主樽、罍、篚、冪、鎖鑰，又有罍洗二人；

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had nine chambers; each chamber had three chiefs to manage wine vessels, jars, baskets, covers, and keys, and also two jar-washers;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had nine chambers; each had three chiefs to manage vessels, covers, and keys, and two jar-washers;

sentences.zh: 郊壇有掌坐二十四人，以主神御之物。

translations.literal: the suburban altar had twenty-four seat managers to oversee objects for the spirit's use.
translations.idiomatic: the suburban altar had twenty-four seat managers to oversee ritual objects.

sentences.zh: 皆禮部奏補。

translations.literal: All were nominated for appointment by memorial from the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed on nomination by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡室長十年、掌座十二年，皆授官。

translations.literal: Chamber chiefs after ten years and seat managers after twelve years were all granted office.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years as chamber chief or twelve as seat manager, all received official appointment.

sentences.zh: 祭饗而員少，兼取三舘學生，皆絳衣絳幘。

translations.literal: When offerings were made and staff were few, students from the three institutes were also taken—all in crimson robes and crimson caps.
translations.idiomatic: When staff were insufficient for offerings, students from the three institutes were also recruited, all in crimson robes and caps.

sentences.zh: 更一番者，戸部下蠲符，歳一申考諸署所擇者，太常以十月申解於禮部，如貢舉法，帖論語及一大經。

translations.literal: After one rotation, the Ministry of Revenue issued tax exemption certificates; once a year those selected by the various offices were examined; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in the tenth month submitted their records to the Ministry of Rites; by the method of the civil service examinations they were tested on the Analects and one great classic.
translations.idiomatic: After one rotation the Ministry of Revenue issued tax exemption certificates; once a year candidates selected by the various offices were examined; in the tenth month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted them to the Ministry of Rites, who tested them on the Analects and one great classic by the civil examination method.

sentences.zh: 中第者，録奏，吏部注冬集散官，否者番上如初。

translations.literal: Those who passed were recorded and memorialized; the Ministry of Personnel assigned winter dispersal honorary offices; those who failed returned to rotation as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were recorded and memorialized; the Ministry of Personnel assigned winter honorary offices; those who failed returned to rotation as before.

sentences.zh: 六試而絀，授散官。

translations.literal: After six examinations with failure, they were granted honorary office.
translations.idiomatic: After failing six examinations, they received honorary office.

sentences.zh: 唐初，以郊社、太樂、鼓吹、太醫、太官、左藏、乘黃、典廄、典客、上林、太倉、平準、常平、典牧、左尙、右尙爲上署，鉤盾、右藏、織染、掌冶爲中署，珍羞、良醞、掌醞、守宮、武器、車府、司儀、崇玄、導官、甄官、河渠、弩坊、甲坊、舟楫、太卜、廩犧、中校、左校、右校爲下署。

translations.literal: Early in Tang, Suburban Sacrifices, Grand Music, Military Music, Imperial Physicians, Grand Steward, Left Treasury, Imperial Horses, Imperial Stables, Imperial Guests, Imperial Park, Grand Granary, Price Regulation, Ever-Normal Granary, Imperial Herds, Left Services, and Right Services were upper offices; Hooked Shield, Right Treasury, Weaving and Dyeing, and Metallurgy were middle offices; Delicacies, Fine Brew, Brew Management, Palace Guard, Weapons, Chariot Office, Ceremonial Protocol, Daoist Affairs, Guide Office, Casting Office, Canals, Crossbow Workshop, Armor Workshop, Boats, Grand Divination, Sacrificial Animals, Central Workshop, Left Workshop, and Right Workshop were lower offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang, Suburban Sacrifices, Grand Music, Military Music, Imperial Physicians, Grand Steward, Left Treasury, Imperial Horses, Imperial Stables, Imperial Guests, Imperial Park, Grand Granary, Price Regulation, Ever-Normal Granary, Imperial Herds, Left Services, and Right Services ranked as upper offices; Hooked Shield, Right Treasury, Weaving and Dyeing, and Metallurgy as middle offices; and Delicacies, Fine Brew, Brew Management, Palace Guard, Weapons, Chariot Office, Ceremonial Protocol, Daoist Affairs, Guide Office, Casting Office, Canals, Crossbow Workshop, Armor Workshop, Boats, Grand Divination, Sacrificial Animals, Central Workshop, Left Workshop, and Right Workshop as lower offices.

sentences.zh: 太樂署太樂署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Grand Music had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Grand Music had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 樂正八人，從九品下。

translations.literal: eight music masters, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and eight music masters, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 令掌調鐘律，以供祭饗。

translations.literal: The directors held charge of tuning bells and pitch pipes to supply sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The directors tuned the bells and pitch pipes to provide music for sacrificial banquets.

sentences.zh: 凡習樂，立師以教，而歳考其師之課業爲三等，以上禮部。

translations.literal: For all who studied music, masters were established to teach; each year the masters' coursework was examined and graded in three classes, and reported upward to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: For music training, masters were appointed to teach; each year their teaching was examined and graded upper, middle, or lower, and reported to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年大校，未成，則五年而校，以番上下。

translations.literal: Every ten years a great review was held; if completion had not been achieved, review came every five years, and by rotation they were advanced or demoted.
translations.idiomatic: A major review was held every ten years; if students had not finished, a review came every five years, and they were promoted or demoted by rotation.

sentences.zh: 有故及不任供奉，則輸資錢，以充伎衣樂器之用。

translations.literal: If there was cause or one was unfit for court service, subsidy money was paid in, to supply costumes and musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Those excused for cause or unfit for court performance paid subsidy fees to cover costumes and instruments.

sentences.zh: 散樂，閏月人出資錢百六十，長上者復繇役，音聲人納資者歳錢二千。

translations.literal: For irregular musicians, in intercalary months each person paid one hundred sixty cash in subsidy money; senior performers again performed corvée labor; vocalists who paid subsidies paid two thousand cash per year.
translations.idiomatic: Irregular musicians paid one hundred sixty cash each in intercalary months; senior performers still owed corvée duty; vocalists paying subsidies owed two thousand cash a year.

sentences.zh: 博士教之，功多者爲上第，功少者爲中第，不勤者爲下第，禮部覆之。

translations.literal: Erudites taught them; those with much achievement were upper class, those with little achievement middle class, the indolent lower class; the Ministry of Rites reviewed this.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites taught them; the most accomplished ranked upper, the less accomplished middle, and the idle lower; the Ministry of Rites reviewed the grades.

sentences.zh: 十五年有五上考、七中考者，授散官，直本司，年滿考少者，不敍。

translations.literal: After fifteen years, those with five superior evaluations and seven middling evaluations were granted irregular office and assigned directly to their office; when the term was full, those with few evaluations received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years, those with five superior and seven middling evaluations received irregular rank and a direct posting in their office; at term's end, those with too few good evaluations received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 教長上弟子四考，難色二人、次難色二人業成者，進考，得難曲五十以上任供奉者爲業成。

translations.literal: In teaching senior disciples, after four examinations, when two of the difficult category and two of the secondary-difficult category had completed their training, they advanced to examination; mastery was achieved when one could perform fifty or more difficult pieces and was appointed to court service.
translations.idiomatic: Senior disciples were examined four times; when two difficult-category and two secondary-difficult students finished training they took the advancement exam, and mastery meant knowing fifty or more difficult pieces and qualifying for court performance.

sentences.zh: 習難色大部伎三年而成，次部二年而成，易色小部伎一年而成，皆入等第三爲業成。

translations.literal: Study of the difficult category in the great ensemble took three years to complete, the secondary ensemble two years, the easy category in the small ensemble one year; all entered the third grade to count as mastery.
translations.idiomatic: The difficult category in the great ensemble took three years, the secondary ensemble two, and the easy category in the small ensemble one; all reached the third grade to count as trained.

sentences.zh: 業成、行脩謹者，爲助教；

translations.literal: Those who had completed training and whose conduct was cultivated and careful became assistant instructors;
translations.idiomatic: Those who finished training and were diligent in conduct became assistant instructors;

sentences.zh: 博士缺，以次補之。

translations.literal: when an erudite post was vacant, they were promoted in order to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: when an erudite post fell vacant, they filled it in order of seniority.

sentences.zh: 長上及別教未得十曲，給資三之一；

translations.literal: Senior performers and those under separate instruction who had not mastered ten pieces received one-third of the subsidy;
translations.idiomatic: Senior performers and separately instructed students who had not mastered ten pieces received one-third of the subsidy;

sentences.zh: 不成者隸鼓吹署。

translations.literal: those who did not complete training were attached to the Office of Military Music.
translations.idiomatic: those who failed to qualify were assigned to the Office of Military Music.

sentences.zh: 習大小橫吹，難色四番而成，易色三番而成；

translations.literal: In studying great and small transverse flutes, the difficult category required four rotations to complete, the easy category three rotations;
translations.idiomatic: Training in great and small transverse flutes took four rotations for the difficult category and three for the easy;

sentences.zh: 不成者，博士有讁。

translations.literal: if they did not complete training, the erudite was censured.
translations.idiomatic: if students failed to finish, their erudite was censured.

sentences.zh: 内教博士及弟子長教者，給資錢而留之。

translations.literal: Inner-instruction erudites and disciples who had long taught were given subsidy money and retained.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-instruction erudites and long-serving teaching disciples received subsidies and were kept on staff.

sentences.zh: 武德後，置内教坊于禁中。

translations.literal: After Wude, an Inner Music Office was established within the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wude era an Inner Music Office was set up inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 武后如意元年，改曰雲韶府，以中官爲使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi under Empress Wu, it was renamed the Cloud Harmony Office, with eunuchs as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's first Ruyi year it was renamed the Cloud Harmony Office and placed under eunuch directors.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，又置内教坊于蓬萊宮側，有音聲博士、第一曹博士、第二曹博士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, an Inner Music Office was again established beside Penglai Palace, with erudites of vocal music, of the First Section, and of the Second Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2 another Inner Music Office was set up beside Penglai Palace, with erudites for vocal music and for the first and second sections.

sentences.zh: 京都置左右教坊，掌俳優雜技。

translations.literal: In the capital, Left and Right Music Offices were established, managing actors and variety arts.
translations.idiomatic: The capital gained Left and Right Music Offices in charge of actors and acrobatic entertainments.

sentences.zh: 自是不隸太常，以中官爲教坊使。

translations.literal: From this time they were no longer subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; eunuchs served as commissioners of the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they no longer reported to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and eunuchs served as Music Office commissioners.

sentences.zh: 唐改太樂爲樂正，有府三人，史六人，典事八人，掌固六人，文武二舞郎一百四十人，散樂三百八十二人，仗内散樂一千人，音聲人一萬二十七人。

translations.literal: Tang changed Grand Music to music masters; there were three clerks, six scribes, eight record keepers, six compound guards, one hundred forty civil and military dancers of the two dances, three hundred eighty-two irregular musicians, one thousand irregular musicians within the guard, and ten thousand twenty-seven vocalists.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Grand Music posts became music masters; the office had three clerks, six scribes, eight record keepers, six compound guards, one hundred forty civil and military dancers, three hundred eighty-two irregular musicians, one thousand guard irregular musicians, and ten thousand twenty-seven vocalists.

sentences.zh: 有別教院。

translations.literal: There was a Separate Instruction Court.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Separate Instruction Court.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，改法曲所處院曰仙韶院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, the court where courtly melodies were housed was renamed the Immortal Harmony Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3 the court that housed courtly melodies was renamed the Immortal Harmony Court.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹署鼓吹署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Military Music had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Military Music had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從八品下；

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 樂正四人，從九品下。

translations.literal: four music masters, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and four music masters, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 令掌鼓吹之節。

translations.literal: The directors held charge of the measures for military music.
translations.idiomatic: The directors oversaw the rhythms and deployment of military music.

sentences.zh: 合朔有變，則帥工人設五鼓于太社，執麾旒于四門之塾，置龍牀，有變則舉麾撃鼓，變復而止。

translations.literal: When the new moon showed an omen, they led workmen to set up five drums at the Grand Altar of Soil, held banners and pennants at the schoolhouses of the four gates, placed dragon couches; when an omen appeared they raised the banner and struck the drums, and when the omen passed they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: If the new moon showed an omen, they led artisans to set five drums at the Grand Altar of Soil, posted banner bearers at the gate schoolhouses, and set out dragon couches; on an omen they raised banners and beat the drums, and ceased when it cleared.

sentences.zh: 馬射，設掆鼓金鉦，施龍牀。

translations.literal: For mounted archery, hanging drums and bronze gongs were set up and dragon couches deployed.
translations.idiomatic: At mounted archery they set up hanging drums and bronze gongs and deployed dragon couches.

sentences.zh: 大儺，帥鼓角以助侲子之唱。

translations.literal: For the great exorcism, they led drums and horns to assist the demon-quellers' chant.
translations.idiomatic: At the great exorcism they led drums and horns to accompany the demon-quellers' singing.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，典事四人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were three clerks, six scribes, four record keepers, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had three clerks, six scribes, four record keepers, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 唐幷淸商、鼓吹爲一署，增令一人。

translations.literal: Tang merged Pure Music and Military Music into one office and added one director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Pure Music and Military Music were merged into one office and one director was added.

sentences.zh: 太醫署太醫署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Imperial Physicians had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Imperial Physicians had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，醫監四人，幷從八品下；

translations.literal: two assistants and four medical supervisors, all subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: two assistants and four medical supervisors, all of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 醫正八人，從九品下。

translations.literal: eight medical masters, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and eight medical masters, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 令掌醫療之法，其屬有四：一曰醫師，二曰針師，三曰按摩師，四曰咒禁師。

translations.literal: The directors held charge of methods of medical treatment; subordinates were four: first, physicians; second, acupuncturists; third, massage therapists; fourth, spell-forbidding masters.
translations.idiomatic: The directors oversaw medical practice; subordinates fell into four groups: physicians, acupuncturists, massage therapists, and spell-forbidding masters.

sentences.zh: 皆教以博士，考試登用如國子監。

translations.literal: All were taught by erudites; examination and appointment followed the State Academy.
translations.idiomatic: All were taught by erudites and examined for appointment on the State Academy model.

sentences.zh: 醫師、醫正、醫工療病，書其全之多少爲考課。

translations.literal: Physicians, medical masters, and medical artisans treated illness; they recorded how many were fully cured for evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians, medical masters, and medical artisans treated patients and recorded cures for their performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 歳給藥以防民疾。

translations.literal: Each year medicines were dispensed to guard against popular illness.
translations.idiomatic: Each year medicines were distributed to prevent widespread disease.

sentences.zh: 凡陵寢廟皆儲以藥，尙藥、太常醫各一人受之。

translations.literal: All imperial tombs and temples were stocked with medicines; one from the Office of Imperial Medicines and one court physician from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices each received them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tombs and temples all kept medicine stores, received by one officer from Imperial Medicines and one physician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宮人患坊有藥庫，監門莅出給；

translations.literal: The palace women's sick ward had a medicine storehouse; gate supervisors attended to dispense supplies;
translations.idiomatic: The palace women's sick ward kept a pharmacy, and gate supervisors issued the drugs;

sentences.zh: 醫師、醫監、醫正番別一人莅坊。

translations.literal: physicians, medical supervisors, and medical masters by rotation each sent one person to attend the ward.
