translations.idiomatic: physicians, medical supervisors, and medical masters rotated one officer each to staff the ward.

sentences.zh: 凡課藥之州，置採藥師一人。

translations.literal: In all provinces levied for medicines, one medicinal-gathering master was established.
translations.idiomatic: Every province taxed for medicines appointed one medicinal-gathering master.

sentences.zh: 京師以良田爲園，庶人十六以上爲藥園生，業成者爲師。

translations.literal: In the capital, good fields served as gardens; commoners sixteen and above became medicinal-garden students, and those who completed training became masters.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital good farmland served as herb gardens; commoners sixteen or older became garden students, and graduates became instructors.

sentences.zh: 凡藥，辨其所出，擇其良者進焉。

translations.literal: For all medicines, their places of origin were distinguished and the finest were selected to be presented.
translations.idiomatic: All medicines were traced to their sources, and only the best were submitted.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人，主藥八人，藥童二十四人，藥園師二人，藥園生八人，掌固四人，醫師二十人，醫工百人，醫生四十人，典藥一人，針工二十人，針生二十人，按摩工五十六人，按摩生十五人，咒禁師二人，咒禁工八人，咒禁生十人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, four scribes, eight chief pharmacists, twenty-four pharmacy youths, two medicinal-garden masters, eight medicinal-garden students, four compound guards, twenty physicians, one hundred medical artisans, forty medical students, one pharmacy manager, twenty needle artisans, twenty needle students, fifty-six massage artisans, fifteen massage students, two spell-forbidding masters, eight spell-forbidding artisans, and ten spell-forbidding students.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two clerks, four scribes, eight chief pharmacists, twenty-four pharmacy youths, two garden masters, eight garden students, four compound guards, twenty physicians, one hundred medical artisans, forty medical students, one pharmacy manager, twenty needle artisans and twenty needle students, fifty-six massage artisans and fifteen massage students, and two spell-forbidding masters with eight artisans and ten students.

sentences.zh: 醫博士一人，正八品上；

translations.literal: One Erudite of Medicine, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: One Erudite of Medicine, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 助教一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: one assistant instructor, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant instructor, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教授諸生以本草、甲乙、脈經，分而爲業：一曰體療，二曰瘡腫，三曰少小，四曰耳目口齒，五曰角法。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students in the Materia Medica, the A and B Canon, and the Pulse Classic, divided into specialties: first, internal medicine; second, sores and swellings; third, pediatrics; fourth, eyes, ears, mouth, and teeth; fifth, horn cautery.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students from the Materia Medica, the A and B Canon, and the Pulse Classic in five specialties: internal medicine, sores and swellings, pediatrics, eyes, ears, mouth, and teeth, and horn cautery.

sentences.zh: 針博士一人，從八品上；

translations.literal: One Erudite of Acupuncture, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: One Erudite of Acupuncture, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 助教一人，針師十人，並從九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant instructor and ten acupuncture masters, all subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: one assistant instructor and ten acupuncture masters, all of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教針生以經脈、孔穴，教如醫生。

translations.literal: They held charge of teaching needle students the channels and points; instruction followed the medical students.
translations.idiomatic: They taught needle students the channels and acupoints on the same model as medical students.

sentences.zh: 按摩博士一人，按摩師四人，并從九品下。

translations.literal: One Erudite of Massage, four massage masters, all subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Erudite of Massage and four massage masters, all of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教導引之法以除疾，損傷折跌者，正之。

translations.literal: They held charge of teaching guiding-and-pulling methods to remove illness; for injury, fracture, and sprain, they set them right.
translations.idiomatic: They taught guiding and pulling exercises to cure illness and set fractures, sprains, and injuries.

sentences.zh: 咒禁博士一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: One Erudite of Spell-Forbidding, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Erudite of Spell-Forbidding, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教咒禁祓除爲厲者，齋戒以受焉。

translations.literal: They held charge of teaching spell-forbidding to exorcise what brings pestilence; one fasted and purified to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: They taught spell-forbidding to exorcise pestilence, received only after fasting and purification.

sentences.zh: 太卜署太卜署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Grand Divination had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Grand Divination had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從八品下；

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 卜正、博士各二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: two divination masters and two erudites each, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: two divination masters and two erudites, all of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌卜筮之法：一曰龜，二曰五兆，三曰易，四曰式。

translations.literal: They held charge of methods of divination by tortoise and milfoil: first, tortoise shell; second, five omens; third, the Changes; fourth, the Shi method.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw divination by four methods: tortoise shell, five omens, the Changes, and the Shi method.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、大事，率卜正卜日，示髙於卿，退而命龜，旣灼而占，先上旬，次中旬，次下旬。

translations.literal: For sacrifices and great affairs, divination masters were led to divine the day, the height was shown to ministers, they withdrew and ordered the tortoise, and once scorched they divined—first the first ten-day period, next the middle ten-day period, next the last ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices and major events, divination masters chose the day, showed the elevation to ministers, withdrew to order the tortoise, and after scorching read it—first the first ten-day period, then the middle, then the last.

sentences.zh: 小祀、小事者，則卜正示髙、命龜、作，而太卜令佐莅之。

translations.literal: For minor sacrifices and minor affairs, the divination master showed the height, ordered the tortoise, and performed the divination, while the director and assistant of Grand Divination attended.
translations.idiomatic: For minor rites and minor matters the divination master showed the elevation, ordered the tortoise, and performed the divination, attended by the director and assistant of Grand Divination.

sentences.zh: 季冬，帥侲子堂贈大儺，天子六隊，太子二隊，方相氏右執戈、左執楯而導之，唱十二神名，以逐惡鬼，儺者出，磔雄鷄于宮門、城門。

translations.literal: In late winter, demon-quellers were led into the central hall to perform the great exorcism of sending away; the Son of Heaven had six companies, the Heir Apparent two; the Fangxiang clan right hand held a halberd, left hand held a shield and guided them, chanting the names of the twelve spirits to drive off evil ghosts; when the exorcists went out, a cock was dismembered at the palace gate and city gate.
translations.idiomatic: In late winter they led demon-quellers into the central hall for the great exorcism; the emperor had six companies and the heir apparent two; the Fangxiang chief bore a halberd in his right hand and a shield in his left, chanting the twelve spirits' names to drive off demons; when the exorcists left, a cock was sacrificed at the palace and city gates.

sentences.zh: 有卜助教二人，卜師二十人，巫師十五人，卜筮生四十五人，府一人，史二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were two assistant instructors of divination, twenty divination masters, fifteen shamans, forty-five divination students, one clerk, two scribes, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two divination assistant instructors, twenty divination masters, fifteen shamans, forty-five divination students, one clerk, two scribes, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 廩犧署廩犧署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Sacrificial Animals had one director, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Sacrificial Animals had one director, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌犧牲粢盛之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of sacrificial victims and grain offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They managed sacrificial animals and grain offerings.

sentences.zh: 祀用太牢者，三牲加酒、脯、醢，與太祝牽牲就牓位，卿省牲，則北面告腯，以授太官。

translations.literal: When sacrifices used the great pen, the three victims were joined with wine, dried meat, and relishes; together with the Grand Invoker they led the victims to the tablet position; when ministers inspected the victims, they faced north and reported the fatness, then handed them to the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When a sacrifice used the great pen, the three victims were accompanied by wine, dried meat, and relishes; with the Grand Invoker they led the animals to the spirit tablet; ministers inspected them, reported the fatness facing north, and handed them to the Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 籍田，則供耒于司農卿，卿以授侍中；

translations.literal: For the plowing ceremony, plows were supplied to the Minister of Agriculture, and the minister handed them to the Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: For the ceremonial plowing they supplied plows to the Minister of Agriculture, who passed them to the Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 籍田所收以供粢盛、五齊、三酒之用，以餘及槀飼犧牲。

translations.literal: the harvest of the plowing field supplied grain offerings, the five clears, and the three wines; the remainder and straw fed sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: the plowing-field harvest supplied grain offerings, the five clears, and the three wines, with the surplus and straw used to feed sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 有府一人，史二人，典事二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, two record keepers, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had one clerk, two scribes, two record keepers, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 汾祠署汾祠署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of the Fen Shrine had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Fen Shrine had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從八品上。

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌享祭灑掃之制。

translations.literal: They held charge of regulations for offerings, sprinkling, and sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: They regulated offerings, sprinkling, and sweeping at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人，廟幹二人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, four scribes, and two temple laborers.
translations.idiomatic: It had two clerks, four scribes, and two temple laborers.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年置署。

translations.literal: The office was established in the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The office was established in Kaiyuan 21.

sentences.zh: 三皇五帝以前帝王、三皇、五帝、周文王、周武王、漢髙祖、兩京武成王廟令一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: Temples to pre–Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors emperors, the Three Sovereigns, the Five Emperors, King Wen of Zhou, King Wu of Zhou, Emperor Gaozu of Han, and the Martial Completion King in the two capitals each had one director, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Temples to pre–Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rulers, the Three Sovereigns, the Five Emperors, Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou, Emperor Gaozu of Han, and the Martial Completion King in both capitals each had one director, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正八品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌開闔、灑掃、釋奠之禮。

translations.literal: They held charge of opening and closing, sprinkling and sweeping, and the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: They managed opening and closing the temples, cleaning, and libation rites.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府二人，史四人，廟幹二人，掌固四人，門僕八人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, two temple laborers, four compound guards, and eight gate servants.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, two temple laborers, four compound guards, and eight gate servants.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，兩京置齊太公廟署，其後廢；

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, temple offices to Duke Tai of Qi were established in the two capitals; later they were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 2 temple offices to Duke Tai of Qi were set up in both capitals, then later abolished;

sentences.zh: 開元十九年復置。

translations.literal: in the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: and restored in Kaiyuan 19.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，初置周文王廟署；

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, a temple office to King Wen of Zhou was first established;
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 a temple office to King Wen of Zhou was first established;

sentences.zh: 六載，置三皇五帝廟署；

translations.literal: in the sixth year, temple offices to the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth year, offices for the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 七載，置三皇五帝以前帝王廟署；

translations.literal: in the seventh year, a temple office to emperors before the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh year, an office for pre–Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors rulers;

sentences.zh: 九載，置周武王漢髙祖廟署。

translations.literal: in the ninth year, temple offices to King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Gaozu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: and in the ninth year, offices for Kings Wu of Zhou and Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，改齊太公署爲武成王廟署，朱全忠曰武明。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, the office to Duke Tai of Qi was changed to the Martial Completion King Temple Office; Zhu Quanzhong styled it Martial Illumination.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1 the Duke Tai of Qi office became the Martial Completion King Temple Office; Zhu Quanzhong later styled it Martial Illumination.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從六品上；

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌酒醴膳羞之政，總太官、珍羞、良醞、掌醢四署。

translations.literal: They held charge of policy for wines, brews, and prepared foods, overseeing the four offices of Grand Steward, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Pickle Management.
translations.idiomatic: They managed wine, brew, and food service and oversaw the offices of Grand Steward, Delicacies, Fine Brew, and Pickle Management.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，省牲鑊、濯溉；

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, they inspected the cooking vessels and washing of victims;
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices they inspected the cooking pots and washing of victims;

sentences.zh: 三公攝祭，則爲終獻。

translations.literal: when the Three Dukes performed the sacrifice by proxy, they made the final offering.
translations.idiomatic: when the Three Dukes officiated by proxy, they performed the final offering.

sentences.zh: 朝會宴享，則節其等差。

translations.literal: At court assemblies and banquets, they regulated the gradations.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies and banquets they regulated the ranks of service.

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: There were two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Two record clerks were on staff.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改光祿寺曰司宰寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Court of Imperial Entertainments was renamed the Court of the Chief Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Court of Imperial Entertainments was renamed the Court of the Chief Steward.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年，曰司膳寺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu, it was called the Court of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's first Guangzhai year it became the Court of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 有府十一人，史二十一人，亭長六人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were eleven clerks, twenty-one scribes, six station chiefs, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had eleven clerks, twenty-one scribes, six station chiefs, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 太官署太官署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Grand Steward had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Grand Steward had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: four assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供祠宴朝會膳食。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying meals for sacrifices, banquets, and court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: They provided food for sacrifices, banquets, and court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 祭日，令白卿詣厨省牲鑊，取明水、明火，帥宰人割牲，取毛血實豆，遂烹。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the director reported to the minister, went to the kitchen to inspect the cooking vessels and victims, took clear water and sacred fire, led the butchers to cut the victims, took hair and blood to fill the dou, then cooked them.
translations.idiomatic: On sacrifice day the director informed the minister, went to the kitchen to inspect pots and victims, drew clear water and sacred fire, led butchers to slaughter the animals, placed hair and blood in the dou vessels, and then cooked the meat.

sentences.zh: 又實簠簋，設于饌幕之内。

translations.literal: They also filled the fu and gui vessels and set them within the feast curtain.
translations.idiomatic: They also filled the fu and gui vessels and set them inside the feast tent.

sentences.zh: 有府四人，史八人，監膳十人，監膳史十五人，供膳二千四百人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were four clerks, eight scribes, ten meal superintendents, fifteen meal superintendents' scribes, two thousand four hundred meal servers, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had four clerks, eight scribes, ten meal superintendents, fifteen scribes to the meal superintendents, two thousand four hundred meal servers, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 珍羞署珍羞署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Delicacies had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Delicacies had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供祭祀、朝會、賓客之庶羞，榛栗、脯脩、魚鹽、菱芡之名數。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying common delicacies for sacrifices, court assemblies, and guests—the kinds and quantities of hazelnuts, chestnuts, dried meats, fish, salt, water caltrop, and gorgon fruit.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied ordinary delicacies for sacrifices, court assemblies, and guests, regulating the kinds and amounts of hazelnuts, chestnuts, dried meats, fish, salt, water caltrop, and gorgon fruit.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱元年，改肴藏署曰珍羞署，神龍元年復舊，開元元年又改。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chui Gong under Empress Wu, the Meat Storehouse Office was renamed the Office of Delicacies; in the first year of Shenlong the old name was restored; in the first year of Kaiyuan it was changed again.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's first Chui Gong year the Meat Storehouse Office became the Office of Delicacies; in Shenlong 1 the former name returned; in Kaiyuan 1 it was changed once more.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，典書八人，餳匠五人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were three clerks, six scribes, eight record keepers, five confectioners, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had three clerks, six scribes, eight record keepers, five confectioners, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 良醞署良醞署令二人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Fine Brew had two directors, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Fine Brew had two directors, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供五齊、三酒。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying the five mashes and three wines.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied the five mashes and three wines.

sentences.zh: 享太廟，則供鬱鬯以實六彝；

translations.literal: When offering at the Grand Temple, they supplied fragrant libation to fill the six ritual vessels;
translations.idiomatic: For offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple they provided fragrant libation to fill the six ritual bronzes;

sentences.zh: 進御，則供春暴、秋淸、酴𨣿、桑落之酒。

translations.literal: for presentation to the emperor, they supplied spring mash, autumn clear, yeast-mash, and Sangluo wines.
translations.idiomatic: for the imperial table they supplied spring mash, autumn clear, yeast-mash, and Sangluo wines.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，監事二人，掌醞二十人，酒匠十三人，奉觶百二十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were three clerks, six scribes, two superintendents, twenty brew keepers, thirteen wine artisans, one hundred twenty cup bearers, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had three clerks, six scribes, two superintendents, twenty brew keepers, thirteen wine artisans, one hundred twenty cup bearers, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 掌醢署掌醢署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Pickle Management had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Pickle Management had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供醢醯之物：一曰鹿醢，二曰兔醢，三曰羊醢，四曰魚醢。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying pickled and fermented items: first, deer pickle; second, hare pickle; third, sheep pickle; fourth, fish pickle.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied pickles and fermented condiments: deer pickle, hare pickle, sheep pickle, and fish pickle.

sentences.zh: 宗廟，用葅以實豆；

translations.literal: for the ancestral temple, they used pickled vegetables to fill the dou;
translations.idiomatic: for the ancestral temple they filled the dou with pickled vegetables;

sentences.zh: 賓客、百官，用醯醬以和羹。

translations.literal: for guests and the hundred officials, they used vinegar sauce to harmonize the stew.
translations.idiomatic: for guests and all officials they used vinegar sauce to season the stew.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史二人，主醢十人，醬匠二十三人，酢匠十二人，豉匠十二人，葅醯匠八人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, two scribes, ten chief pickle officers, twenty-three sauce artisans, twelve vinegar artisans, twelve fermented-bean artisans, eight pickled-and-vinegar artisans, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had two clerks, two scribes, ten chief pickle officers, twenty-three sauce artisans, twelve vinegar artisans, twelve fermented-bean artisans, eight pickle-and-vinegar artisans, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 衞尉寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Guards had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Guards had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌器械文物，總武庫、武器、守宮三署。

translations.literal: They held charge of implements and ritual objects, overseeing the three offices of the Armory, Weapons, and Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: They managed implements and ceremonial equipment and oversaw the Armory, Weapons, and Palace Guard offices.

sentences.zh: 兵器入者，皆籍其名數。

translations.literal: All weapons brought in were registered by name and number.
translations.idiomatic: Every weapon received was entered in the register by name and count.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、朝會，則供羽儀、節鉞、金鼓、帷帟、茵席。

translations.literal: At sacrifices and court assemblies, they supplied feather insignia, batons of authority, gilded drums, curtains and canopies, and mats.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices and court assemblies they provided feather banners, ceremonial axes, gilded drums, curtains and canopies, and mats.

sentences.zh: 凡供宮衞者，歳再閲，有敝則脩於少府。

translations.literal: All items supplied for palace guard were inspected twice a year; if worn out, they were repaired at the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Palace-guard equipment was inspected twice yearly; worn items were sent to the Court of the Imperial Treasury for repair.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade,

sentences.zh: 録事一人。

translations.literal: and one record clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk were on staff.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改曰司衞寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, it was renamed the Court of the Chief Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of the Chief Guard.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年又改。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu it was changed again.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's first Guangzhai year it was changed again.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十一人，亭長四人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were six clerks, eleven scribes, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had six clerks, eleven scribes, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 丞，掌判寺事，辨器械出納之數。

translations.literal: The assistants held charge of deciding court affairs and distinguishing the numbers of implements issued and received.
translations.idiomatic: The assistants adjudicated court business and tracked the issue and receipt of equipment.

sentences.zh: 大事承制敕，小事則聽於尙書省。

translations.literal: Major matters followed imperial edicts; minor matters were decided by the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Major matters followed imperial edicts; minor ones were referred to the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 兩京武庫署兩京武庫署令各二人，從六品下；

translations.literal: The Armory Offices of the two capitals each had two directors, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Armory Offices of the two capitals each had two directors, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各二人，從八品下。

translations.literal: each with two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: each with two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌藏兵械。

translations.literal: They held charge of storing weapons.
translations.idiomatic: They stored arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 有赦，建金鷄，置鼓宮城門之右、大理及府縣囚徒至，則撃之。

translations.literal: When there was an amnesty, they erected a golden rooster and set a drum to the right of the palace-city gate; when prisoners of the Court of Judicial Review and the prefectures and counties arrived, it was struck.
translations.idiomatic: On amnesty they raised a golden rooster and placed a drum to the right of the palace gate; when prisoners from the Court of Judicial Review and the prefectures and counties arrived, the drum was beaten.

sentences.zh: 監事各一人，正九品上。

translations.literal: Each had one superintendent, regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one superintendent, of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 諸署監事，品同。

translations.literal: Superintendents of the various offices shared the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents of the various offices held the same rank.

sentences.zh: 有府各六人，史各六人，典事各二人，掌固各五人。

translations.literal: Each had six clerks, six scribes, two record keepers, and five compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each had six clerks, six scribes, two record keepers, and five compound guards.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年，東都亦置署。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, the Eastern Capital also established an office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 an office was also established in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 武器署武器署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Weapons had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Weapons had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌外戎器。

translations.literal: They held charge of external military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: They managed field weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、巡幸，則納於武庫。

translations.literal: At sacrifices and imperial tours, items were turned in to the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: After sacrifices and imperial tours, equipment was returned to the Armory.

sentences.zh: 給六品以上葬鹵簿、棨戟。

translations.literal: They supplied funeral regalia and halberd escorts for those of sixth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: They issued funeral regalia and halberd escorts for officials of sixth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 凡戟，廟、社、宮、殿之門二十有四，東宮之門一十八，一品之門十六，二品及京兆河南太原尹、大都督、大都護之門十四，三品及上都督、中都督、上都護、上州之門十二，下都督、下都護、中州、下州之門各十。

translations.literal: For halberds in general: twenty-four at the gates of the temple, altar of soil and grain, palace, and hall; eighteen at the gates of the Eastern Palace; sixteen at a first-ranker's gates; fourteen at a second-ranker's gates and those of the metropolitan magistrates of Jingzhao, Henan, and Taiyuan, grand area commanders, and grand protectors-general; twelve at a third-ranker's gates and those of a superior area commander, middle area commander, superior protector-general, and superior prefecture; ten each at the gates of an inferior area commander, inferior protector-general, middle prefecture, and inferior prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Halberd escorts were allotted thus: twenty-four at the gates of temples, altars, palaces, and halls; eighteen at the Eastern Palace; sixteen for first rank; fourteen for second rank and for the Jingzhao, Henan, and Taiyuan metropolitan magistrates, grand area commanders, and grand protectors-general; twelve for third rank and for superior area commanders, middle area commanders, superior protectors-general, and superior prefectures; ten each for inferior area commanders, inferior protectors-general, middle prefectures, and inferior prefectures.

sentences.zh: 衣幡壞者，五歳一易之。

translations.literal: When garment banners were damaged, they were replaced once every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Damaged garment banners were replaced every five years.

sentences.zh: 薨卒者旣葬，追還。

translations.literal: After those who died in office were buried, the items were pursued and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral of a deceased official, the regalia was recovered.

sentences.zh: 監事二人。

translations.literal: There were two superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: Two superintendents were on staff.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史六人，典事二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, six scribes, two record keepers, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had two clerks, six scribes, two record keepers, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，東都亦置署。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, the Eastern Capital also established an office.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan an office was also set up in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 守宮署守宮署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Palace Guard had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Palace Guard had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供帳帟。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying tents and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: They provided tents, curtains, and canopies.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、巡幸，則設王公百官之位。

translations.literal: At sacrifices and imperial tours, they set the places for princes and dukes and the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices and imperial tours they arranged seating for princes, dukes, and all officials.

sentences.zh: 吏部、兵部、禮部試貢舉人，則供帷幕。

translations.literal: When the Ministries of Personnel, War, and Rites examined tribute candidates, they supplied curtains.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministries of Personnel, War, and Rites tested tribute candidates, they provided examination curtains.

sentences.zh: 王公婚禮，亦供帳具。

translations.literal: For princely and ducal weddings, they also supplied tent furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: They also furnished tents and fittings for princely and ducal weddings.

sentences.zh: 京諸司長上官，以品給其牀罽。

translations.literal: For senior officials of the various offices in the capital, beds and rugs were allotted by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials of capital agencies received beds and rugs according to rank.

sentences.zh: 供蕃客帷帟，則題歳月。

translations.literal: When supplying curtains for foreign guests, the year and month were inscribed.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains issued to foreign guests were dated by year and month.

sentences.zh: 席壽三年，氈壽五年，褥壽七年；

translations.literal: mats had a service life of three years, felt five years, and mattresses seven years;
translations.idiomatic: mats lasted three years, felt five, and mattresses seven;

sentences.zh: 不及期而壞，有罰。

translations.literal: if they were damaged before the term, there was punishment.
translations.idiomatic: premature wear incurred penalties.

sentences.zh: 監事二人。

translations.literal: There were two superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: Two superintendents were on staff.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史四人，掌設六人，幕士八十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, four scribes, six setup officers, eighty tent men, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had two clerks, four scribes, six setup officers, eighty tent men, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 宗正寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Clan had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Clan had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌天子族親屬籍，以別昭穆；

translations.literal: They held charge of the registers of the emperor's clan kinship, to distinguish senior and junior lines;
translations.idiomatic: They kept the registers of the imperial clan to distinguish senior and junior lines;

sentences.zh: 領陵臺、崇玄二署。

translations.literal: they oversaw the two offices of Mausoleum Terrace and Exalted Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: and oversaw the Mausoleum Terrace and Exalted Mystery offices.

sentences.zh: 凡親有五等，先定於司封：一曰皇帝周親、皇后父母，視三品；

translations.literal: Kinship in general had five grades, first determined by the Bureau of Enfeoffment: first, the emperor's close kin and the empress's parents, treated as third rank;
translations.idiomatic: Kin were divided into five grades, first set by the Bureau of Enfeoffment: first, the emperor's close kin and the empress's parents, treated as third rank;

sentences.zh: 二曰皇帝大功親、小功尊屬，太皇太后、皇太后、皇后周親，視四品；

translations.literal: second, the emperor's greater-mourning kin and lesser-mourning senior kin, and the close kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress, treated as fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: second, the emperor's greater-mourning kin and lesser-mourning senior kin, and the close kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress, treated as fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 三曰皇帝小功親、緦麻尊屬，太皇太后、皇太后、皇后大功親，視五品；

translations.literal: third, the emperor's lesser-mourning kin and finest-hemp senior kin, and the greater-mourning kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress, treated as fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: third, the emperor's lesser-mourning kin and finest-hemp senior kin, and the greater-mourning kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress, treated as fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 四曰皇帝緦麻親、袒免尊屬，太皇太后、皇太后、皇后小功親；

translations.literal: fourth, the emperor's finest-hemp kin and bare-shoulder senior kin, and the lesser-mourning kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the emperor's finest-hemp kin and bare-shoulder senior kin, and the lesser-mourning kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and empress;

sentences.zh: 五曰皇帝袒免親，太皇太后小功卑屬，皇太后、皇后緦麻親，視六品。

translations.literal: fifth, the emperor's bare-shoulder kin, the lesser-mourning junior kin of the Grand Empress Dowager, and the finest-hemp kin of the Empress Dowager and empress, treated as sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the emperor's bare-shoulder kin, the Grand Empress Dowager's lesser-mourning junior kin, and the Empress Dowager's and empress's finest-hemp kin, treated as sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 皇帝親之夫婦男女，降本親二等，餘親降三等，尊屬進一等，降而過五等者不爲親。

translations.literal: For husbands, wives, sons, and daughters among the emperor's kin, they were lowered two grades from their original kin grade; other kin were lowered three grades; senior kin advanced one grade; if lowering passed beyond the fifth grade, they were no longer counted as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Spouses and children of the emperor's kin dropped two grades from their original kin grade; other relatives dropped three; senior kin advanced one; kin lowered beyond the fifth grade ceased to count as kin.

sentences.zh: 諸王、大長公主、長公主親，本品；

translations.literal: Kin of princes, grand elder princesses, and elder princesses kept their own rank;
translations.idiomatic: Kin of princes, grand elder princesses, and elder princesses retained their own rank;

sentences.zh: 嗣王、郡王非三等親者，亦視五品；

translations.literal: heirs apparent and commandery princes who were not kin of the third grade were also treated as fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: heirs apparent and commandery princes who were not third-grade kin were also treated as fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉，視諸親。

translations.literal: the Commandant of Horse-Attendants was treated like other kin.
translations.idiomatic: the Commandant of Horse-Attendants was ranked like other kin.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、冊命、朝會，陪位、襲封者皆以簿書上司封。

translations.literal: For sacrifices, investitures, and court assemblies, those attending in support and those inheriting enfeoffments all submitted their registers to the Bureau of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices, investitures, and court assemblies, attendants in support and heirs to enfeoffments all reported through registers to the Bureau of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade,

sentences.zh: 知圖譜官一人，脩玉牒官一人，知宗子表疎官一人，録事二人。

translations.literal: one officer knowing genealogical charts, one officer revising the jade genealogy, one officer knowing the tables of imperial sons and collaterals, and two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: one officer for genealogical charts, one for the jade genealogy, one for tables of imperial sons and collaterals, and two record clerks were on staff.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，置宗師一人，後省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, one clan mentor was established; later it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 one clan mentor was appointed; the post was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改宗正寺曰司宗寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Court of the Imperial Clan was renamed the Court of the Clan Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the Court of the Imperial Clan was renamed the Court of the Clan Director.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年曰司屬寺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu it was called the Court of Clan Subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's first Guangzhai year it became the Court of Clan Subordinates.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史五人，亭長四人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were five clerks, five scribes, four station chiefs, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: It had five clerks, five scribes, four station chiefs, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 京都太廟齋郎各一百三十人，門僕各三十三人，主簿、録事各二人。

translations.literal: At the capital, the Grand Temple had one hundred thirty fast officers each, thirty-three gate servants each, and two registrars and two record clerks each.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the Grand Temple had one hundred thirty fast officers and thirty-three gate servants each, with two registrars and two record clerks.

sentences.zh: 諸陵臺諸陵臺令各一人，從五品上；

translations.literal: The various Mausoleum Terrace offices each had one director, subordinate fifth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each Mausoleum Terrace office had one director, of subordinate fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，從七品下。

translations.literal: each with one assistant, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: each with one assistant, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 建初、啓運、興寧、永康陵，令各一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: For the tombs of Jianchu, Qiyun, Xingning, and Yongkang, each had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Jianchu, Qiyun, Xingning, and Yongkang tombs each had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: each with one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: each with one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌守衞山陵。

translations.literal: They held charge of guarding the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: They guarded the imperial mountain tombs.

sentences.zh: 凡陪葬，以文武分左右，子孫從父祖者亦如之；

translations.literal: For all co-burial, civil and military were placed left and right; descendants following fathers and grandfathers were likewise arranged;
translations.idiomatic: Co-burials placed civil officials on one side and military on the other; descendants buried with fathers and grandfathers followed the same rule;

sentences.zh: 宮人陪葬，則陵戸成墳。

translations.literal: when palace women were co-buried, tomb households formed the mound.
translations.idiomatic: when palace women were buried alongside, tomb households formed the mound.

sentences.zh: 諸陵四至有封，禁民葬，唯故墳不毀。

translations.literal: All tombs had sealed boundaries on the four sides; commoners were forbidden to bury there; only old mounds were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Each tomb had sealed boundaries on all sides; common burials were forbidden; only pre-existing mounds were left intact.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，以宗廟所奉不可名以署，太常少卿韋縚奏廢太廟署，以少卿一人知太廟事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, because what the ancestral temple enshrined could not be named as an office, Vice Director Wei Zong of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized to abolish the Grand Temple Office and have one vice director manage Grand Temple affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24, because the ancestral temple's charge could not be titled as an office, Vice Director Wei Zong of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized to abolish the Grand Temple Office and assign one vice director to manage temple affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，濮陽王徹爲宗正卿，恩遇甚厚，建議以宗正司屬籍，乃請以陵寢、宗廟隸宗正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Prince Che of Puyang became Director of the Imperial Clan, received very generous favor, and proposed that because the Imperial Clan Court managed subordinate registers, he then requested that mausoleums and the ancestral temple be placed under the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Prince Che of Puyang became Director of the Imperial Clan. Favored warmly, he argued that the court's proper charge was clan registers and asked that imperial tombs and the ancestral temple be placed under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，駙馬都尉張垍爲太常卿，得幸，又以太廟諸陵署隸太常。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, Commandant of Horse-Attendants Zhang Yi became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, gained favor, and again placed the Grand Temple and the various mausoleum offices under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 12 Commandant of Horse-Attendants Zhang Yi became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Favored by the throne, he again placed the Grand Temple and all mausoleum offices under that court.

sentences.zh: 十載，改獻、昭、乾、定、橋五陵署爲臺，升令品，永康、興寧二陵稱署如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the five mausoleum offices of Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, and Qiao were changed to terraces, the directors' ranks were raised, while the two tombs of Yongkang and Xingning kept the title office as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, and Qiao mausoleum offices were renamed terraces and their directors' ranks were raised; the Yongkang and Xingning tombs still used the title office.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，復以陵廟隸宗正。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, mausoleum temples were again placed under the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 mausoleum temples were again placed under the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，太常卿姜慶初復奏以陵廟隸太常，大暦二年復舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Director Jiang Qingchu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again memorialized to place mausoleum temples under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in the second year of Dali the former arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 Director Jiang Qingchu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again asked that mausoleum temples be placed under his court; in Dali 2 the old arrangement was restored.

sentences.zh: 陵臺有録事各一人，府各二人，史各四人，主衣、主輦、主藥各四人，典事各三人，掌固各二人，陵戸各三百人，昭陵、乾陵、橋陵增百人。

translations.literal: Each Mausoleum Terrace had one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, four chiefs each for garments, carriages, and medicines, three setup officers, two compound guards, and three hundred tomb households; Zhaoling, Qianling, and Qiaoling each added one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each Mausoleum Terrace had one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, four chiefs each for garments, carriages, and medicines, three setup officers, two compound guards, and three hundred tomb households; Zhaoling, Qianling, and Qiaoling each added one hundred more.

sentences.zh: 諸陵有録事各一人，府各一人，史各二人，典事各二人，掌固各二人，陵戸各百人。

translations.literal: Each mausoleum had one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, two compound guards, and one hundred tomb households.
translations.idiomatic: Each mausoleum had one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, two compound guards, and one hundred tomb households.

sentences.zh: 諸太子廟諸太子廟令各一人，從八品上；

translations.literal: Each Crown Prince Temple office had one director, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each Crown Prince Temple had one director, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，正九品下；

translations.literal: each with one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each with one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 録事各一人。

translations.literal: each with one record clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk each.

sentences.zh: 令掌灑掃開闔之節，四時享祭焉。

translations.literal: The directors held charge of the rules for sweeping, opening, and closing, and seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The directors oversaw sweeping, opening and closing the gates, and the seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 有府各一人，史各二人，典事各二人，掌固各一人。

translations.literal: Each had one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, and one compound guard.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, and one compound guard.

sentences.zh: 諸太子陵諸太子陵令各一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: Each Crown Prince Tomb office had one director, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each crown prince tomb had one director, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，從九品下；

translations.literal: each with one assistant, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each with one assistant, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 録事各一人。

translations.literal: each with one record clerk.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk each.

sentences.zh: 有府各一人，史各二人，典事各二人，掌固各一人，陵戸各三十人。

translations.literal: Each had one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, one compound guard, and thirty tomb households.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one clerk, two scribes, two setup officers, one compound guard, and thirty tomb households.

sentences.zh: 太常舊有太廟署，令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices formerly had a Grand Temple Office, with one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices formerly maintained a Grand Temple Office with one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: two assistants, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 齋郎二十四人。

translations.literal: twenty-four fast officers.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty-four fast officers.

sentences.zh: 崇玄署令崇玄署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Exalted Mystery Office had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Exalted Mystery Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌京都諸觀名數與道士帳籍、齋醮之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of the names and numbers of all abbeys in the capital, the registers of Daoist priests, and fasting and offering rites.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the roster of capital abbeys, Daoist priests' registers, and fasting and offering rites.

sentences.zh: 新羅、日本僧入朝學問，九年不還者編諸籍。

translations.literal: Monks from Silla and Japan who came to court to study and did not return within nine years were entered in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Silla and Japanese monks who came to court to study and failed to return within nine years were entered on the registers.

sentences.zh: 道士、女官、僧、尼，見天子必拜。

translations.literal: Daoist priests, priestesses, monks, and nuns all bowed on seeing the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests, priestesses, monks, and nuns all bowed when received by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡止民家，不過三夜。

translations.literal: Whenever they lodged in commoners' homes, they might not stay more than three nights.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging in private homes was limited to three nights.

sentences.zh: 出踰宿者，立案連署，不過七日，路遠者州縣給程。

translations.literal: Those away overnight required a filed document with joint signatures, not exceeding seven days; for distant routes prefectures and counties issued travel schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight absences required a filed document with joint signatures, for no more than seven days; distant travel received itineraries from prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 天下觀一千六百八十七，道士七百七十六，女官九百八十八；

translations.literal: Under Heaven there were one thousand six hundred eighty-seven abbeys, seven hundred seventy-six Daoist priests, and nine hundred eighty-eight priestesses;
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide there were 1,687 abbeys, 776 Daoist priests, and 988 priestesses;

sentences.zh: 寺五千三百五十八，僧七萬五千五百二十四，尼五萬五百七十六。

translations.literal: five thousand three hundred fifty-eight temples, seventy-five thousand five hundred twenty-four monks, and fifty thousand five hundred seventy-six nuns.
translations.idiomatic: 5,358 temples, 75,524 monks, and 50,576 nuns.

sentences.zh: 兩京度僧、尼、道士、女官，御史一人涖之。

translations.literal: For ordaining monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and priestesses in the Two Capitals, one censor attended.
translations.idiomatic: Ordination of monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and priestesses in the Two Capitals was supervised by one censor.

sentences.zh: 毎三歳州、縣爲籍，一以留縣，一以留州；

translations.literal: Every three years prefectures and counties compiled registers: one copy remained in the county, one in the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Every three years prefectures and counties compiled registers, keeping one copy in the county and one in the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 僧、尼，一以上祠部，道士、女官，一以上宗正，一以上司封。

translations.literal: for monks and nuns, one copy went up to the Bureau of Temples; for Daoist priests and priestesses, one to the Imperial Clan and one to the Bureau of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: monks and nuns sent one copy to the Bureau of Temples; Daoist priests and priestesses sent one to the Imperial Clan and one to the Bureau of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史三人，典事六人，掌固二人，崇玄學博士一人、學生百人。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, three scribes, six setup officers, two compound guards, one erudite of the Exalted Mystery Academy, and one hundred students.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two clerks, three scribes, six setup officers, two compound guards, one Exalted Mystery erudite, and one hundred students.

sentences.zh: 隋以署隸鴻臚，又有道塲、玄壇。

translations.literal: Under Sui the office was attached to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and there were also the Daoist Arena and Mystery Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui the office belonged to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, which also maintained the Daoist Arena and Mystery Altar.

sentences.zh: 唐置諸寺觀監，隸鴻臚寺，毎寺觀有監一人。

translations.literal: Tang established supervisors for temples and abbeys, attached to the Court of Imperial Entertainments; each temple or abbey had one supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang appointed supervisors for temples and abbeys under the Court of Imperial Entertainments, one supervisor per temple or abbey.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，廢寺觀監。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, temple and abbey supervisors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan the temple and abbey supervisors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，置漆園監，尋廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, a Lacquer Garden supervisor was established and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 a Lacquer Garden supervisor was established and soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年，置崇玄學於玄元皇帝廟。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, the Exalted Mystery Academy was established at the Temple of the Mysterious Primordial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 the Exalted Mystery Academy was founded at the Temple of the Mysterious Primordial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，兩京置博士、助教各一員，學生百人，毎祠享，以學生代齋郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, the Two Capitals each received one erudite and one teaching assistant, with one hundred students; at each sacrificial offering, students replaced fast officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 each capital received one erudite and one teaching assistant and one hundred students; at each offering students replaced the fast officers.

sentences.zh: 二載，改崇玄學曰崇玄舘，博士曰學士，助教曰直學士，置大學士一人，以宰相爲之，領兩京玄元宮及道院，改天下崇玄學爲通道學，博士曰道德博士，未幾而罷。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Exalted Mystery Academy was renamed the Exalted Mystery Hall; erudites became academicians, teaching assistants direct academicians; one grand academician was appointed, held by the chief minister, overseeing the Mysterious Primordial palaces and Daoist courts of the Two Capitals; empire-wide Exalted Mystery academies became Passage academies, erudites moral erudites—and soon all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the academy became the Exalted Mystery Hall; erudites became academicians and assistants direct academicians; a grand academician, filled by the chief minister, oversaw the Mysterious Primordial palaces and Daoist courts of the Two Capitals; empire-wide schools were renamed Passage academies with moral erudites—and the reform was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 寶應、永泰間，學生存者亡幾。

translations.literal: Between Baoying and Yongtai, few students survived.
translations.idiomatic: Between Baoying and Yongtai scarcely any students remained.

sentences.zh: 大暦三年，復增至百人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, the number was restored to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 3 enrollment was restored to one hundred.

sentences.zh: 初，天下僧、尼、道士、女官，皆隸鴻臚寺，武后延載元年，以僧、尼隸祠部。

translations.literal: At first, empire-wide monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and priestesses all belonged to the Court of Imperial Entertainments; in the first year of Yanzai under Empress Wu, monks and nuns were placed under the Bureau of Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Initially all monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and priestesses fell under the Court of Imperial Entertainments; in Empress Wu's Yanzai 1 monks and nuns were transferred to the Bureau of Temples.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，道士、女官隸宗正寺，天寶二載，以道士隸司封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, Daoist priests and priestesses were placed under the Court of the Imperial Clan; in the second year of Tianbao, Daoist priests were placed under the Bureau of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24 Daoist priests and priestesses were placed under the Court of the Imperial Clan; in Tianbao 2 Daoist priests were transferred to the Bureau of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，崇玄舘罷大學士，後復置左右街大功德使、東都功德使、脩功德使，總僧、尼之籍及功役。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, the Exalted Mystery Hall abolished the grand academician; later the commissioners of great merit for the Left and Right Streets, Eastern Capital merit, and repair merit were restored, overseeing registers and corvée of monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 the Exalted Mystery Hall abolished the grand academician; later commissioners of great merit for the Left and Right Streets, the Eastern Capital, and repairs were restored to oversee monks' and nuns' registers and labor service.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，以道士、女官隸左右街功德使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, Daoist priests and priestesses were placed under the commissioners of merit of the Left and Right Streets.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2 Daoist priests and priestesses were placed under the Left and Right Street commissioners of merit.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，以僧、尼隸主客，太淸宮置玄元舘，亦有學士，至六年廢，而僧、尼復隸兩街功德使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang, monks and nuns were placed under the Bureau of Guests; the Grand Purity Palace established a Mysterious Primordial Hall, which also had academicians; by the sixth year it was abolished, and monks and nuns again belonged to the Two Streets' commissioners of merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 2 monks and nuns were transferred to the Bureau of Guests; the Grand Purity Palace founded a Mysterious Primordial Hall with its own academicians; by Huichang 6 that hall was abolished and monks and nuns again fell under the Two Streets' commissioners of merit.

sentences.zh: 太僕寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Stud had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Stud had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從六品上；

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: four assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上；

translations.literal: two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and two record clerks.

sentences.zh: 卿掌廄牧、輦輿之政，總乘黃、典廄、典牧、車府四署及諸監牧。

translations.literal: The minister held charge of stable herds and carriage policy, overseeing the four offices of Imperial Horses, Imperial Stables, Imperial Herds, and Chariot Office and the various pasture supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: The minister managed stables, herds, and imperial transport, overseeing the Imperial Horses, Imperial Stables, Imperial Herds, and Chariot offices and all pasture supervisors.

sentences.zh: 行幸，供五路屬車。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses, they supplied attendant carriages for the five routes.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses they supplied attendant carriages for the five routes.

sentences.zh: 凡監牧籍帳，歳受而會之，上駕部以議考課。

translations.literal: All pasture-supervisor registers were received yearly and consolidated, then submitted to the Carriage Department for performance review.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture supervisors' registers were received each year, consolidated, and submitted to the Carriage Department for performance review.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，太僕寺曰司馭寺，武后光宅元年改曰司僕寺。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, the Court of the Imperial Stud was called the Court of Chariot Mastery; in the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu it was renamed the Court of Servants.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui the court was renamed the Court of Chariot Mastery; in Empress Wu's Guangzhai 1 it became the Court of Servants.

sentences.zh: 有府十七人，史三十四人，獸醫六百人，獸醫博士四人，學生百人，亭長四人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were seventeen clerks, thirty-four scribes, six hundred veterinary physicians, four veterinary erudites, one hundred students, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seventeen clerks, thirty-four scribes, six hundred veterinary physicians, four veterinary erudites, one hundred students, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 乘黃署乘黃署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Imperial Horses Office had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Horses Office had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供車路及馴馭之法。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying carriage routes and methods of training and driving.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied imperial carriage routes and oversaw training and driving.

sentences.zh: 凡有事，前期四十日，率駕士調習，尙乘隨路色供馬；

translations.literal: For any affair, forty days beforehand they led carriage masters in drill; the Office of Imperial Carriages supplied horses by route color;
translations.idiomatic: Before any event they drilled the carriage masters forty days in advance; the Office of Imperial Carriages supplied horses by route color;

sentences.zh: 前期二十日，調習於内侍省。

translations.literal: twenty days beforehand they drilled at the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: and drilled at the Palace Domestic Service twenty days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 有府一人，史二人，駕士一百四十人，羊車小史十四人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, one hundred forty carriage masters, fourteen goat-carriage junior scribes, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one clerk, two scribes, one hundred forty carriage masters, fourteen goat-carriage junior scribes, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 典廄署典廄署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Imperial Stables Office had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Stables Office had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and four assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌飼馬牛、給養雜畜。

translations.literal: They held charge of feeding horses and cattle and supplying mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: They fed horses and cattle and supplied miscellaneous livestock.

sentences.zh: 良馬一丁，中馬二丁，駑馬三丁，乳駒、乳犢十給一丁。

translations.literal: One labor unit for each fine horse, two for each middling horse, three for each poor horse; ten nursing colts or calves counted as one unit.
translations.idiomatic: Fine horses required one labor unit each, middling horses two, poor horses three; ten nursing colts or calves counted as one unit.

sentences.zh: 有府四人，史八人，主乘六人，典事八人，執馭百人，駕士八百人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were four clerks, eight scribes, six chiefs of carriage, eight setup officers, one hundred drivers, eight hundred carriage masters, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included four clerks, eight scribes, six chiefs of carriage, eight setup officers, one hundred drivers, eight hundred carriage masters, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 典牧署典牧署令三人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Imperial Herds Office had three directors, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Herds Office had three directors, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞六人，從九品上。

translations.literal: six assistants, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and six assistants, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌諸牧雜畜給納及酥酪脯腊之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of delivery of mixed livestock from the pastures and matters of butter, cheese, dried meat, and cured meats.
translations.idiomatic: They received mixed livestock from the pastures and managed butter, cheese, dried meat, and cured meats.

sentences.zh: 羣牧所送羊犢，以供廩犧、尙食。

translations.literal: Lambs and kids sent by the herd offices supplied the Sacrificial Animals Office and Imperial Food Service.
translations.idiomatic: Lambs and kids from the herd offices supplied the Sacrificial Animals Office and Imperial Food Service.

sentences.zh: 監事八人。

translations.literal: eight supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: It had eight supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府四人，史八人，典事十六人，主酪七十四人，駕士百六十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were four clerks, eight scribes, sixteen setup officers, seventy-four chiefs of dairy, one hundred sixty carriage masters, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included four clerks, eight scribes, sixteen setup officers, seventy-four dairy chiefs, one hundred sixty carriage masters, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 車府署車府署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Chariot Office had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Chariot Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌王公以下車路及馴馭之法。

translations.literal: They held charge of carriage routes for princes and dukes downward and methods of training and driving.
translations.idiomatic: They managed carriage routes for princes, dukes, and lower ranks and oversaw training and driving.

sentences.zh: 從官三品以上婚、葬，給駕士。

translations.literal: For weddings and funerals of attendant officials of third rank and above, carriage masters were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Weddings and funerals of attendant officials of third rank and above were supplied with carriage masters.

sentences.zh: 凡路車之馬牛，率馭士調習。

translations.literal: For all road-carriage horses and cattle, driving masters led drill.
translations.idiomatic: Horses and cattle for road carriages were drilled under driving masters.

sentences.zh: 有府一人，史二人，典書四人，馭士百七十五人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were one clerk, two scribes, four archive clerks, one hundred seventy-five driving masters, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one clerk, two scribes, four archive clerks, one hundred seventy-five driving masters, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 諸牧監上牧監監各一人，從五品下；

translations.literal: Each upper pasture supervisor had one supervisor, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each upper pasture supervisor had one supervisor, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監各二人，正六品下；

translations.literal: each with two deputy supervisors, regular sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each with two deputy supervisors, of regular sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各二人，正八品上；

translations.literal: each with two assistants, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: each with two assistants, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿各一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: each with one registrar, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one registrar each, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 中牧監監，正六品下；

translations.literal: Middle pasture supervisors had supervisors of regular sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Middle pasture supervisors ranked regular sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監，從六品下；

translations.literal: deputy supervisors, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: deputy supervisors of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞，從八品上；

translations.literal: assistants, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: assistants of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿，從九品上。

translations.literal: registrars, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: registrars of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 下牧監監，從六品下；

translations.literal: Lower pasture supervisors had supervisors of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Lower pasture supervisors ranked subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監，正七品下；

translations.literal: deputy supervisors, regular seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: deputy supervisors of regular seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞，正九品上；

translations.literal: assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: assistants of regular ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿，從九品下。

translations.literal: registrars, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: registrars of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 中牧監副監、丞，減上牧監一員。

translations.literal: Middle pasture supervisors had one fewer deputy supervisor and assistant than upper pasture supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Middle pasture supervisors had one fewer deputy supervisor and assistant than upper ones.

sentences.zh: 南使、西使，丞各三人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Southern and Western commissioners each had three assistants, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern and Western commissioners each had three assistants, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 録事各一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: each with one record clerk, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk each, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 北使、鹽州使，丞各二人，從七品下。

translations.literal: The Northern and Yanchuan commissioners each had two assistants, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern and Yanchuan commissioners each had two assistants, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌群牧孳課。

translations.literal: They held charge of herd breeding and tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw herd breeding and tax levies.

sentences.zh: 凡馬五千爲上監，三千爲中監，不及爲下監。

translations.literal: In general, five thousand horses made an upper supervisor, three thousand a middle supervisor, and fewer made a lower supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Pastures with five thousand horses ranked as upper supervisors, three thousand as middle, and fewer as lower.

sentences.zh: 馬牛之羣，有牧長，有尉。

translations.literal: Horse and cattle herds had herd chiefs and wardens.
translations.idiomatic: Horse and cattle herds had herd chiefs and wardens.

sentences.zh: 馬之駑、良，皆著籍，良馬稱左，駑馬稱右。

translations.literal: Poor and fine horses were all entered in registers; fine horses were called left, poor horses right.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and fine horses were all registered; fine horses were listed as left, poor horses as right.

sentences.zh: 毎歳孟秋，羣牧使以諸監之籍合爲一，以仲秋上於寺，送細馬，則有牽夫、識馬小兒、獸醫等。

translations.literal: Each year in early autumn the herd commissioner consolidated the registers of all supervisors into one; in mid-autumn it was submitted to the court, and when delivering fine horses there were handlers, horse-knowing youths, veterinary physicians, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in early autumn the herd commissioner consolidated all pasture registers; in mid-autumn they were submitted to the court. Fine-horse deliveries included handlers, horse boys, veterinary physicians, and the like.

sentences.zh: 凡馬游牝以三月，駒犢在牧者，三歳別羣。

translations.literal: In general, roaming mares were bred in the third month; colts and calves kept on the pastures were separated into herds at age three.
translations.idiomatic: Mares were bred in the third month; colts and calves on the pastures were separated into herds at age three.

sentences.zh: 孳生過分有賞，死耗亦以率除之。

translations.literal: Breeding beyond quota received rewards; deaths and losses were also deducted according to set rates.
translations.idiomatic: Breeding above quota earned rewards; deaths and losses were deducted at prescribed rates.

sentences.zh: 歳終監牧使巡按，以功過相除爲考課。

translations.literal: At year's end the pasture-supervisor commissioner toured and inspected, offsetting merits against faults to determine performance review.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the pasture-supervisor commissioner made inspection tours, netting merits against faults for performance review.

sentences.zh: 上牧監，有録事各一人，府各三人，史各六人，典事各八人，掌固各四人。

translations.literal: Upper pasture supervisors each had one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, eight setup officers, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each upper pasture supervisor had one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, eight setup officers, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 中牧監，減府一人，史、典事各減二人。

translations.literal: Middle pasture supervisors had one fewer clerk, and two fewer scribes and setup officers each.
translations.idiomatic: Middle pasture supervisors had one fewer clerk and two fewer scribes and setup officers each.

sentences.zh: 下牧監，典事、掌固減二人。

translations.literal: Lower pasture supervisors had two fewer setup officers and compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Lower pasture supervisors had two fewer setup officers and compound guards.

sentences.zh: 南使、西使，録事、史各一人，府各五人，史各九人；

translations.literal: The Southern and Western commissioners each had one record clerk and one scribe, five clerks, and nine scribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern and Western commissioners each had one record clerk and one scribe, five clerks, and nine scribes;

sentences.zh: 北使、鹽州使，録事以下員數及品，如南使。

translations.literal: The Northern and Yanchuan commissioners had the same numbers and ranks below record clerk as the Southern commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern and Yanchuan commissioners matched the Southern commissioner in staff numbers and ranks from record clerk down.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，置八使，分總監坊。

translations.literal: During Linde, eight commissioners were established to oversee pasture compounds separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the Linde era eight commissioners were set up, each overseeing pasture compounds.

sentences.zh: 秦、蘭、原、渭四州及河曲之地。

translations.literal: the four prefectures of Qin, Lan, Yuan, and Wei and the lands of the River Bend.
translations.idiomatic: covering Qin, Lan, Yuan, and Wei prefectures and the River Bend region.

sentences.zh: 凡監四十有八：南使有監十五，西使有監十六，北使有監七，鹽州使有監八，嵐州使有監二。

translations.literal: In all there were forty-eight supervisors: the Southern commissioner had fifteen, the Western sixteen, the Northern seven, the Yanchuan eight, and the Lanzhou two.
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-eight supervisors in all: fifteen under the Southern commissioner, sixteen under the Western, seven under the Northern, eight under Yanchuan, and two under Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自京師西屬隴右，有七馬坊，置隴右三使領之。

translations.literal: West from the capital through Longyou there were seven horse compounds, placed under three Longyou commissioners to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: West from the capital through Longyou stood seven horse compounds, overseen by three Longyou commissioners.

sentences.zh: 又有沙苑、樓煩、天馬監。

translations.literal: There were also the Shayuan, Loufan, and Heavenly Horse supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Shayuan, Loufan, and Heavenly Horse supervisors.

sentences.zh: 沙苑監掌畜隴右諸牧牛羊，給宴祭及尙食所用，毎歳與典牧署供焉。

translations.literal: The Shayuan supervisor held charge of raising cattle and sheep from the Longyou pastures, supplying banquets, sacrifices, and the Imperial Food Service, and each year supplied the Imperial Herds Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Shayuan supervisor raised cattle and sheep from the Longyou pastures for banquets, sacrifices, and the Imperial Food Service, and each year supplied the Imperial Herds Office as well.

sentences.zh: 自監以下，品數如下牧監。

translations.literal: From supervisor down, ranks and numbers matched lower pasture supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: From supervisor down, ranks and staff matched lower pasture supervisors.

sentences.zh: 至開元二十三年，廢監。
