translations.literal: By the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan the supervisors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 the supervisors were abolished.

sentences.zh: 東宮九牧監東宮九牧監丞二人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace Nine Pastures supervisor had two assistants, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace Nine Pastures Office had two assistants, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 録事一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: one record clerk, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌牧養馬牛，以供皇太子之用。

translations.literal: They held charge of pasturing and raising horses and cattle to supply the crown prince's needs.
translations.idiomatic: They pastured and raised horses and cattle for the crown prince's use.

sentences.zh: 有録事史各一人，府三人，史六人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk and one scribe, three clerks, and six scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, one scribe, three clerks, and six scribes.

sentences.zh: 初，監有監、副監、丞、主簿、録事各一人，府二人，史四人，典事四人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: Initially each supervisor had one supervisor, deputy supervisor, assistant, registrar, and record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, four setup officers, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Originally each pasture had one director, deputy director, assistant, registrar, and record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, four setup officers, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 自監以下，品同下牧監。

translations.literal: From supervisor down, ranks matched lower pasture supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: From director down, ranks matched lower pasture supervisors.

sentences.zh: 又有馬牧使，有丞以下官。

translations.literal: There was also a horse-pasture commissioner, with assistants and subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a horse-pasture commissioner with assistants and other subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 大理寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review had one director, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review had one director, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從五品下。

translations.literal: two vice directors, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice directors, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌折獄、詳刑。

translations.literal: They held charge of deciding cases and reviewing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated cases and reviewed punishments.

sentences.zh: 凡罪抵流、死，皆上刑部，覆於中書、門下。

translations.literal: All crimes warranting exile or death were submitted to the Ministry of Justice and reviewed by the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: All crimes calling for exile or death went to the Ministry of Justice and were reviewed by the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 繫者五日一慮。

translations.literal: Prisoners were reviewed every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were reviewed every five days.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改曰詳刑寺；

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it was renamed the Court of Detailed Punishments;
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of Detailed Punishments;

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年，改曰司刑寺；

translations.literal: in Empress Wu's first year of Guangzhai it was renamed the Court of Punishment Administration;
translations.idiomatic: in Empress Wu's Guangzhai 1 it became the Court of Punishment Administration;

sentences.zh: 中宗時廢獄丞，有府二十八人，史五十六人，司直史十二人，評事史二十四人，獄史六人，亭長四人，掌固十八人，問事百人。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhongzong the prison assistant was abolished; there were twenty-eight clerks, fifty-six scribes, twelve scribes for investigating censors, twenty-four scribes for reviewing officials, six prison scribes, four station chiefs, eighteen compound guards, and one hundred inquiry officers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong the prison assistant was abolished. Staff included twenty-eight clerks, fifty-six scribes, twelve scribes for investigating censors, twenty-four for reviewing officials, six prison scribes, four station chiefs, eighteen compound guards, and one hundred inquiry officers.

sentences.zh: 正二人，從五品下。

translations.literal: There were two directors of review, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two directors of review, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌議獄，正科條。

translations.literal: They held charge of deliberating cases and correcting statutory articles.
translations.idiomatic: They deliberated on cases and corrected statutory provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡丞斷罪不當，則以法正之。

translations.literal: Whenever an assistant's judgment of guilt was improper, they corrected it according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an assistant misjudged a case, they corrected it under the law.

sentences.zh: 五品以上論者，莅決。

translations.literal: For defendants of fifth rank and above under discussion, they presided at the decision.
translations.idiomatic: They presided over trials of defendants of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 巡幸，則留總持寺事。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses they remained to handle affairs of Zongchi Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses they stayed behind to manage Zongchi Temple affairs.

sentences.zh: 丞六人，從六品上。

translations.literal: There were six assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Six assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌分判寺事，正刑之輕重。

translations.literal: They held charge of dividing and deciding court affairs and correcting the severity of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: They divided court business among themselves and adjusted the severity of punishments.

sentences.zh: 徒以上囚，則呼與家屬告罪，問其服否。

translations.literal: For prisoners sentenced to penal servitude or above, they summoned family members to announce the crime and asked whether they accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: For prisoners sentenced to penal servitude or worse, they summoned the family to announce the verdict and asked whether the prisoner accepted it.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: There were two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌印，省署鈔目，句檢稽失。

translations.literal: They held the seal, reviewed office copies and registers, and checked and audited errors.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the seal, reviewed office registers, and audited for errors.

sentences.zh: 凡官吏抵罪及雪免，皆立簿。

translations.literal: All officials who incurred guilt and those cleared of it were entered in registers.
translations.idiomatic: All officials convicted of offenses and those exonerated were recorded in registers.

sentences.zh: 私罪贖銅一斤，公罪二斤，皆爲一負；

translations.literal: One jin of copper redeemed for a private offense and two jin for a public offense each counted as one demerit;
translations.idiomatic: One jin of copper redeemed a private offense and two jin a public offense; each counted as one demerit;

sentences.zh: 十負爲一殿。

translations.literal: ten demerits made one major demerit.
translations.idiomatic: ten demerits made one major demerit.

sentences.zh: 毎歳，吏部、兵部牒覆選人殿負，録報焉。

translations.literal: Each year the Ministries of Civil Appointments and War sent documents reviewing candidates' major demerits and demerits, which were recorded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Ministries of Civil Appointments and War sent reviews of candidates' demerits, which were recorded and filed.

sentences.zh: 獄丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: There were two prison assistants, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two prison assistants, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌率獄史，知囚徒。

translations.literal: They led prison scribes and kept track of prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: They led prison scribes and oversaw prisoners.

sentences.zh: 貴賤、男女異獄。

translations.literal: Noble and common, male and female, had separate prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners, men and women, were held in separate prisons.

sentences.zh: 五品以上月一沐，暑則置漿。

translations.literal: Those of fifth rank and above bathed once a month; in summer fermented drink was provided.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners of fifth rank and above bathed once a month; in summer they were given fermented drink.

sentences.zh: 禁紙筆、金刃、錢物、杵梃入者。

translations.literal: Paper, brushes, metal blades, money, goods, pestles, and clubs were forbidden entry.
translations.idiomatic: Paper, brushes, blades, money, goods, pestles, and clubs were barred from entry.

sentences.zh: 囚病，給醫藥，重者脱械鎖，家人入侍。

translations.literal: When prisoners fell ill, medicine was supplied; serious cases had fetters removed and family members admitted to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Sick prisoners received medicine; in serious cases fetters were removed and family members were allowed in to attend them.

sentences.zh: 司直六人，從六品上；

translations.literal: There were six investigating censors, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Six investigating censors, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 評事八人，從八品下。

translations.literal: eight reviewing officials, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and eight reviewing officials, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌出使推按。

translations.literal: They held charge of going on mission to investigate and examine.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent on missions to investigate and examine cases.

sentences.zh: 凡承制推訊長吏，當停務禁錮者，請魚書以往。

translations.literal: Whenever by imperial order they interrogated senior officials who should be suspended from duty and placed under detention, they requested fish tally documents before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to interrogate senior officials who were to be suspended and detained, they obtained fish tally credentials before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: There were two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: There were two record clerks.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of State Ceremonial had one director, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of State Ceremonial had one director, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上；

translations.literal: two vice directors, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two vice directors, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌賓客及凶儀之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of guests and matters of mourning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: They managed foreign guests and mourning ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 領典客、司儀二署。

translations.literal: They oversaw the two offices of Guests and Ceremonial Order.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw the Offices of Guests and Ceremonial Order.

sentences.zh: 凡四夷君長，以蕃望髙下爲簿，朝見辨其等位，第三等居武官三品之下，第四等居五品之下，第五等居六品之下，有官者居本班。

translations.literal: For all foreign chieftains, registers were kept by barbarian prestige high and low; at court audiences their ranks were distinguished—the third rank below military officials of third rank, the fourth below fifth rank, the fifth below sixth rank; those with offices stood in their own ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign chieftains were listed by tribal prestige; at audiences their ranks were fixed—the third below military third rank, the fourth below fifth, the fifth below sixth; those with official titles took their normal places.

sentences.zh: 御史察食料。

translations.literal: Censors inspected food provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Censors inspected their food rations.

sentences.zh: 二王後、夷狄君長襲官爵者，辨嫡庶。

translations.literal: For heirs of the two overthrown dynasties and foreign chieftains inheriting offices and titles, legitimate and secondary sons were distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: For heirs of the two former dynasties and foreign chieftains inheriting rank, legitimate and secondary succession was determined.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃封命，則受冊而往。

translations.literal: For investitures of various barbarians, they received the patent and went.
translations.idiomatic: For foreign investitures they received the patent and traveled to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 海外諸蕃朝賀進貢使有下從，留其半於境；

translations.literal: Envoys from overseas barbarians coming to congratulate, pay tribute, or present gifts had subordinate attendants; half were left at the border;
translations.idiomatic: Overseas envoys coming to congratulate or offer tribute brought attendants; half were left at the border;

sentences.zh: 繇海路朝者，廣州擇首領一人、左右二人入朝；

translations.literal: those coming by sea route had Guangzhou select one chieftain and two attendants to enter court;
translations.idiomatic: those arriving by sea had Guangzhou choose one chieftain and two attendants to proceed to court;

sentences.zh: 所獻之物，先上其數於鴻臚。

translations.literal: items presented were first reported in number to the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: presented goods were first reported in quantity to the court.

sentences.zh: 凡客還，鴻臚籍衣齎賜物多少以報主客，給過所。

translations.literal: When guests returned, the Court of State Ceremonial registered how much clothing and bestowed goods they carried to report to the Office of Guests, and issued travel passes.
translations.idiomatic: When guests departed, the court recorded their clothing and gifts to report to the Office of Guests and issued travel passes.

sentences.zh: 蕃客奏事，具至日月及所奏之宜，方別爲狀，月一奏，爲簿，以副藏鴻臚。

translations.literal: When barbarian guests memorialized affairs, they listed arrival dates and the substance of what was memorialized, then made separate petitions; once a month they memorialized, made registers, and copies were stored at the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign guests presented matters, they recorded arrival dates and the substance of each petition; monthly reports were compiled into registers, with copies kept at the court.

sentences.zh: 獻馬，則殿中、太僕寺涖閲，良者入殿中，駑病入太僕。

translations.literal: When horses were presented, the Palace Domestic Service and Court of the Imperial Stud jointly inspected them; fine ones entered the Palace Domestic Service, poor and sick ones the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Presented horses were jointly inspected by the Palace Domestic Service and the Court of the Imperial Stud; fine horses went to the palace, poor or sick ones to the stud.

sentences.zh: 獻藥者，鴻臚寺驗覆，少府監定價之髙下。

translations.literal: For presented medicines, the Court of State Ceremonial verified and reviewed them, and the Imperial Workshop Directorate set prices high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Presented medicines were verified by the Court of State Ceremonial and priced by the Imperial Workshop Directorate.

sentences.zh: 鷹、鶻、狗、豹無估，則鴻臚定所報輕重。

translations.literal: Hawks, falcons, dogs, and leopards had no fixed valuation, so the Court of State Ceremonial determined the reported weight and value.
translations.idiomatic: Hawks, falcons, dogs, and leopards had no fixed price; the court determined their reported value.

sentences.zh: 凡獻物，皆客執以見，駝馬則陳于朝堂，不足進者州縣留之。

translations.literal: All presented goods were carried in by the guest to be seen; camels and horses were displayed in the court hall; what was unfit for presentation was retained by prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Guests carried presented goods in person; camels and horses were displayed in the court hall; items unfit for presentation were kept by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇太子爲五服親及大臣發哀臨弔，則卿贊相。

translations.literal: When the emperor or crown prince expressed mourning and attended condolences for relatives within five degrees of mourning or great ministers, the director assisted and directed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor or crown prince mourned relatives within five degrees of kinship or great ministers, the director guided the rites.

sentences.zh: 大臣一品葬，以卿護；

translations.literal: For funerals of first-rank ministers, the director escorted;
translations.idiomatic: First-rank ministers' funerals were escorted by the director;

sentences.zh: 二品，以少卿；

translations.literal: second rank, by the vice director;
translations.idiomatic: second rank, by the vice director;

sentences.zh: 三品，以丞。

translations.literal: third rank, by the assistant.
translations.idiomatic: third rank, by the assistant.

sentences.zh: 皆司儀示以禮制。

translations.literal: In all cases the Office of Ceremonial Order showed the ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Ceremonial Order instructed them in the ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從七品上。

translations.literal: There was one registrar, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: There were two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and two record clerks.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改鴻臚寺曰同文寺，武后光宅元年，改曰司賓寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Court of State Ceremonial was renamed the Court of Shared Script; in Empress Wu's first year of Guangzhai it was renamed the Court of Guest Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of Shared Script; in Empress Wu's Guangzhai 1 it became the Court of Guest Administration.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十人，亭長四人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were five clerks, ten scribes, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included five clerks, ten scribes, four station chiefs, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 典客署典客署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Guests had one director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Guests had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞三人，從八品下。

translations.literal: three assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and three assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌二王後介公、酅公之版籍及四夷歸化在藩者，朝貢、宴享、送迎皆預焉。

translations.literal: They held charge of registers of the heirs of the two dynasties, the Lord of Jie, and the Lord of Xi, and of barbarians who had submitted and remained in their domains; they took part in tribute audiences, banquets, and send-offs and welcomes.
translations.idiomatic: They kept registers of the two former dynasties' heirs, the Lords of Jie and Xi, and submitted foreigners in their domains, and handled tribute audiences, banquets, and receptions.

sentences.zh: 酋渠首領朝見者，給稟食；

translations.literal: Tribal chiefs and leaders coming to audience were given grain rations;
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs coming to audience received grain rations;

sentences.zh: 病，則遣醫給湯藥；

translations.literal: if ill, physicians were sent with decoctions and medicines;
translations.idiomatic: if they fell ill, physicians were sent with medicines;

sentences.zh: 喪，則給以所須；

translations.literal: if they died, what was needed was supplied;
translations.idiomatic: if they died, funeral needs were supplied;

sentences.zh: 還蕃賜物，則佐其受領，教拜謝之節。

translations.literal: when returning to their domains with bestowed goods, they assisted in receiving them and taught the etiquette of bowing in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: when they returned home with imperial gifts, they helped them receive the goods and taught the proper forms of thanks.

sentences.zh: 有典客十三人，府四人，史八人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: There were thirteen guest officers, four clerks, eight scribes, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included thirteen guest officers, four clerks, eight scribes, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 掌客十五人，正九品上。

translations.literal: There were fifteen guest stewards, regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen guest stewards, of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌送迎蕃客，顓莅舘舍。

translations.literal: They held charge of escorting and welcoming barbarian guests and exclusively managed hostel quarters.
translations.idiomatic: They received and escorted foreign guests and managed the hostels.

sentences.zh: 司儀署司儀署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Ceremonial Order had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Ceremonial Order had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌凶禮喪葬之具。

translations.literal: They held charge of equipment for mourning rites and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied equipment for mourning rites and funerals.

sentences.zh: 京官職事三品以上、散官二品以上祖父母、父母喪，職事散官五品以上、都督、刺史卒于京師，及五品死王事者，將葬，祭以少牢，率齋郎執俎豆以往。

translations.literal: For capital officials with substantive posts of third rank and above or honorary posts of second rank and above mourning grandparents or parents, and for those with substantive or honorary posts of fifth rank and above, regional commanders, or prefects who died in the capital, and fifth-rank officials who died in the ruler's service—before burial, they sacrificed with a minor tai-lao victim, leading fast-officers carrying stands and dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Before burial they offered a minor tai-lao sacrifice for capital officials of third substantive rank or second honorary rank mourning parents or grandparents; for fifth rank and above, regional commanders, or prefects who died in the capital, and fifth-rank officials who died in state service—leading fast-officers bearing ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 三品以上贈以束帛，黑一、纁二，一品加乘馬；

translations.literal: Third rank and above were bestowed bundled silks, one black and two crimson; first rank added a riding horse;
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above received bundled silks—one black and two crimson; first rank also received a riding horse;

sentences.zh: 旣引，遣使贈於郭門之外，皆有束帛，一品加璧。

translations.literal: after the coffin procession, envoys were sent to bestow gifts outside the outer city gate; all received bundled silks, first rank added a jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: after the procession, envoys presented gifts outside the city gate—all received bundled silks, and first rank also a jade disk.

sentences.zh: 五品以上葬，給營墓夫。

translations.literal: For burials of fifth rank and above, grave-building laborers were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above received laborers to prepare the tomb.

sentences.zh: 有司儀六人，府二人，史四人，掌設十八人，齋郎三十人，掌固四人，幕士六十人。

translations.literal: There were six ceremonial officers, two clerks, four scribes, eighteen setup officers, thirty fast-officers, four compound guards, and sixty tent laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included six ceremonial officers, two clerks, four scribes, eighteen setup officers, thirty fast-officers, four compound guards, and sixty tent laborers.

sentences.zh: 司農寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of the National Granary had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the National Granary had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上。

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌倉儲委積之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of granary storage and accumulated stores.
translations.idiomatic: They managed granary storage and stockpiles.

sentences.zh: 總上林、太倉、鉤盾、䆃官四署及諸倉、司竹、諸湯、宮苑、鹽池、諸屯等監。

translations.literal: They oversaw the four offices of the Imperial Park, Grand Granary, Hooked Shield, and Grain Winnowing, and the various granaries, Bamboo Office, hot-spring offices, palace parks, salt ponds, and agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw the Imperial Park, Grand Granary, Hooked Shield, and Grain Winnowing offices, together with the various granaries, bamboo farms, hot-spring stations, palace parks, salt ponds, and colony farms.

sentences.zh: 凡京都百司官吏祿稟、朝會、祭祀所須，皆供焉。

translations.literal: Whatever the hundred offices of the capital required for officials' salary grain, court assemblies, and sacrifices, they all supplied.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied whatever the capital's offices needed for official salaries, court assemblies, and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 藉田，則進耒耜。

translations.literal: For the ceremonial plowing field, they presented plows and clod-breakers.
translations.idiomatic: For the ceremonial plowing they presented plows and clod-breakers.

sentences.zh: 丞六人，從六品上。

translations.literal: six assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Six assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 總判寺事。

translations.literal: They collectively adjudicated the affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly handled the court's business.

sentences.zh: 凡租及藳秸至京都者，閲而納焉。

translations.literal: All land tax and straw and stalks arriving at the capital were inspected and received.
translations.idiomatic: All land tax grain and fodder straw reaching the capital were inspected and received.

sentences.zh: 官戸奴婢有技能者配諸司，婦人入掖庭，以類相偶，行宮監牧及賜王公、公主皆取之。

translations.literal: Government-household slaves with skills were assigned to the various offices; women entered the Palace Women's Quarters and were paired by category; traveling-palace herds and flocks and gifts to princes, dukes, and princesses all drew on them.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled government slaves were assigned to offices; women went to the inner quarters and were matched by category; traveling-palace herds and gifts to princes, dukes, and princesses all drew on this pool.

sentences.zh: 凡孳生鷄彘，以戸奴婢課養。

translations.literal: For all breeding of chickens and swine, household slaves were levied to raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Household slaves were assigned to raise all breeding chickens and swine.

sentences.zh: 俘口則配輕使，始至給稟食。

translations.literal: Captives were assigned to light labor; on first arrival they were given grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Captives were assigned light labor and given grain rations on arrival.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上；

translations.literal: two chief clerks, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: two chief clerks, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: two record clerks.
translations.idiomatic: and two record clerks.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改司農寺曰司稼寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Court of the National Granary was renamed the Court of Grain Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of Grain Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 有府三十八人，史七十六人，計史三人，亭長九人，掌固七人。

translations.literal: There were thirty-eight clerks, seventy-six scribes, three accounting clerks, nine station chiefs, and seven compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included thirty-eight clerks, seventy-six scribes, three accounting clerks, nine station chiefs, and seven compound guards.

sentences.zh: 上林署上林署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of the Imperial Park had two directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Imperial Park had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and four assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌苑囿園池。

translations.literal: They held charge of parks, enclosures, gardens, and ponds.
translations.idiomatic: They managed parks, gardens, and ponds.

sentences.zh: 植果蔬，以供朝會、祭祀及尙食諸司常料。

translations.literal: They planted fruits and vegetables to supply court assemblies, sacrifices, and the regular provisions of the Imperial Catering and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: They raised fruits and vegetables for court assemblies, sacrifices, and the regular provisions of Imperial Catering and other offices.

sentences.zh: 季冬，藏冰千段，先立春三日納之冰井，以黑牡、秬黍祭司寒，仲春啓冰亦如之。

translations.literal: In late winter they stored a thousand segments of ice; three days before Start of Spring they deposited them in the ice well, sacrificing a black bull and black millet to the Cold Spirit; in mid-spring opening the ice followed the same rite.
translations.idiomatic: In late winter they stored a thousand blocks of ice; three days before Start of Spring they placed them in the ice well, offering a black bull and black millet to the Cold Spirit; mid-spring ice-opening followed the same ritual.

sentences.zh: 監事十人。

translations.literal: There were ten superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: Ten superintendents were on staff.

sentences.zh: 有府七人，史十四人，典事二十四人，掌固五人。

translations.literal: There were seven clerks, fourteen scribes, twenty-four stewards, and five compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seven clerks, fourteen scribes, twenty-four stewards, and five compound guards.

sentences.zh: 太倉署太倉署令三人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Office of the Grand Granary had three directors, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Grand Granary had three directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞五人，從八品下；

translations.literal: five assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: five assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 監事八人。

translations.literal: eight superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: and eight superintendents.

sentences.zh: 掌廩藏之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of granary storage.
translations.idiomatic: They managed granary storage.

sentences.zh: 有府十人，史二十人，典事二十四人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: There were ten clerks, twenty scribes, twenty-four stewards, and eight compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included ten clerks, twenty scribes, twenty-four stewards, and eight compound guards.

sentences.zh: 鉤盾署鉤盾署令二人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Office of Hooked Shield had two directors, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Hooked Shield had two directors, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，正九品上；

translations.literal: four assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: four assistants, of regular ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 監事十人。

translations.literal: ten superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: and ten superintendents.

sentences.zh: 掌供薪炭、鵝鴨、蒲藺、陂池藪澤之物，以給祭祀、朝會、饗燕賓客。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying firewood and charcoal, geese and ducks, rushes and sedge, and products of ponds, marshes, and wetlands, to furnish sacrifices, court assemblies, and banquets for guests.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied firewood and charcoal, poultry, rushes and sedge, and marsh and pond products for sacrifices, court assemblies, and guest banquets.

sentences.zh: 有府七人，史十四人，典事十九人，掌固五人。

translations.literal: There were seven clerks, fourteen scribes, nineteen stewards, and five compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seven clerks, fourteen scribes, nineteen stewards, and five compound guards.

sentences.zh: 䆃官署䆃官署令二人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Grain Winnowing had two directors, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Grain Winnowing had two directors, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，正九品上；

translations.literal: four assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: four assistants, of regular ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 監事十人。

translations.literal: ten superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: and ten superintendents.

sentences.zh: 掌䆃擇米麥。

translations.literal: They held charge of winnowing and selecting rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They winnowed and graded rice and wheat.

sentences.zh: 凡九穀，皆隨精粗差其耗損而供焉。

translations.literal: For all nine grains, they supplied according to fine and coarse grades and their respective wastage.
translations.idiomatic: All nine grains were supplied according to grade, with allowances for wastage by fineness.

sentences.zh: 有府八人，史十六人，典事二十四人，掌固五人。

translations.literal: There were eight clerks, sixteen scribes, twenty-four stewards, and five compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included eight clerks, sixteen scribes, twenty-four stewards, and five compound guards.

sentences.zh: 初有御細倉督、麴麪倉督，貞觀中省。

translations.literal: Initially there were superintendents of the Imperial Fine Granary and of the Yeast and Flour Granary; these were abolished in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: At first there were superintendents of the imperial fine-grain and yeast-and-flour granaries; both posts were abolished in the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 太原、永豐、龍門等倉太原、永豐、龍門等倉毎倉，監一人，正七品下；

translations.literal: The Taiyuan, Yongfeng, Longmen, and other granaries—each granary had one superintendent, regular seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan, Yongfeng, Longmen, and other granaries each had one superintendent, of regular seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從八品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌倉廩儲積。

translations.literal: They held charge of granary storage and accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: They managed granary storage and stockpiles.

sentences.zh: 凡出納帳籍，歳終上寺。

translations.literal: All receipt and disbursement ledgers were submitted to the court at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Receipt and disbursement ledgers were submitted to the court at year's end.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府三人，史六人，典事八人，掌固六人；

translations.literal: There were one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, eight stewards, and six compound guards;
translations.idiomatic: each had one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, eight stewards, and six compound guards;

sentences.zh: 龍門等倉，減府一人，史、典事、掌固各減二人。

translations.literal: At the Longmen and other granaries, one clerk was reduced, and scribes, stewards, and compound guards were each reduced by two.
translations.idiomatic: At Longmen and similar granaries staff was reduced by one clerk and two each among scribes, stewards, and compound guards.

sentences.zh: 司竹監司竹監一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: The Bamboo Office had one superintendent, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Bamboo Office had one superintendent, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監一人，正七品下；

translations.literal: one deputy superintendent, regular seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: one deputy superintendent, of regular seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌植竹、葦，供宮中百司簾篚之屬，歳以筍供尙食。

translations.literal: They held charge of planting bamboo and reeds to supply the hundred palace offices with curtains, baskets, and the like, and each year supplied bamboo shoots to Imperial Catering.
translations.idiomatic: They cultivated bamboo and reeds for palace curtains, baskets, and similar goods, and each year sent bamboo shoots to Imperial Catering.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府二人，史四人，典事三十人，掌固四人，葦園匠一百人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, thirty stewards, four compound guards, and one hundred reed-garden artisans.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, two clerks, four scribes, thirty stewards, four compound guards, and one hundred reed-garden artisans.

sentences.zh: 慶善、石門、温泉湯等監慶善、石門、温泉湯等監毎監，監一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: The Qingshan, Shimen, Wenquan, and other hot-spring offices—each office had one superintendent, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Qingshan, Shimen, Wenquan, and other hot-spring stations each had one superintendent, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正七品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌湯池、宮禁、防堰及偫粟芻、脩調度，以備供奉。

translations.literal: They held charge of hot pools, palace security, protective dikes, stored grain and fodder, and repair and supply arrangements to prepare for imperial service.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the baths, palace security, dikes, stored grain and fodder, and repairs and logistics for imperial visits.

sentences.zh: 王公以下湯舘，視貴賤爲差。

translations.literal: Bath lodges for princes, dukes, and below were graded according to noble and humble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bath lodges for princes, dukes, and lower ranks were allotted according to status.

sentences.zh: 凡近湯所潤瓜蔬，先時而熟者，以薦陵廟。

translations.literal: All melons and vegetables nourished near the springs that ripened early were offered to the imperial tombs and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Early-ripening melons and vegetables from the warm spring districts were sent to the tombs and temples.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each station had one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 京都諸宮苑總監京都諸宮苑總監監各一人，從五品下；

translations.literal: The general superintendents of the capital's palace parks—each had one superintendent, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The capital's palace-park general offices each had one superintendent, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監各一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: each one deputy superintendent, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each one deputy superintendent, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: each two assistants, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each two assistants, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿各二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: each two chief clerks, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: each two chief clerks, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌苑内宮舘、園池、禽魚、果木。

translations.literal: They held charge of palaces and lodges within the parks, gardens and ponds, birds and fish, and fruit trees.
translations.idiomatic: They managed palaces and lodges, gardens and ponds, birds and fish, and orchards within the parks.

sentences.zh: 凡官屬人畜出入，皆有籍。

translations.literal: All entry and exit of officials, retainers, people, and livestock was recorded in registers.
translations.idiomatic: All movement of staff, people, and livestock in and out was registered.

sentences.zh: 有録事各二人，府各八人，史各十六人，亭長各四人，掌固各六人，獸醫各五人。

translations.literal: Each had two record clerks, eight clerks, sixteen scribes, four station chiefs, six compound guards, and five veterinary physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had two record clerks, eight clerks, sixteen scribes, four station chiefs, six compound guards, and five veterinary physicians.

sentences.zh: 京都諸園苑監、苑四面監監各一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: The various garden-park superintendents of the capital and the four-side park superintendents—each had one superintendent, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The capital's garden-park offices and the four-side park offices each had one superintendent, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監各一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: each one deputy superintendent, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: each one deputy superintendent, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各二人，正八品下。

translations.literal: each two assistants, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: each two assistants, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌完葺苑面、宮舘、園池與種蒔、蕃養六畜之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of completing and repairing the park perimeter, palaces and lodges, gardens and ponds, planting and sowing, and breeding the six domestic animals.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained the park grounds, palaces, gardens, and ponds, and handled planting and the breeding of livestock.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，改靑城宮監曰東都苑北面監，明德宮監曰東都苑南面監，洛陽宮農圃監曰東都苑東面監，倉貨監曰東都苑西面監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing the Qingcheng Palace Superintendent was renamed Eastern Capital Park North-Side Superintendent; the Mingde Palace Superintendent was renamed Eastern Capital Park South-Side Superintendent; the Luoyang Palace Farm and Garden Superintendent was renamed Eastern Capital Park East-Side Superintendent; the Granary Goods Superintendent was renamed Eastern Capital Park West-Side Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 the Qingcheng Palace office became the Eastern Capital Park North-Side office; the Mingde Palace office became the South-Side office; the Luoyang Palace Farm and Garden office became the East-Side office; and the Granary Goods office became the West-Side office.

sentences.zh: 有録事各一人，府各三人，史各六人，典事各六人，掌固各六人。

translations.literal: Each had one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, six stewards, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one record clerk, three clerks, six scribes, six stewards, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 九成宮總監九成宮總監監一人，從五品下；

translations.literal: The Jiucheng Palace general superintendent had one superintendent, subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiucheng Palace general office had one superintendent, of subordinate fifth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: one deputy superintendent, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: one deputy superintendent, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: one assistant, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: one chief clerk, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one chief clerk, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌脩完宮苑，供進鍊餌之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of repairing and completing the palace park and supplying refined cakes for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained the palace park and supplied refined cakes for imperial presentation.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府三人，自監以下，品同宮苑。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk and three clerks; from the superintendent down, ranks were the same as for palace parks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk and three clerks; from the superintendent down, ranks matched those of the palace-park offices.

sentences.zh: 武德初，改隋仁壽宮監曰九成宮監。

translations.literal: Early in Wude the Sui Renshou Palace Superintendent was renamed Jiucheng Palace Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude the Sui Renshou Palace office was renamed the Jiucheng Palace office.

sentences.zh: 諸鹽池監諸鹽池鹽監一人，正七品下，掌鹽功簿帳。

translations.literal: The various salt-pond superintendents—each salt pond had one salt superintendent, regular seventh rank, lower grade, who held charge of salt-production ledgers and accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Each salt pond had one superintendent, of regular seventh rank, lower grade, who kept the salt-production accounts.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，史二人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk and two scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one record clerk and two scribes.

sentences.zh: 諸屯監諸屯監一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The various colony superintendents—each colony had one superintendent, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each agricultural colony had one superintendent, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌營種屯田，句會功課及畜産簿帳，以水旱蝝蝗定課。

translations.literal: They held charge of managing and planting colony fields, tabulating labor quotas and livestock accounts, and fixing levies according to flood, drought, locusts, and grasshoppers.
translations.idiomatic: They managed colony farming, reconciled labor quotas and livestock accounts, and set levies according to flood, drought, and pest damage.

sentences.zh: 屯主勸率營農，督斂地課。

translations.literal: Colony chiefs urged and led farming operations and supervised collection of land levies.
translations.idiomatic: Colony chiefs encouraged farming and supervised collection of land taxes.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史二人，典事二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, two stewards, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony had one record clerk, one clerk, two scribes, two stewards, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 毎屯主一人，屯副一人，主簿一人，録事一人，府三人，史五人。

translations.literal: Each colony had one colony chief, one deputy colony chief, one chief clerk, one record clerk, three clerks, and five scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony had one chief, one deputy chief, one chief clerk, one record clerk, three clerks, and five scribes.

sentences.zh: 太府寺卿一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Court of the Grand Treasury had one minister, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Grand Treasury had one minister, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，從四品上。

translations.literal: two vice ministers, subordinate fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice ministers, of subordinate fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌財貨、廩藏、貿易，總京都四市、左右藏、常平七署。

translations.literal: They held charge of wealth and goods, granary storage, and trade, and oversaw the capital's four markets, Left and Right Treasuries, and the seven offices of the Ever-Normal.
translations.idiomatic: They managed wealth, stores, and trade, and oversaw the capital's four markets, the Left and Right Treasuries, and the seven Ever-Normal offices.

sentences.zh: 凡四方貢賦、百官俸秩，謹其出納。

translations.literal: For all tribute and levies from the four directions and the salary emoluments of the hundred officials, they carefully handled receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: They carefully handled receipts and disbursements for tribute from all quarters and officials' salaries.

sentences.zh: 賦物任土所出，定精粗之差，祭祀幣帛皆供焉。

translations.literal: Tribute goods followed what each region produced; fine and coarse grades were fixed; all ritual silks and fabrics for sacrifices were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute followed local products, with grades fixed by quality, and they supplied all ritual silks for sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改太府寺曰外府寺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Court of the Grand Treasury was renamed the Court of the Outer Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it was renamed the Court of the Outer Treasury.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年，改曰司府寺。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's first year of Guangzhai it was renamed the Court of Treasury Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's Guangzhai 1 it became the Court of Treasury Administration.

sentences.zh: 中宗卽位，復曰太府寺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, it was restored to the Court of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, the name Court of the Grand Treasury was restored.

sentences.zh: 有府二十五人，史五十人，計史四人，亭長七人，掌固七人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-five clerks, fifty scribes, four accounting clerks, seven station chiefs, and seven compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included twenty-five clerks, fifty scribes, four accounting clerks, seven station chiefs, and seven compound guards.

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從六品上。

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Four assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌判寺事。

translations.literal: They adjudicated the affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: They handled the court's business.

sentences.zh: 凡元日、冬至以方物陳于庭者，受而進之。

translations.literal: For New Year's Day and Winter Solstice, whatever regional products were displayed in the courtyard, they received and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the Winter Solstice they received regional tribute displayed in the courtyard and presented it onward.

sentences.zh: 會賜及別敕六品以下賜者，給於朝堂。

translations.literal: Assembly grants and special-edict gifts to sixth rank and below were distributed in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Assembly gifts and special-edict grants to sixth rank and below were distributed in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 以一人主左、右藏署帳，凡在署爲簿，在寺爲帳，三月一報金部。

translations.literal: One person was put in charge of the accounts of the Left and Right Treasury offices; what was in the offices was called a register, in the court an account, and every three months a report was made to the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: One officer managed the Left and Right Treasury accounts—office records were called registers, court records accounts—and reported quarterly to the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: two chief clerks, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌印，省鈔目，句檢稽失，平權衡度量，歳以八月印署，然後用之。

translations.literal: They held the seal, reviewed draft ledgers, checked and audited errors, and balanced weights and measures; each year in the eighth month they stamped and signed them, and only then were they used.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the seal, reviewed draft ledgers, audited errors, and calibrated weights and measures; each year in the eighth month they stamped and certified them before use.

sentences.zh: 録事二人。

translations.literal: two recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Two recorders.

sentences.zh: 兩京諸市署兩京諸市署令一人，從六品上；

translations.literal: The Market Offices of the Two Capitals had one director of the Market Offices of the Two Capitals, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Market Offices of the Two Capitals had one director, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正八品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two assistants, of regular eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌財貨交易、度量器物，辨其眞偽輕重。

translations.literal: They held charge of the exchange of wealth and goods and of measures and utensils, distinguishing their genuineness and falsity, lightness and heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised trade in goods and standards of measure, distinguishing genuine from counterfeit and correct weight.

sentences.zh: 市肆皆建標築土爲候，禁榷固及參市自殖者。

translations.literal: All market stalls erected markers and mounded earth as signposts; monopolistic hoarding and those who joined the market to sell their own produce were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Every stall had to post markers and a raised earth sign; hoarding for monopoly and private selling in the market were banned.

sentences.zh: 凡市，日中撃鼓三百以會衆，日入前七刻，撃鉦三百而散。

translations.literal: For all markets, at midday three hundred drumbeats gathered the crowd; seven quarters before sunset, three hundred gong-strokes dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: In every market, three hundred drumbeats at noon opened trade, and three hundred strokes on the gong seven quarters before sunset closed it.

sentences.zh: 有果毅巡迣。

translations.literal: There were guoyi patrols.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyi guards patrolled the markets.

sentences.zh: 平貨物爲三等之直，十日爲簿。

translations.literal: Goods were priced in three grades of value, with a register made every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Goods were rated in three price grades, recorded in a ledger every ten days.

sentences.zh: 車駕行幸，則立市于頓側互市，有衞士五十人，以察非常。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled on tour, a market was set up at the halt for mutual trade; fifty guards were posted to watch for irregularities.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, a market was opened at each halt for exchange, with fifty guards to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府三人，史七人，典事三人，掌固一人。

translations.literal: There were one recorder, three clerks, seven scribes, three registry officers, and one compound guard.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one recorder, three clerks, seven scribes, three registry officers, and one compound guard.

sentences.zh: 左藏署左藏署令三人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Left Treasury Office had three directors of the Left Treasury Office, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Treasury Office had three directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞五人，從八品下；

translations.literal: five assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Five assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 監事八人。

translations.literal: eight supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Eight supervisors.

sentences.zh: 掌錢帛、雜綵。

translations.literal: They held charge of coin, silk, and miscellaneous colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: They managed coin, silk, and miscellaneous fabrics.

sentences.zh: 天下賦調，卿及御史監閲。

translations.literal: For the empire's taxes and levies, the minister and censors supervised inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The minister and censors supervised the empire's tax and levy collections.

sentences.zh: 有府九人，史十八人，典事十二人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: There were nine clerks, eighteen scribes, twelve registry officers, and eight compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included nine clerks, eighteen scribes, twelve registry officers, and eight compound guards.

sentences.zh: 右藏署右藏署令二人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Right Treasury Office had two directors of the Right Treasury Office, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Treasury Office had two directors, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞三人，正九品上；

translations.literal: three assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Three assistants, of regular ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 監事四人。

translations.literal: four supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Four supervisors.

sentences.zh: 掌金玉、珠寶、銅鐵、骨角、齒毛、綵畫。

translations.literal: They held charge of gold and jade, pearls and gems, copper and iron, bone and horn, ivory and fur, and painted silks.
translations.idiomatic: They managed gold and jade, pearls and gems, copper and iron, bone and horn, ivory and fur, and painted silks.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十二人，典事七人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: There were five clerks, twelve scribes, seven registry officers, and ten compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included five clerks, twelve scribes, seven registry officers, and ten compound guards.

sentences.zh: 常平署常平署令一人，從七品上；

translations.literal: The Ever-Normal Office had one director of the Ever-Normal Office, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal Office had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從八品下；

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 監事五人。

translations.literal: five supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Five supervisors.

sentences.zh: 掌平糴、倉儲、出納。

translations.literal: They held charge of grain price stabilization, granary storage, and receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: They managed grain price stabilization, granary storage, and receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 有府四人，史八人，典事五人，掌固六人。

translations.literal: There were four clerks, eight scribes, five registry officers, and six compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included four clerks, eight scribes, five registry officers, and six compound guards.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，置署。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing the office was established.
translations.idiomatic: The office was established in Xianqing 3.

sentences.zh: 武后時，東都亦置署。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time an office was also established in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu an office was also set up in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 國子監祭酒一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Imperial University had one chancellor, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Imperial University had one chancellor, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 司業二人，從四品下。

translations.literal: two vice chancellors, subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two vice chancellors, of subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌儒學訓導之政，總國子、太學、廣文、四門、律、書、算凡七學。

translations.literal: They held charge of the administration of Confucian learning and instruction, and oversaw in all seven schools: the Imperial University, the Grand Academy, the Broad Learning Hall, the Four Gates Hall, Law, Calligraphy, and Mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: They directed Confucian instruction and oversaw seven schools: the Imperial University, Grand Academy, Broad Learning Hall, Four Gates Hall, Law, Calligraphy, and Mathematics.

sentences.zh: 天子視學，皇太子齒冑，則講義。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven inspected the schools, or the Crown Prince donned cap and armor, they lectured on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor inspected the schools, or the crown prince donned cap and armor, they delivered lectures on the classics.

sentences.zh: 釋奠，執經論議，奏京文武七品以上觀禮。

translations.literal: At the libation sacrifice they held the classics and debated them, and reported that civil and military officials of seventh rank and above in the capital should observe the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the libation sacrifice they expounded the classics in debate and had civil and military officials of seventh rank and above in the capital attend.

sentences.zh: 凡授經，以周易、尙書、周禮、儀禮、禮記、毛詩、春秋左氏傳、公羊傳、穀梁傳各爲一經，兼習孝經、論語、老子，歳終，考學官訓導多少爲殿最。

translations.literal: For all instruction in the classics, the Changes, Documents, Rites of Zhou, Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary each formed one classic; the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, and Laozi were studied concurrently; at year's end the instructional officers were examined on how much they had taught and ranked best to worst.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction was divided among nine classics—the Changes, Documents, Rites of Zhou, Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, and the Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang commentaries—along with the Filial Piety Classic, Analects, and Laozi; at year's end the teaching staff were graded on their instruction.

sentences.zh: 丞一人，從六品下，掌判監事。

translations.literal: one assistant, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade, who adjudicated the directorate's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade, who handled the directorate's business.

sentences.zh: 毎歳，七學生業成，與司業、祭酒莅試，登第者上於禮部。

translations.literal: Each year, when students of the seven schools completed their course, they were examined on the spot with the vice chancellors and chancellor; those who passed were forwarded to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Each year, when students of the seven schools finished their course, the vice chancellors and chancellor examined them; those who passed were sent to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從七品下。

translations.literal: one chief clerk, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌印，句督監事。

translations.literal: They held the seal and checked and supervised the directorate's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the seal and supervised the directorate's business.

sentences.zh: 七學生不率教者，舉而免之。

translations.literal: Students of the seven schools who did not follow instruction were reported and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the seven schools who would not obey instruction were reported and expelled.

sentences.zh: 録事一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: one recorder, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: One recorder, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以國子監曰國子學，隸太常寺，貞觀二年復曰監。

translations.literal: Early in Wude the Directorate of Imperial University was called the Imperial University School and was subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in the second year of Zhenguan it was again called a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude the directorate was renamed the Imperial University School and placed under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in Zhenguan 2 it became a directorate again.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改國子監曰司成舘，祭酒曰大司成，司業曰少司成。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Directorate of Imperial University was renamed the Hall of Completion, the chancellor was called Grand Completer, and the vice chancellor Junior Completer.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the directorate became the Hall of Completion, the chancellor the Grand Completer, and the vice chancellor the Junior Completer.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年復曰監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng it was again called a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 it was again called a directorate.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年，改國子監曰成均監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong the Directorate of Imperial University was renamed the Directorate of the Balanced Mean.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 1 the Directorate of Imperial University became the Directorate of the Balanced Mean.

sentences.zh: 有府七人，史十三人，亭長六人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: There were seven clerks, thirteen scribes, six station chiefs, and eight compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seven clerks, thirteen scribes, six station chiefs, and eight compound guards.

sentences.zh: 國子學國子學博士五人，正五品上。

translations.literal: The Imperial University School had five erudites of the Imperial University School, regular fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University School had five erudites, of regular fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教三品以上及國公子孫、從二品以上曾孫爲生者。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of third rank and above, sons and grandsons of the imperial clan, and great-grandsons of officials of subordinate second rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of third rank and above, imperial clansmen, and great-grandsons of officials of subordinate second rank and above.

sentences.zh: 五分其經以爲業：周禮、儀禮、禮記、毛詩、春秋左氏傳各六十人，暇則習隸書、國語、説文、字林、三倉、爾雅。

translations.literal: The classics were divided into five for their curriculum: Rites of Zhou, Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, and Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn, sixty students each; in leisure time they studied clerical script, the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum was divided among five classics—Rites of Zhou, Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, and the Zuo Commentary—with sixty students each; in spare time they studied clerical script, the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.

sentences.zh: 毎歳通兩經。

translations.literal: Each year they had to master two classics.
translations.idiomatic: Each year students had to pass two classics.

sentences.zh: 求仕者，上於監，秀才、進士亦如之。

translations.literal: Those seeking office were forwarded to the directorate; cultivated talents and presented scholars were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Those seeking office were referred to the directorate, as were cultivated talents and presented scholars.

sentences.zh: 學生以長幼爲序，習正業之外，教吉、凶二禮，公私有事則相儀。

translations.literal: Students were ordered by age; apart from their main studies they were taught the two rites of auspicious and inauspicious occasions, and for public or private affairs they served as ritual attendants for one another.
translations.idiomatic: Students were ranked by age; beyond their main coursework they learned auspicious and mourning rites and assisted one another at public and private ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改博士曰宣業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo erudites were renamed Proclaimers of Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 erudites were renamed Proclaimers of Achievement.

sentences.zh: 有大成十人，學生八十人，典學四人，廟幹二人，掌固四人，東都學生十五人。

translations.literal: There were ten senior graduates, eighty students, four school registrars, two temple stewards, four compound guards, and fifteen students in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included ten senior graduates, eighty students, four school registrars, two temple stewards, four compound guards, and fifteen students in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 助教五人，從六品上。

translations.literal: five instructors, subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Five instructors, of subordinate sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌佐博士分經教授。

translations.literal: They held charge of assisting the erudites in dividing the classics for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the erudites in teaching the classics by division.

sentences.zh: 直講四人，掌佐博士、助教以經術講授。

translations.literal: four lecturers, who held charge of assisting erudites and instructors in lecturing on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Four lecturers assisted erudites and instructors in expounding the classics.

sentences.zh: 五經博士各二人，正五品上。

translations.literal: two erudites for each of the Five Classics, regular fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two erudites for each of the Five Classics, of regular fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌以其經之學教國子。

translations.literal: They held charge of teaching the imperial university students with the learning of their respective classic.
translations.idiomatic: Each taught imperial university students in his own classic.

sentences.zh: 周易、尙書、毛詩、左氏春秋、禮記爲五經，論語、孝經、爾雅不立學官，附中經而已。

translations.literal: The Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Zuo Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites were the Five Classics; the Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, and Erya had no separate instructional posts and were attached to the central classics only.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Classics were the Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Zuo Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites; the Analects, Filial Piety Classic, and Erya had no separate posts and were taught as adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 太學太學博士六人，正六品上；

translations.literal: The Grand Academy had six erudites of the Grand Academy, regular sixth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Academy had six erudites, of regular sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 助教六人，從七品上。

translations.literal: six instructors, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Six instructors, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教五品以上及郡縣公子孫、從三品曾孫爲生者，五分其經以爲業，毎經百人。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of fifth rank and above, sons and grandsons of prefectural and county nobles, and great-grandsons of officials of subordinate third rank and above; the classics were divided into five for their curriculum, one hundred students per classic.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of fifth rank and above, sons and grandsons of prefectural and county nobles, and great-grandsons of officials of subordinate third rank and above, with five classics and one hundred students each.

sentences.zh: 有學生七十人，典學四人，掌固六人，東都學生十五人。

translations.literal: There were seventy students, four school registrars, six compound guards, and fifteen students in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventy students, four school registrars, six compound guards, and fifteen students in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 廣文舘廣文舘博士四人，助教二人。

translations.literal: The Broad Learning Hall had four erudites of the Broad Learning Hall and two instructors.
translations.idiomatic: The Broad Learning Hall had four erudites and two instructors.

sentences.zh: 掌領國子學生業進士者。

translations.literal: They held charge of overseeing imperial university students preparing for the presented-scholar examination.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised imperial university students studying for the presented-scholar examination.

sentences.zh: 有學生六十人，東都十人。

translations.literal: There were sixty students and ten in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixty students and ten in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，置廣文舘，有知進士助教，後罷知進士之名。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao the Broad Learning Hall was established, with an instructor who knew the presented-scholar curriculum; later the title of presented-scholar specialist was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 9 the Broad Learning Hall was established with an instructor specializing in the presented-scholar curriculum; later that title was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四門舘四門舘博士六人，正七品上；

translations.literal: The Four Gates Hall had six erudites of the Four Gates Hall, regular seventh rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Four Gates Hall had six erudites, of regular seventh rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 助教六人，從八品上；

translations.literal: six instructors, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Six instructors, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 直講四人。

translations.literal: four lecturers.
translations.idiomatic: Four lecturers.

sentences.zh: 掌教七品以上、侯伯子男子爲生及庶人子爲俊士生者。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of seventh rank and above, sons of marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons, and commoners' sons enrolled as talented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of seventh rank and above, sons of marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons, and commoners' sons enrolled as talented scholars.

sentences.zh: 有學生三百人，典學四人，掌固六人；

translations.literal: There were three hundred students, four school registrars, and six compound guards;
translations.idiomatic: There were three hundred students, four school registrars, and six compound guards;

sentences.zh: 東都學生五十人。

translations.literal: fifty students in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty students in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 律學律學博士三人，從八品下；

translations.literal: The School of Law had three erudites of the School of Law, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The School of Law had three erudites, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 助教一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: one instructor, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: One instructor, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌教八品以下及庶人子爲生者。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons enrolled as students.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons.

sentences.zh: 律令爲顓業，兼習格式法例。

translations.literal: Statutes and ordinances were the specialized curriculum, with formats and legal precedents studied concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and ordinances were the core curriculum, with formats and legal precedents studied as well.

sentences.zh: 隋，律學隸大理寺，博士八人。

translations.literal: Under Sui the School of Law was subordinate to the Court of Judicial Review, with eight erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui the School of Law belonged to the Court of Judicial Review and had eight erudites.

sentences.zh: 武德初，隸國子監，尋廢；

translations.literal: Early in Wude it was subordinate to the Directorate of Imperial University and soon abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude it was placed under the Directorate of Imperial University and soon abolished;

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年復置，顯慶三年又廢，以博士以下隸大理寺；

translations.literal: in the sixth year of Zhenguan it was restored, in the third year of Xianqing abolished again, and erudites and below were placed under the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: it was restored in Zhenguan 6, abolished again in Xianqing 3, and the erudites and below assigned to the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年復置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in Longshuo 2.

sentences.zh: 有學生二十人，典學二人。

translations.literal: There were twenty students and two school registrars.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty students and two school registrars.

sentences.zh: 元和初，東都置學生五人。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhe five students were established in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe five students were enrolled in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 書學書學博士二人，從九品下；

translations.literal: The School of Calligraphy had two erudites of the School of Calligraphy, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The School of Calligraphy had two erudites, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 助教一人。

translations.literal: one instructor.
translations.idiomatic: One instructor.

sentences.zh: 掌教八品以下及庶人子爲生者。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons enrolled as students.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons.

sentences.zh: 石經、説文、字林爲顓業，兼習餘書。

translations.literal: The Stone Classics, Shuowen, and Zilin were the specialized curriculum, with other books studied concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Classics, Shuowen, and Zilin were the core curriculum, with other texts studied as well.

sentences.zh: 武德初，廢書學，貞觀二年復置，顯慶三年又廢，以博士以下隸祕書省，龍朔二年復。

translations.literal: Early in Wude the School of Calligraphy was abolished; in the second year of Zhenguan it was restored; in the third year of Xianqing abolished again, and erudites and below were placed under the Secretariat; in the second year of Longshuo it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude the school was abolished, restored in Zhenguan 2, abolished again in Xianqing 3 with staff assigned to the Secretariat, and restored in Longshuo 2.

sentences.zh: 有學生十人，典學二人，東都學生三人。

translations.literal: There were ten students, two school registrars, and three students in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten students, two school registrars, and three students in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 算學算學博士二人，從九品下；

translations.literal: The School of Mathematics had two erudites of the School of Mathematics, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The School of Mathematics had two erudites, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 助教一人。

translations.literal: one instructor.
translations.idiomatic: One instructor.

sentences.zh: 掌教八品以下及庶人子爲生者。

translations.literal: They held charge of instructing students who were officials of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons enrolled as students.
translations.idiomatic: They taught students of eighth rank and below and commoners' sons.

sentences.zh: 二分其經以爲業：九章、海島、孫子、五曹、張丘建、夏侯陽、周髀、五經算、綴術、緝古爲顓業，兼習記遺、三等數。

translations.literal: The texts were divided into two for their curriculum: the specialized curriculum comprised the Nine Chapters, Sea Island, Master Sun, Five Departments, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhou Bi, Five-Classics Mathematics, Continuation Methods, and Collated Antiquity; the Records of Remaining Methods and Three-Grade Numbers were studied concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum was divided in two: the core texts were the Nine Chapters, Sea Island, Master Sun, Five Departments, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhou Bi, Five-Classics Mathematics, Continuation Methods, and Collated Antiquity, with the Records of Remaining Methods and Three-Grade Numbers studied as well.

sentences.zh: 凡六學束脩之禮、督課、試舉，皆如國子學；

translations.literal: For all six schools, the ceremony of presentation gifts, supervision of lessons, and examinations were all as in the Imperial University School;
translations.idiomatic: In all six schools, presentation gifts, supervision, and examinations followed the Imperial University School;

sentences.zh: 助教以下所掌亦如之。

translations.literal: what instructors and below held charge of was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: and the duties of instructors and below were the same.

sentences.zh: 唐廢算學，顯慶元年復置，三年又廢，以博士以下隸太史局。

translations.literal: Tang abolished the School of Mathematics; in the first year of Xianqing it was restored, in the third year abolished again, and erudites and below were placed under the Bureau of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Tang abolished the School of Mathematics, restored it in Xianqing 1, abolished it again in year 3, and assigned the erudites and below to the Bureau of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in Longshuo 2.

sentences.zh: 有學生十人，典學二人，東都學生二人。

translations.literal: There were ten students, two school registrars, and two students in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten students, two school registrars, and two students in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 少府監一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Directorate of the Palace Workshops had one director, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of the Palace Workshops had one director, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少監二人，從四品下。

translations.literal: two vice directors, subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice directors, of subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌百工技巧之政。

translations.literal: They held charge of the administration of the hundred crafts and technical skills.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw policy for the hundred crafts and skilled trades.

sentences.zh: 總中尙、左尙、右尙、織染、掌冶五署及諸冶、鑄錢、互市等監。

translations.literal: They had overall charge of the five offices—Central Shang, Left Shang, Right Shang, Dyeing and Weaving, and Metals Foundry—and of the various foundries, coin mints, border-trade markets, and other directorates.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised the five offices of Central Shang, Left Shang, Right Shang, Dyeing and Weaving, and Metals Foundry, together with the regional foundries, mints, and border-market directorates.

sentences.zh: 供天子器御、后妃服飾及郊廟圭玉、百官儀物。

translations.literal: They supplied the Son of Heaven's vessels and regalia, the empress's and consorts' dress and ornaments, and the jade tablets for suburban and temple rites and the ceremonial objects of all officials.
translations.idiomatic: They furnished the emperor's vessels and regalia, the dress and ornaments of empresses and consorts, jade tablets for suburban and temple sacrifices, and the ceremonial regalia of the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 凡武庫袍襦，皆識其輕重乃藏之，冬至、元日以給衞士。
