translations.literal: For all robes and jackets in the armory, they marked their weight before storing them; on the winter solstice and New Year's Day they were issued to the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Armory robes and jackets were weighed and labeled before storage, then issued to the guards on the winter solstice and New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 諸州市牛皮角以供用，牧畜角筋腦革悉輸焉。

translations.literal: The markets of the various prefectures supplied ox hides and horns for use; horn, sinew, brain, and hide from livestock were all delivered there.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural markets supplied ox hides and horns as needed, and all horn, sinew, brain, and hide from livestock were delivered to the directorate.

sentences.zh: 鈿鏤之工，教以四年；

translations.literal: For inlay and engraving work, instruction lasted four years;
translations.idiomatic: Inlay and engraving apprentices trained for four years;

sentences.zh: 車路樂器之工，三年；

translations.literal: for carriage fittings and musical instruments, three years;
translations.idiomatic: carriage fittings and musical instruments, three years;

sentences.zh: 平漫刀矟之工，二年，矢鏃竹漆屈柳之工半焉；

translations.literal: for plain and damascened blades and spears, two years; for arrowheads, bamboo, lacquer, and bent-willow work, half that;
translations.idiomatic: plain and damascened blades and spears, two years; arrowheads, bamboo, lacquer, and bent-willow work, half as long;

sentences.zh: 冠冕弁幘之工，九月。

translations.literal: for caps, crowns, court caps, and headcloths, nine months.
translations.idiomatic: caps, crowns, court caps, and headcloths, nine months.

sentences.zh: 教作者傳家技，四季以令丞試之，歳終以監試之，皆物勒工名。

translations.literal: Those taught to work passed down family skills; each season the office directors tested them, and at year's end the directorate tested them—all products bore the craftsman's inscribed name.
translations.idiomatic: Apprentices inherited family techniques; office directors examined them each season and the directorate examined them at year's end. Every finished piece bore the craftsman's name.

sentences.zh: 丞六人，從六品下。

translations.literal: six assistants, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were six assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌判監事。

translations.literal: They held charge of adjudicating directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated directorate business.

sentences.zh: 給五署所須金石、齒革、羽毛、竹木，所入之物，各以名數州土爲籍。

translations.literal: They supplied the five offices with needed metal, stone, ivory, hide, feathers, bamboo, and timber; for all goods received they kept registers listing names, quantities, and the prefectures and lands of origin.
translations.idiomatic: They provisioned the five offices with metal, stone, ivory, hide, feathers, bamboo, and timber, keeping registers of each item's name, quantity, and source prefecture.

sentences.zh: 工役衆寡難易有等差，而均其勞逸。

translations.literal: Labor assignments were graded by the size of the workforce and the difficulty of the work, and toil and rest were equalized.
translations.idiomatic: Work gangs were graded by size and difficulty, and labor and rest were balanced among them.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: two chief clerks, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: two chief clerks, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 録事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: two record clerks, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two record clerks, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德初，廢監，以諸署隸太府寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era the directorate was abolished and its offices were placed under the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era the directorate was abolished and its offices subordinated to the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年復置。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhenguan era it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in Zhenguan 1.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改曰内府監，武后垂拱元年曰尙方監。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Longshuo era it was renamed the Directorate of the Inner Palace; in the first year of Empress Wu's Chuigong era it was called the Directorate of the Palace Ateliers.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 it became the Directorate of the Inner Palace; in Wu Zetian's Chuigong 1, the Directorate of the Palace Ateliers.

sentences.zh: 有府二十七人，史十七人，計史三人，亭長八人，掌固六人，短蕃匠五千二十九人，綾錦坊巧兒三百六十五人，内作使綾匠八十三人，掖庭綾匠百五十人，内作巧兒四十二人，配京都諸司諸使雜匠百二十五人。

translations.literal: Staff included twenty-seven stewards, seventeen clerks, three accounting clerks, eight booth chiefs, six custodians, five thousand twenty-nine short-term foreign artisans, three hundred sixty-five skilled workers of the Brocade and Damask Workshop, eighty-three damask artisans of the Inner Works Office, one hundred fifty damask artisans of the Palace Rear Apartments, forty-two skilled workers of the Inner Works, and one hundred twenty-five miscellaneous artisans assigned from the various offices and agencies of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff comprised twenty-seven stewards, seventeen clerks, three accounting clerks, eight booth chiefs, six custodians, 5,029 short-term foreign artisans, 365 skilled workers in the Brocade and Damask Workshop, 83 damask artisans for the Inner Works Office, 150 for the Palace Rear Apartments, 42 Inner Works specialists, and 125 miscellaneous artisans detailed from capital agencies.

sentences.zh: 中尙署中尙署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Central Shang Office—one director of the Central Shang Office, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Central Shang Office had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從八品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供郊祀圭璧及天子器玩、后妃服飾彫文錯綵之制。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying jade tablets and disks for suburban sacrifices, the Son of Heaven's vessels and curios, and the regulations for the carved patterns and mixed colors of empresses' and consorts' dress and ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied jade tablets for suburban sacrifices, the emperor's vessels and curios, and the patterned dress and ornaments of empresses and consorts.

sentences.zh: 凡金木齒革羽毛，任土以時而供。

translations.literal: For all metal, wood, ivory, hide, and feathers, they supplied according to the products of each region and the season.
translations.idiomatic: Metal, wood, ivory, hide, and feathers were supplied according to regional products and the seasons.

sentences.zh: 赦日，樹金鷄於仗南，竿長七丈，有鷄髙四尺，黃金飾首，銜絳幡長七尺，承以綵盤，維以絳繩，將作監供焉。

translations.literal: On amnesty days a golden rooster was erected south of the halberd guard; the pole was seven zhang long, with a rooster four chi high, its head adorned in gold, holding in its beak a crimson banner seven chi long, borne on a colored tray and secured with crimson cord—the Directorate of Imperial Construction supplied it.
translations.idiomatic: On amnesty days a golden rooster was raised south of the halberd guard on a pole seven zhang tall. The bird stood four chi high, gilded at the head, with a seven-chi crimson banner in its beak on a colored tray, secured by crimson cord. The Directorate of Imperial Construction furnished it.

sentences.zh: 撃掆鼓千聲，集百官、父老、囚徒。

translations.literal: A carrying-pole drum was struck a thousand times to assemble all officials, elders, and prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: A carrying-pole drum was beaten a thousand strokes to gather officials, elders, and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 坊小兒得鷄首者官以錢購，或取絳幡而已。

translations.literal: Lane children who obtained the rooster's head were paid for it by the authorities, or they might take only the crimson banner.
translations.idiomatic: Children of the wards who seized the rooster's head were paid by the authorities, though some took only the crimson banner.

sentences.zh: 歳二月，獻牙尺。

translations.literal: Each year in the second month they presented ivory measuring rods.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the second month they presented ivory measuring rods.

sentences.zh: 寒食，獻毬。

translations.literal: At Cold Food they presented balls.
translations.idiomatic: At Cold Food they presented balls.

sentences.zh: 五月，獻綬帶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they presented ribbons and sashes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they presented ribbons and sashes.

sentences.zh: 夏至，獻雷車。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice they presented thunder carts.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice they presented thunder carts.

sentences.zh: 七月，獻鈿針。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they presented inlaid needles.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they presented inlaid needles.

sentences.zh: 臘日，獻口脂。

translations.literal: On the La festival day they presented lip balm.
translations.idiomatic: On the La festival they presented lip balm.

sentences.zh: 唯筆、琴瑟絃，月獻。

translations.literal: Only brushes and zither and se strings were presented monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Only brushes and zither and se strings were presented every month.

sentences.zh: 金銀暨紙，非旨不獻。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, and paper were not presented unless by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and paper were presented only on imperial order.

sentences.zh: 製魚袋以給百官；

translations.literal: They made fish pouches to issue to all officials;
translations.idiomatic: They made fish pouches for all officials;

sentences.zh: 蕃客賜寶鈿帶魚袋，則授鴻臚寺丞、主簿。

translations.literal: when foreign guests were granted jeweled-inlay belts and fish pouches, these were conferred by the assistant directors and chief clerks of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: when foreign guests received jeweled belts and fish pouches, the Court of Imperial Entertainments' assistants and chief clerks conferred them.

sentences.zh: 監作四人，從九品下。

translations.literal: four production supervisors, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: four production supervisors, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 凡監作，皆同品。

translations.literal: All production supervisors shared the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: All production supervisors held the same rank.

sentences.zh: 有府九人，史十八人，典事四人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Staff included nine stewards, eighteen clerks, four clerks of records, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included nine stewards, eighteen clerks, four records clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 唐改内尙方署曰中尙方署。

translations.literal: Under Tang the Inner Shang Atelier Office was renamed the Central Shang Atelier Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the Inner Shang Atelier was renamed the Central Shang Atelier.

sentences.zh: 武后改少府監曰尙方監，而中左右尙方、織染方、掌冶方五署，皆去方以避監。

translations.literal: Empress Wu changed the Directorate of the Palace Workshops to the Directorate of the Palace Ateliers, and for the five offices—Central, Left, and Right Shang Ateliers, Dyeing and Weaving Atelier, and Metals Foundry Atelier—the word fang was dropped to avoid clashing with jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian renamed the Palace Workshops directorate the Palace Ateliers directorate; the five offices of Central, Left, and Right Shang, Dyeing and Weaving, and Metals Foundry all dropped fang from their titles to avoid clashing with jian.

sentences.zh: 自是不改矣。

translations.literal: From then on these names were not changed.
translations.idiomatic: These names were not changed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 有金銀作坊院。

translations.literal: There was a Gold and Silver Workshop Court.
translations.idiomatic: It also maintained a Gold and Silver Workshop Court.

sentences.zh: 左尙署左尙署令一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Left Shang Office—one director of the Left Shang Office, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Shang Office had one director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞五人，從八品下。

translations.literal: five assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and five assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供翟扇、蓋繖、五路、五副、七輦、十二車，及皇太后、皇太子、公主、王妃、内外命婦、王公之車路。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying pheasant-feather fans, parasols and umbrellas, the Five Routes, Five Supports, Seven Palanquins, and Twelve Carriages, and the carriage fittings of the empress dowager, crown prince, princesses, princesses consort, inner and outer titled ladies, and princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied pheasant-feather fans, parasols, the Five Routes, Five Supports, Seven Palanquins, and Twelve Carriages, and the carriages of the empress dowager, crown prince, princesses, consorts, titled ladies, and princes.

sentences.zh: 凡畫素刻鏤與宮中蠟炬雜作，皆領之。

translations.literal: They also had charge of all painting on silk, carving, inlay work, and miscellaneous palace tasks such as wax torches.
translations.idiomatic: They also oversaw silk painting, carving, inlay work, and miscellaneous palace crafts including wax torches.

sentences.zh: 監作六人。

translations.literal: six production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: six production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府七人，史二十人，典事十八人，掌固十四人。

translations.literal: Staff included seven stewards, twenty clerks, eighteen clerks of records, and fourteen custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seven stewards, twenty clerks, eighteen records clerks, and fourteen custodians.

sentences.zh: 右尙署右尙署令二人，從七品下；

translations.literal: The Right Shang Office—two directors of the Right Shang Office, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Shang Office had two directors, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: four assistants, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and four assistants, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供十二閑馬之轡。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying bridles for the horses of the twelve pasture studs.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied bridles for the horses of the twelve imperial pasture studs.

sentences.zh: 毎歳取於京兆、河南府，加飾乃進。

translations.literal: Each year they were taken from the Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, adorned, and then presented.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they were obtained from Jingzhao and Henan, embellished, and then presented.

sentences.zh: 凡五品三部之帳，刀劍、斧鉞、甲冑、紙筆、茵席、履舄，皆儗其用，皮毛之工亦領焉。

translations.literal: For all the stores of the three departments of fifth rank and above—swords, blades, axes and halberds, armor, paper and brushes, mats and cushions, shoes and slippers—they matched supplies to use, and fur and hide work was also under their charge.
translations.idiomatic: They provisioned the stores of the three central departments with swords, axes, halberds, armor, paper, brushes, mats, and footwear according to need, and also oversaw fur and hide work.

sentences.zh: 監作六人。

translations.literal: six production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: six production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府七人，史二十人，典事十三人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: Staff included seven stewards, twenty clerks, thirteen clerks of records, and ten custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seven stewards, twenty clerks, thirteen records clerks, and ten custodians.

sentences.zh: 織染署織染署令一人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Dyeing and Weaving Office—one director of the Dyeing and Weaving Office, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Dyeing and Weaving Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供冠冕、組綬及織絍、色染。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying caps and crowns, ribbons and sashes, weaving and spinning, and dyeing in colors.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied caps and crowns, ribbons and sashes, weaving and spinning, and dyeing.

sentences.zh: 錦、羅、紗、縠、綾、紬、絁、絹、布，皆廣尺有八寸，四丈爲匹。

translations.literal: Brocade, gauze, plain gauze, fine gauze, damask, pongee, coarse silk, silk, and cloth were all one zhang and eight chi in width; four zhang made a bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade, gauze, plain gauze, fine gauze, damask, pongee, coarse silk, silk, and cloth were all one zhang and eight chi wide; four zhang made a bolt.

sentences.zh: 布五丈爲端，綿六兩爲屯，絲五兩爲絇，麻三斤爲綟。

translations.literal: Five zhang of cloth made a duan; six liang of cotton made a tun; five liang of silk made a qu; three jin of hemp made a ting.
translations.idiomatic: Five zhang of cloth made a duan; six liang of cotton a tun; five liang of silk a qu; three jin of hemp a ting.

sentences.zh: 凡綾錦文織，禁示於外。

translations.literal: All damask, brocade, and patterned weaves were forbidden to be displayed outside.
translations.idiomatic: Damask, brocade, and patterned weaves were barred from display outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 髙品一人專莅之，歳奏用度及所織。

translations.literal: One official of high rank was assigned exclusively to oversee it; each year he reported consumption and what had been woven.
translations.idiomatic: A senior official oversaw it exclusively and reported each year on usage and production.

sentences.zh: 毎掖庭經錦，則給酒羊。

translations.literal: Whenever the Palace Rear Apartments finished a length of brocade, wine and sheep were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Palace Rear Apartments completed a length of brocade, wine and sheep were distributed.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，祭杼。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month they sacrificed to the shuttle.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month they sacrificed to the weaving shuttle.

sentences.zh: 監作六人。

translations.literal: six production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: six production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十四人，典事十一人，掌固五人。

translations.literal: Staff included six stewards, fourteen clerks, eleven clerks of records, and five custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included six stewards, fourteen clerks, eleven records clerks, and five custodians.

sentences.zh: 掌冶署掌冶署令一人，正八品上；

translations.literal: The Metals Foundry Office—one director of the Metals Foundry Office, regular eighth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Metals Foundry Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品上。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌范鎔金銀銅鐵及塗飾琉璃玉作。

translations.literal: They held charge of casting and smelting gold, silver, copper, and iron and of coating, glazing, and jade work.
translations.idiomatic: They cast and smelted gold, silver, copper, and iron and oversaw glazing and jade work.

sentences.zh: 銅鐵人得採，而官收以稅，唯鑞官市。

translations.literal: The people might mine copper and iron, but the government collected it as tax; only tin alloy was sold by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Private persons might mine copper and iron, but the state collected it as tax; only tin alloy was sold through official markets.

sentences.zh: 邊州不置鐵冶，器用所須，皆官供。

translations.literal: Border prefectures did not establish iron foundries; whatever utensils were needed were all supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures had no iron foundries; all needed utensils were supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 凡諸冶成器，上數于少府監，然後給之。

translations.literal: For all finished goods from the various foundries, inventories were submitted to the Directorate of the Palace Workshops, and only then were they issued.
translations.idiomatic: Finished goods from all foundries were inventoried to the Palace Workshops directorate before issue.

sentences.zh: 監作二人。

translations.literal: two production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: two production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十二人，典事二十三人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Staff included six stewards, twelve clerks, twenty-three clerks of records, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included six stewards, twelve clerks, twenty-three records clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 諸冶監諸冶監令各一人，正七品下；

translations.literal: The various foundry directorates—each foundry directorate had one director, regular seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each regional foundry directorate had one director, of regular seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，從八品上。

translations.literal: each with one assistant, subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant each, of subordinate eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌鑄兵農之器，給軍士、屯田居民，唯興農冶顓供隴右監牧。

translations.literal: They held charge of casting military and agricultural implements, issuing them to soldiers and garrison colonists; only the Xingnong foundry exclusively supplied the Longyou stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: They cast military and farm tools for soldiers and garrison colonists; only the Xingnong foundry supplied the Longyou stud farms exclusively.

sentences.zh: 監作四人。

translations.literal: four production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: four production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史二人，典事二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Staff included one record clerk, one steward, two clerks, two clerks of records, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, one steward, two clerks, two records clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 太原冶，減監作二人。

translations.literal: At the Taiyuan foundry, two production supervisors were omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan foundry had two fewer production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 諸鑄錢監諸鑄錢監監各一人，副監各二人，丞各一人。

translations.literal: The various coin-mint directorates—each mint had one director, two vice directors, and one assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: Each coin mint had one director, two vice directors, and one assistant.

sentences.zh: 以所在都督、刺史判焉；

translations.literal: The area military commander or prefect served concurrently in these posts;
translations.idiomatic: The local area commander or prefect served concurrently;

sentences.zh: 副監，上佐；

translations.literal: the vice directors were senior aides;
translations.idiomatic: vice directors were senior aides;

sentences.zh: 丞，以判司；

translations.literal: the assistants were acting bureau chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: assistants were acting bureau chiefs;

sentences.zh: 監事以參軍及縣尉爲之。

translations.literal: supervisors were drawn from army staff officers and county deputies.
translations.idiomatic: and supervisors from army staff officers and county deputies.

sentences.zh: 監事各一人。

translations.literal: Each had one supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Each mint had one supervisor.

sentences.zh: 有録事各一人，府各三人，史各四人，典事各五人。

translations.literal: Each had one record clerk, three stewards, four clerks, and five clerks of records.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one record clerk, three stewards, four clerks, and five records clerks.

sentences.zh: 凡鑄錢有七監，會昌中，增至八監，毎道置鑄錢坊一。

translations.literal: In all there were seven coin mints; in the Huichang era the number rose to eight, and each circuit had one coin-casting workshop.
translations.idiomatic: There were seven mints in all; under Huichang the number rose to eight, with one casting workshop per circuit.

sentences.zh: 大中初，三監廢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era three mints were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong era three mints were abolished.

sentences.zh: 互市監互市監毎監，監一人，從六品下；

translations.literal: The Border-Trade Market Directorate—at each market one director, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each border-trade market had one director, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正八品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌蕃國交易之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of trade with foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: They regulated trade with foreign states.

sentences.zh: 隋以監隸四方舘。

translations.literal: Under Sui the directorate was subordinate to the Four Directions Hostels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui it was subordinate to the Four Directions Hostels.

sentences.zh: 唐隸少府。

translations.literal: Under Tang it was subordinate to the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang it was subordinated to the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，改交市監曰互市監，副監曰丞，武后垂拱元年曰通市監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhenguan era the Exchange Market Directorate was renamed the Border-Trade Market Directorate, vice directors were called assistants, and in the first year of Empress Wu's Chuigong era it was called the General Market Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 the Exchange Market Directorate became the Border-Trade Market Directorate, vice directors became assistants, and in Wu Zetian's Chuigong 1 it became the General Market Directorate.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府二人，史四人，價人四人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: Staff included one record clerk, two stewards, four clerks, four appraisers, and eight custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, two stewards, four clerks, four appraisers, and eight custodians.

sentences.zh: 將作監監一人，從三品；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Imperial Construction—one director, subordinate third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Imperial Construction had one director, of subordinate third rank;

sentences.zh: 少監二人，從四品下。

translations.literal: two vice directors, subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice directors, of subordinate fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌土木工匠之政，總左校、右校、中校、甄官等署，百工等監。

translations.literal: They held charge of the administration of civil works, earthworks, and craftsmen, and had overall charge of the Left Works, Right Works, Central Works, and Casting offices, and of the various hundred-crafts directorates.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw civil construction and craftsmen, supervising the Left, Right, and Central Works offices, the Casting Office, and the regional hundred-crafts directorates.

sentences.zh: 大明、興慶、上陽宮，中書、門下、六軍仗舍、閑廄，謂之内作；

translations.literal: The Daming, Xingqing, and Shangyang palaces; the Chancellery, Secretariat, armories of the Six Armies, and spare stables were called inner works;
translations.idiomatic: Work at the Daming, Xingqing, and Shangyang palaces, the Chancellery, Secretariat, Six Armies armories, and spare stables counted as inner works;

sentences.zh: 郊廟、城門、省、寺、臺、監、十六衞、東宮、王府諸廨，謂之外作。

translations.literal: suburban altars and temples, city gates, ministries, monasteries, directorates, commissions, the Sixteen Guards, the Eastern Palace, and the various offices of princely establishments were called outer works.
translations.idiomatic: while suburban altars and temples, city gates, ministries, monasteries, directorates, commissions, the Sixteen Guards, the Eastern Palace, and princely household offices counted as outer works.

sentences.zh: 自十月距二月，休冶功；

translations.literal: from the tenth month through the second month metalworking was suspended;
translations.idiomatic: from the tenth month through the second month metalworking ceased;

sentences.zh: 自冬至距九月，休土功。

translations.literal: from the winter solstice through the ninth month earthworks were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: from the winter solstice through the ninth month earthworks ceased.

sentences.zh: 凡治宮廟，太常擇日以聞。

translations.literal: Whenever palaces or temples were repaired, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose the day and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever palace or temple repairs were undertaken, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices chose an auspicious day and reported it.

sentences.zh: 丞四人，從六品下。

translations.literal: Four assistants, subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were four assistants, of subordinate sixth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌判監事。

translations.literal: They adjudicated directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated directorate business.

sentences.zh: 凡外營繕、大事則聽制敕，小事則須省符。

translations.literal: For all outer construction and repairs, major matters followed imperial edicts, minor matters required provincial orders.
translations.idiomatic: For outer construction and repairs, major projects required imperial edicts and minor ones provincial authorization.

sentences.zh: 功有長短，役有輕重。

translations.literal: Work periods had long, medium, and short terms; labor had light and heavy grades.
translations.idiomatic: Work periods were classified as long, medium, or short, and labor as light or heavy.

sentences.zh: 自四月距七月，爲長功；

translations.literal: from the fourth month through the seventh month was long work;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth through seventh months were long-work season;

sentences.zh: 二月、三月、八月、九月，爲中功；

translations.literal: the second, third, eighth, and ninth months were medium work;
translations.idiomatic: the second, third, eighth, and ninth months were medium-work season;

sentences.zh: 自十月距正月，爲短功。

translations.literal: from the tenth month through the first month was short work.
translations.idiomatic: and the tenth month through the first month was short-work season.

sentences.zh: 長上匠，州率資錢以酬雇。

translations.literal: Master craftsmen on long-term roster were paid hire wages raised by the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Master craftsmen on long-term roster were paid from funds raised by their home prefectures.

sentences.zh: 軍器則勒歳月與工姓名。

translations.literal: For military equipment the year and month and the craftsman's name were inscribed.
translations.idiomatic: Military equipment was stamped with the date and the craftsman's name.

sentences.zh: 武德初，改令曰大匠，少令曰少匠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era the director was renamed chief artisan, the vice director junior artisan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era the director was retitled Chief Artisan and the vice director Junior Artisan.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改將作監曰繕工監，大匠曰大監，少匠曰少監。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Longshuo era the Directorate of Imperial Construction was renamed the Construction Works Directorate, the chief artisan was called senior director, and the junior artisan vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 the directorate became the Construction Works Directorate, the chief artisan became senior director, and the junior artisan vice director.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，繕工監曰營繕監。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianheng era the Construction Works Directorate was renamed the Building and Repair Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 it was renamed the Building and Repair Directorate.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，改大匠曰大監，少匠曰少監。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of the Tianbao era the chief artisan was again called senior director and the junior artisan vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 11 the titles chief artisan and junior artisan were changed back to senior director and vice director.

sentences.zh: 有府十四人，史二十八人，計史三人，亭長四人，掌固六人，短蕃匠一萬二千七百四十四人，明資匠二百六十人。

translations.literal: Staff included fourteen stewards, twenty-eight clerks, three accounting clerks, four depot chiefs, six custodians, twelve thousand seven hundred forty-four short-term foreign artisans, and two hundred sixty salaried craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included fourteen stewards, twenty-eight clerks, three accounting clerks, four depot chiefs, six custodians, 12,744 short-term foreign artisans, and 260 salaried craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 主簿二人，從七品下。

translations.literal: Two registrars, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two registrars, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌官吏糧料、俸食，假使必由之。

translations.literal: They held charge of officials' grain rations and salary provisions; all temporary assignments had to pass through them.
translations.idiomatic: They managed officials' grain rations and salaries, and all temporary assignments had to pass through their office.

sentences.zh: 諸司供署監物有闕，舉焉。

translations.literal: When any office's supply depot lacked supervised goods, it was reported to them.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls in supplies held by any office's depot were reported to them.

sentences.zh: 録事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two record clerks, subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two record clerks, of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 左校署左校署令二人，從八品下；

translations.literal: The Left Works Office had two directors, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Works Office had two directors, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌梓匠之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of carpentry.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw carpentry.

sentences.zh: 樂縣、簨簴、兵械、喪葬儀物皆供焉。

translations.literal: They supplied musical frames, banner poles, weapons, and funeral ceremonial objects.
translations.idiomatic: They furnished musical frames, banner poles, weapons, and funeral regalia.

sentences.zh: 宮室之制，自天子至士庶有等差，官脩者左校爲之。

translations.literal: Standards for palaces and dwellings had graded distinctions from the Son of Heaven down to commoners; official repairs were done by the Left Works.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and dwelling standards were graded from emperor to commoner; official repairs were the Left Works' responsibility.

sentences.zh: 監作十人。

translations.literal: Ten production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府六人，史十二人，監作十二人。

translations.literal: Staff included six stewards, twelve clerks, and twelve production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included six stewards, twelve clerks, and twelve production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 右校署右校署令二人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Right Works Office had two directors, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Works Office had two directors, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞三人，正九品下。

translations.literal: three assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and three assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌版築、塗泥、丹堊、匽廁之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of rammed earth, plastering, cinnabar and white wash, and latrines.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw rammed-earth construction, plastering, cinnabar and whitewash, and latrines.

sentences.zh: 有所須，則審其多少而市之。

translations.literal: When anything was needed, they assessed the quantity and purchased it.
translations.idiomatic: When materials were needed, they determined quantities and procured them on the market.

sentences.zh: 監作十人。

translations.literal: Ten production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were ten production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十人，典事二十四人。

translations.literal: Staff included five stewards, ten clerks, and twenty-four records clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included five stewards, ten clerks, and twenty-four records clerks.

sentences.zh: 右校署中校署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: The Central Works Office had one director, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Central Works Office had one director, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞三人，正九品下。

translations.literal: three assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and three assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供舟車、兵械、雜器。

translations.literal: They held charge of supplying boats, carriages, weapons, and miscellaneous implements.
translations.idiomatic: They supplied boats, carriages, weapons, and miscellaneous equipment.

sentences.zh: 行幸陳設則供竿柱，閑廄繫秣則供行槽，禱祀則供棘葛，内外營作所須皆取焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled they supplied poles and posts for display; when spare stables tethered fodder they supplied traveling troughs; for prayer sacrifices they supplied thorn and vine; whatever inner or outer construction required was taken from them.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours they furnished display poles; for spare stables they furnished traveling troughs; for prayer sacrifices, thorn and vine; and all materials for inner and outer construction came from their office.

sentences.zh: 監牧車牛，有年支芻豆，則受之以給車坊。

translations.literal: They supervised pasturing of draft oxen; when there was annual fodder and beans, they received it to supply the carriage workshops.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised draft cattle; annual allocations of fodder and beans were delivered to them for the carriage workshops.

sentences.zh: 監事四人。

translations.literal: Four supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were four supervisors.

sentences.zh: 武后時，改曰營繕署。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu it was renamed the Building and Repair Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu it was renamed the Building and Repair Office.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年復舊，尋廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Chuigong era the former name was restored, and soon after it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 1 the former name was restored, then the office was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 開元初復置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era it was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era it was reestablished.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，典事八人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: Staff included three stewards, six clerks, eight records clerks, and two custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included three stewards, six clerks, eight records clerks, and two custodians.

sentences.zh: 甄官署甄官署令一人，從八品下；

translations.literal: The Casting Office had one director, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Casting Office had one director, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌琢石、陶土之事，供石磬、人、獸、碑、柱、碾、磑、甁、缶之器，敕葬則供明器。

translations.literal: They held charge of stone carving and pottery, supplying stone chimes, human and animal figures, steles, pillars, millstones, querns, jars, and pots; when an imperial burial was ordered they supplied spirit objects.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw stone carving and pottery, furnishing stone chimes, figurines, steles, pillars, millstones, querns, jars, and pots, and spirit objects for imperial burials by edict.

sentences.zh: 監作四人。

translations.literal: Four production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were four production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府五人，史十人，典事十八人。

translations.literal: Staff included five stewards, ten clerks, and eighteen records clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included five stewards, ten clerks, and eighteen records clerks.

sentences.zh: 百工、就谷、庫谷、斜谷、太陰、伊陽諸監百工、就谷、庫谷、斜谷、太陰、伊陽監監各一人，正七品下；

translations.literal: The Hundred Crafts, Jiugu, Kugu, Xiegu, Taiyin, and Yiyang directorates—each had one director, regular seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Hundred Crafts, Jiugu, Kugu, Xiegu, Taiyin, and Yiyang directorates each had one director, of regular seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 副監一人，從七品下；

translations.literal: one vice director, subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: one vice director, of subordinate seventh rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正八品上。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular eighth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌采伐材木。

translations.literal: They held charge of felling timber.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised timber harvesting.

sentences.zh: 監作四人。

translations.literal: Four production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were four production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 武德初，置百工監，掌舟車及營造雜作，有監、少監各一人，丞四人，主簿一人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era the Hundred Crafts Directorate was established to hold charge of boats, carriages, and miscellaneous construction work; it had one director and one vice director, four assistants, and one registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era the Hundred Crafts Directorate was established for boats, carriages, and miscellaneous construction, with one director, one vice director, four assistants, and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 又置就谷、庫谷、斜谷、太陰、伊陽五監。

translations.literal: Five more directorates were also established: Jiugu, Kugu, Xiegu, Taiyin, and Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Five more directorates were also established at Jiugu, Kugu, Xiegu, Taiyin, and Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，廢百工監。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era the Hundred Crafts Directorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era the Hundred Crafts Directorate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 髙宗置百工署，掌東都土木瓦石之功。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong established the Hundred Crafts Office to hold charge of civil, earth, tile, and stone work in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong established the Hundred Crafts Office for civil, earth, tile, and stone work in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年爲監。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of the Kaiyuan era it became a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 it was elevated to a directorate.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府一人，史三人，典事二十人。

translations.literal: Staff included one record clerk, one steward, three clerks, and twenty records clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one record clerk, one steward, three clerks, and twenty records clerks.

sentences.zh: 軍器監監一人，正四品上；

translations.literal: The Directorate of Military Equipment had one director, regular fourth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Military Equipment had one director, of regular fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正七品上。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌繕甲弩，以時輸武庫。

translations.literal: They held charge of repairing armor and crossbows and delivering them to the armory on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained armor and crossbows and delivered them to the armory on schedule.

sentences.zh: 總署二：一曰弩坊，二曰甲坊。

translations.literal: They had overall charge of two offices: the first was called the Crossbow Workshop, the second the Armor Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised two offices: the Crossbow Workshop and the Armor Workshop.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: One registrar, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: There was one registrar, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 録事一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: one record clerk, subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one record clerk, of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 武德初，有武器監一人，正八品下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era there was an Arms Directorate with one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era an Arms Directorate was established with one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌兵仗、廏牧。

translations.literal: It held charge of weapons and stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw weapons and stud farms.

sentences.zh: 少監一人，丞二人，主簿一人。

translations.literal: It had one vice director, two assistants, and one registrar.
translations.idiomatic: It had one vice director, two assistants, and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 七年廢軍器監，八年復置，九年又廢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Directorate of Military Equipment was abolished; in the eighth it was restored; in the ninth it was abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the Directorate of Military Equipment was abolished, restored in year 8, and abolished again in year 9.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，廢武器監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhenguan era the Arms Directorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 the Arms Directorate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 開元以前，軍器皆出右尙署，三年置軍器監，十一年復廢爲甲弩坊，隸少府，十六年復爲監。

translations.literal: Before the Kaiyuan era all military equipment came from the Right Shang Office; in the third year the Directorate of Military Equipment was established; in the eleventh year it was again abolished and made the Armor and Crossbow Workshop, subordinate to the Palace Workshops; in the sixteenth year it was again made a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Before Kaiyuan all military equipment came from the Right Shang Office. In Kaiyuan 3 the directorate was established; in 11 it was abolished and became the Armor and Crossbow Workshop under the Palace Workshops; in 16 it was restored as a directorate.

sentences.zh: 有府八人，史十二人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Staff included eight stewards, twelve clerks, two depot chiefs, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included eight stewards, twelve clerks, two depot chiefs, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 弩坊署弩坊署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Crossbow Workshop Office had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Crossbow Workshop Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌出納矛矟、弓矢、排弩、刃鏃、雜作及工匠。

translations.literal: They held charge of issuing and receiving spears and halberds, bows and arrows, repeating crossbows, blades and arrowheads, miscellaneous work, and craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: They issued and received spears, halberds, bows, arrows, repeating crossbows, blades, arrowheads, miscellaneous work, and craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 監作二人。

translations.literal: Two production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were two production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史五人，典事二人。

translations.literal: Staff included two stewards, five clerks, and two records clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two stewards, five clerks, and two records clerks.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，改弓弩署爲弩坊署，甲鎧署爲甲坊署。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhenguan era the Bow and Crossbow Office was renamed the Crossbow Workshop Office, and the Armor Office was renamed the Armor Workshop Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 the Bow and Crossbow Office became the Crossbow Workshop Office and the Armor Office the Armor Workshop Office.

sentences.zh: 甲坊署甲坊署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Armor Workshop Office had one director, regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Armor Workshop Office had one director, of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品下。

translations.literal: one assistant, regular ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant, of regular ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌出納甲冑、綅繩、筋角、雜作及工匠。

translations.literal: They held charge of issuing and receiving armor and helmets, scarlet cords, sinew and horn, miscellaneous work, and craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: They issued and received armor and helmets, scarlet cords, sinew and horn, miscellaneous work, and craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 監作二人。

translations.literal: Two production supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: There were two production supervisors.

sentences.zh: 有府二人，史五人，典事二人。

translations.literal: Staff included two stewards, five clerks, and two records clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two stewards, five clerks, and two records clerks.

sentences.zh: 都水監使者二人，正五品上。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Waterways had two commissioners, regular fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Waterways had two commissioners, of regular fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌川澤、津梁、渠堰、陂池之政，總河渠、諸津監署。

translations.literal: They held charge of the administration of rivers and marshes, ferries and bridges, canals and dikes, and reservoirs and ponds, and had overall charge of the River Works and various ferry directorates and offices.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw rivers and marshes, ferries, bridges, canals, dikes, and reservoirs, and supervised the River Works and ferry directorates.

sentences.zh: 凡漁捕有禁，溉田自遠始，先稻後陸，渠長、斗門長節其多少而均焉。

translations.literal: Fishing and hunting were subject to prohibitions; irrigation of fields began from the farthest reaches, rice fields first and dry fields after; canal chiefs and sluice-gate chiefs regulated the amounts and equalized them.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing and hunting were regulated by seasonal prohibitions; irrigation began at the farthest fields, rice before dry land, with canal and sluice chiefs apportioning water fairly.

sentences.zh: 府縣以官督察。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties supervised with officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties enforced this through official oversight.

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Two assistants, subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were two assistants, of subordinate seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌判監事。

translations.literal: They adjudicated directorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated directorate business.

sentences.zh: 凡京畿諸水，因灌溉盜費者有禁。

translations.literal: For all waters in the capital region, wasting water through irrigation theft was prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital region, misusing irrigation water or diverting it unlawfully was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 水入内之餘，則均王公百官。

translations.literal: What remained of water entering the inner city was then apportioned among princes, dukes, and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus water after supply to the inner city was apportioned among princes, dukes, and officials.

sentences.zh: 主簿一人，從八品下。

translations.literal: One registrar, subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There was one registrar, of subordinate eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌運漕、漁捕程，會而糾舉之。

translations.literal: They held charge of transport-canal and fishing schedules, convened accounts, and investigated and reported violations.
translations.idiomatic: They managed canal transport and fishing schedules, convened accounts, and investigated violations.

sentences.zh: 武德初，廢都水監爲署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era the Directorate of Waterways was demoted to an office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era the Directorate of Waterways was demoted to an office.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年復爲監，改令曰使者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhenguan era it was again made a directorate, and the director was renamed commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 it was restored as a directorate and the director retitled commissioner.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改都水監曰司津監，使者曰監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Directorate of Waterways was renamed the Directorate of Fords; the commissioner was called Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo the Directorate of Waterways was renamed the Directorate of Fords, and its commissioner was titled Director.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱元年，改都水監曰水衡監，使者曰都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong under Empress Wu, the Directorate of Waterways was renamed the Directorate of Water Balance; the commissioner was called Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chuigong Empress Wu renamed it the Directorate of Water Balance, and the commissioner was titled Commandant.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年，不隸將作監。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, it was no longer subordinate to the Directorate of Imperial Construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan it was removed from the Directorate of Imperial Construction's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 有録事一人，府五人，史十人，亭長一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There was one recording clerk, five office clerks, ten scribes, one station chief, and four compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included one recording clerk, five office clerks, ten scribes, one station chief, and four compound guards.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀六年，置舟楫署，有令一人，正八品下，掌舟楫、運漕；

translations.literal: Initially, in the sixth year of Zhenguan, the Office of Boats was established, with one director of regular eighth rank, lower grade, in charge of boats and transport grain;
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the sixth year of Zhenguan, the Office of Boats was established with one director of regular eighth rank, lower grade, in charge of boats and grain transport;

sentences.zh: 漕正一人，府三人，史六人，監漕一人，漕史二人，典事六人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: one transport chief, three office clerks, six scribes, one transport supervisor, two transport scribes, six stewards, and eight compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: one transport chief, three office clerks, six scribes, one transport supervisor, two transport scribes, six stewards, and eight compound guards.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，置丞二人，正九品下，掌運漕隱失。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, two assistants of regular ninth rank, lower grade, were established to oversee concealed losses in transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan two assistants of regular ninth rank, lower grade, were added to investigate concealed losses in grain transport.

sentences.zh: 開元二十六年，署廢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan, the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 河渠署令河渠署令一人，正八品下；

translations.literal: The Office of Rivers and Canals had one director of regular eighth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Rivers and Canals had one director of regular eighth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 丞一人，正九品上。

translations.literal: one assistant of regular ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: and one assistant of regular ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌河渠、陂池、隄堰、魚醢之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of rivers and canals, reservoirs and ponds, dikes and weirs, and fish and pickled fish.
translations.idiomatic: They managed rivers and canals, reservoirs and ponds, dikes and weirs, and fish supplies and pickling.

sentences.zh: 凡溝渠開塞，漁捕時禁，皆顓之。

translations.literal: For all opening and closing of ditches and canals and seasonal prohibitions on fishing, they had exclusive authority.
translations.idiomatic: They had exclusive authority over opening and closing ditches and canals and seasonal fishing prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 饗宗廟，則供魚鮍；

translations.literal: When feasting at the ancestral temple, they supplied fish and minnows;
translations.idiomatic: For ancestral temple feasts they supplied fish and minnows;

sentences.zh: 祀昊天上帝，有司攝事，則供腥魚。

translations.literal: when sacrificing to August Heaven, if the relevant office acted in proxy, they supplied raw fish.
translations.idiomatic: when sacrificing to August Heaven, if a relevant office acted for the emperor, they supplied raw fish.

sentences.zh: 日供尙食及給中書、門下，歳供諸司及東宮之冬藏。

translations.literal: Daily they supplied the Imperial Kitchen and provided for the Secretariat and Chancellery; yearly they supplied the various offices and the Eastern Palace's winter stores.
translations.idiomatic: Daily they supplied the Imperial Kitchen and the Secretariat and Chancellery; yearly they supplied the various offices and the Eastern Palace's winter stores.

sentences.zh: 渭河三百里内漁釣者，五坊捕治之。

translations.literal: Those who fished within three hundred li of the Wei River were apprehended and punished by the Five Wards.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who fished within three hundred li of the Wei River was apprehended by the Five Wards.

sentences.zh: 供祠祀，則自便橋至東渭橋禁民漁。

translations.literal: When supplying sacrifices, fishing by the people was prohibited from Bian Bridge to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When supplying sacrifices, commoners were forbidden to fish from Bian Bridge to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 三元日，非供祠不採魚。

translations.literal: On the three yuan festival days, fish were not taken except for sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On the three yuan festival days, fish were not harvested except for sacrificial use.

sentences.zh: 唐有河隄使者。

translations.literal: Tang had River Dike envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang there were River Dike envoys.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初改曰河隄謁者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan they were renamed River Dike ushers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan they were renamed River Dike ushers.

sentences.zh: 有府三人，史六人，典事三人，毎渠及斗門有長一人，掌固三人，魚師十二人。

translations.literal: There were three office clerks, six scribes, three stewards; for each canal and sluice gate there was one chief, three compound guards, and twelve fish masters.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included three office clerks, six scribes, and three stewards; each canal and sluice gate had one chief, three compound guards, and twelve fish masters.

sentences.zh: 初，有監漕十人，從九品上，大暦後省。

translations.literal: Initially there were ten transport supervisors of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade; after Dali they were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Initially there were ten transport supervisors of subordinate ninth rank, upper grade; after Dali the post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 興成、五門、六門、龍首、涇堰、滋隄，凡六堰，皆有丞一人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Xingcheng, Five Gates, Six Gates, Dragon Head, Jing Weir, and Zi Dike—in all six weirs—each had one assistant of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: The six weirs—Xingcheng, Five Gates, Six Gates, Dragon Head, Jing Weir, and Zi Dike—each had one assistant of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 府一人，史二人，典事二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: One office clerk, two scribes, two stewards, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each had one office clerk, two scribes, two stewards, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年皆廢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 河隄謁者六人，正八品下。

translations.literal: Six River Dike ushers, regular eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were six River Dike ushers, of regular eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌完隄堰、利溝瀆、漁捕之事。

translations.literal: They held charge of completing dikes and weirs, benefiting ditches and canals, and fishing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained dikes and weirs, kept ditches and canals functioning, and oversaw fishing.

sentences.zh: 涇、渭、白渠，以京兆少尹一人督視。

translations.literal: The Jing, Wei, and White Canal were supervised by one Vice Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing, Wei, and White Canal were supervised by one Vice Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 諸津令諸津令各一人，正九品上；

translations.literal: For each ford there was one director of regular ninth rank, upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: Each ford had one director of regular ninth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 丞二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: two assistants of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: and two assistants of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌天下津濟舟梁。

translations.literal: They held charge of the empire's fords, ferry crossings, and bridges.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the empire's fords, ferry crossings, and bridges.

sentences.zh: 灞橋、永濟橋，以勳官散官一人莅之；

translations.literal: Ba Bridge and Yongji Bridge were overseen by one merit-title honorary official;
translations.idiomatic: Ba Bridge and Yongji Bridge were overseen by one merit-title honorary official;

sentences.zh: 天津橋、中橋，則以衞士拚掃。

translations.literal: Tianjin Bridge and Central Bridge were swept by guards.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin Bridge and Central Bridge were maintained by guards.

sentences.zh: 凡舟渠之備，皆先儗其半，袽塞、竹𥷨，所在供焉。

translations.literal: For all boat and canal preparations, half was kept in advance; caulking, plugs, and bamboo matting were supplied wherever needed.
translations.idiomatic: For all boat and canal preparations, half the supplies were kept in reserve; caulking, plugs, and bamboo matting were supplied as needed.

sentences.zh: 唐改津尉曰令，有録事一人，府一人，史二人，典事三人，津吏五人，橋丁各三十人，匠各八人。

translations.literal: Tang changed Ford Captains to Directors; there was one recording clerk, one office clerk, two scribes, three stewards, five ford clerks, thirty bridge laborers each, and eight craftsmen each.
translations.idiomatic: Tang renamed Ford Captains as Directors; staff included one recording clerk, one office clerk, two scribes, three stewards, five ford clerks, thirty bridge laborers per bridge, and eight craftsmen per bridge.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南諸津，隸都水監；

translations.literal: Fords of Jingzhao and Henan were subordinate to the Directorate of Waterways;
translations.idiomatic: Fords in Jingzhao and Henan were subordinate to the Directorate of Waterways;

sentences.zh: 便橋、渭橋、萬年三橋，有丞一人，從九品下；

translations.literal: Bian Bridge, Wei Bridge, and the three Wanian bridges each had one assistant of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;
translations.idiomatic: Bian Bridge, Wei Bridge, and the three Wanian bridges each had one assistant of subordinate ninth rank, lower grade;

sentences.zh: 府一人，史十人，典事二人，掌固二人。

translations.literal: one office clerk, ten scribes, two stewards, and two compound guards.
translations.idiomatic: with one office clerk, ten scribes, two stewards, and two compound guards.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中廢。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They were abolished during Zhenguan.
